title: Like many "mature adults"
text:
Like many "mature adults", it seems that I grow nose hair faster than any other hair. Ugh! I had a little miniature clipper years ago, and it sat in the damp bathroom and the battery rusted, so now it's "toast". Had always been fascinated by these little "finger powered" trimmers, but never seemed to come across one. Searched Amazon, and there it is! Looks exactly like I remembered from years ago, and inexpensive as well.

The quality and packaging are fantastic! Comes with a cleaning brush, a spring, and instructions. Packaging is very nice. Looks like it will last FOREVER. And, NO BATTERIES. Electric products that look a lot like this cost twice as much.

It requires a little bit of practice to use because everything is "backwards" looking into a mirror and holding the tool. Very sharp, and despite my clumsy hands, no nicks or scratches. Seems to be "idiot proof." I give it only four stars because despite hacking away for some time, I was never able to clip ALL of my nose hair. It doesn't show, but it's still pretty long in there and will reappear quicker than I'd like. Cannot imagine using it on "ear hair", because looking at my ears in the mirror seems too difficult. (Guess the lady who cuts my hair will continue to clean up that hair and trim my eyebrows. Ive never had the nerve to ask her to trim my nose!)

This quality for this price is still a GREAT DEAL.

title: Cute color/great fit!
text: I bought these locally (for about the same price) and loved them. I wore salon acrylics for many years and these are only my fourth set (third by Kiss) of DIY full coverage false nails. On my prior (and first) set of Kiss nails I initially used the adhesive tabs rather than the glue to keep from damaging my nails. They didn't stay on really great but I think there are some good reasons for that. First, its important to find which nails fit yours exactly. If they are too small the curve will interfere with the adhesive. If they are too big they will overlap your cuticles and expose the adhesive to liquids and such. I did not file my nails to encourage adhesion. I also did not use a primer nor did I push back my cuticles. Nevertheless, they stayed on reasonably well. The big bonus was that when it was time to take them off it just takes a short soak with acetone polish remover and they pop right off. The adhesive becomes rather like rubber cement. It comes cleanly off your natural nails as well as the acrylic ones (and you can use them again). The next time I tried nails from Kiss they were a different color but the package contents and instructions were identical. This time I wanted to see how the glue worked. Still no filing, primer, or cuticle pushing. Despite those facts the nails stuck tight. They weren't going anywhere and I'm tough on nails. I even used them to pry things. So, if you can't tell, I'm still sort of learning and experimenting to find things that work for me. I have some muscle control problems and the Kiss glue applicator (which is every bit as good as every other non-brush applicator) presents a bit of a problem for me. I decided to use a non-Kiss brush-on glue for this particular set. I lightly buffed, pushed back cuticles, cleaned with acetone, and primed. Despite being treated delicately for a special occasion and having very limited exposure to water they started popping off in less than 24 hours. Obviously the Kiss glue is superior. If anyone knows where I can get Kiss glue with a brush please let me know. Anyhow, aside from the adhesive the color is really pretty. Enough color to be noticed but it doesn't jump out at you. One thing I have learned during my false nail journey is that these things have a right way and a wrong way to be applied. I always get square nails so its easy to tell now that I know to look. The part that fits against your cuticle is the rounded end. Also, if you want them to look real you have to push them into your cuticles a bit. I found it a bit uncomfortable during the initial application but it faded quickly. Well worth the final look for me. There is one other cool feature of these nails I'd like to mention. All of them are numbered. This speeds up the nail selection process quite a bit. You just find a fit for one hand and then find the other nail with the same number. I'm going to be sure to write them down next time so I can just pick out the ones I need based on number without testing lots of them. I continue to be really pleased with the Kiss nails and I plan to buy many of them in the future. Not only can I change my manicure frequently but I can also protect my natural nails.

text:
A little disappointed in this package. I'll start with the good, the gloves work nicely and fit comfortably. The gloves are soft and easy to adjust on the hand and they're lightweight too so they don't get hot and make your hands sweaty.

The standing lamp is a micro USB cable and receiver for power. There is flex when I gently push the top of the lamp and the base. It feels really fragile. The light is a nice soft blue and doesn't get hot when it's on, the power button is fairly easy to press.

The individual handheld lamp isn't chargeable. It runs off three AAA batteries. The hand lamp is a deep blue light but it seems feint. The pink grips also slide on and off the casing fairly easily. It feels really lightweight and cheaper rather than a quality lightweight material.

I think this would be a great kit for travel, you wouldn't be devastated if you lost or damaged and had to replace these tools or maybe for a younger child who is starting to express interest in gel manicures. You wouldn't mind if there's some wear on these and you would replace them with nice quality items when they get used to handling them. This is the nail kit equivalent of giving your cousin your MadCatz controller instead of the official Nintendo one. It's good to have but I think it's worth it to throw a little more into the savings bank and buying a higher quality set or individual set of lamps.

text:
Where do I begin with this one... The ponytail arrived in good condition but with a strong smell to it. I needed to dye it dark brown before wearing so I stored it in the bag it came in for a month or two. When I took it out I noticed it was quite (really) tangled, but I was able to wash it and detangle it just fine, and it was shiny and bouncy after the first wash. After this is when things went downhill. I lifted the color so it could take the brown dye, but to my horror it was badly tangled again almost instantly. I went ahead and put the brown dye on so that I could do all of the serious detangling when it was done. However, it wasn't quite that simple.

I have pretty thick, long, curly, color treated hair myself but never have I had such a hard time detangling hair. I had soaked it overnight in conditioner, and when that didn't work, used almost an entire bottle of detangler but it didnt seem to do much, I couldn't pass a wide tooth comb through it at all. After HOURS of brushing it out from tip to roots, soaked in conditioner and detangler it finally got to a manageable place, and I had a whole handful of hair that had been shed in the process. I have heard that some hair suppliers clean and treat low quality hair from multiple donors with harsh chemicals that dissolve the cuticle, then re-coat it with silicon before selling it so it looks smooth... I am certain that is what happened. The worst part is there is no way to really tell until you wash it a couple of times, at which point it can't be returned. How convenient. Seriously, these people should go to jail for fraud, and amazon should be investigated for selling items from any random vendor in unregulated countries. What if an adult gets a life threatening allergic reaction, or a child is poisoned because a toy has lead on it, for example. Who is responsible then? This is not okay and I will be looking into my options to get my money back, although I will never get back the lost time. DONT BUY HAIR ON AMAZON!

title: Calming Blue
text: Hello friends, I received a white and pink, sturdy plastic Miropure UV LED Nail lamp (22x15.5x5.9 cm) with UV shielding gloves and two nail emery boards. This lamp also comes with a 12 month warranty, and 24/7 live chat support. It is a made in China product. It has an input voltage of DC 24V and output voltage of 54W (max). The lamp’s upper mouth contains 30 LEDs. The wavelength is 365nmt 405nm. The unit has a LED display screen with 3 buttons. The buttons are available to set the lamp on 30 seconds, 60 seconds and 99 seconds. This lamp comes in low heat mode, it is recyclable, environmentally safe, non-harmful and non-tanning. The UV LED lamp is only meant for drying or curing the nails. It will not tan the skin or be harmful to the skin. The gloves are an added protection for those who think it may be harmful. Some people also wear sunscreen before placing their hands under a UV lamp. Not only does it do a great job with curing the nails, but it is also fun to look at. Once you plug this lamp up, it illuminates in a cool and relaxing blue. The color blue is captured in the outskirts of the lamp, so please don’t look directly at the light. Long-term exposure can cause damage to your eyes and skin. The light under the lamp does put off a mild heat that may be uncomfortable for some people. The gloves will help to shield the hands from that. It runs off a DC adapter, however, I wish it also ran off of batteries so as to use it anywhere, even while traveling. The emery boards are an added bonus that comes in a cute pink. The gloves are a white PES (polyester) fabric. It’s very thoughtful of Miropure to give these gloves away as a gift. The brand of gel that you use and the number of coats you apply to the nail before placing them under the lamp will determine how long it will take for the gel nail polish to cure (bake/dry) on the nail. The opening of the lamp is big enough for me to place both hands (excluding my thumbs) under the UV light to cure. One full hand (including the thumb) will fit in the mouth of the lamp comfortably. Equally so, I am able to place both of my feet under the lamp at the same time. These lamps are used to cure gel nail polish, but you can absolutely use this lamp to fast dry regular nail polish. Once you plug in the unit, it will be in standby mode. The infrared sensors on this lamp come on automatically when you place your nails under the lamp. If you don’t press a timer button the default timer is automatically set at 120 seconds. Also the 30s/60s settings have a memory settings and the lamp will use the last used time settings as the default time. So, say I pressed 30s and cured my nails for that time. Once I take my hands out and place it under the lamp again, it will automatically set for 30s (as the new default) until I fully use the lamp set at another time or it will also reset back to 120 if I place my hand under the lamp but don’t use it for the full time set. The 99 second button activates the low heat mode. Once you select a timer button on the unit the time will count up to that selected time all while curing the nails. I applied gel polish to my nails and it cured for 60s for the first coat, 60s for the second coat and 60s for the top coat. The nails were completely cured with no streaks and no finger nail print to the touch. Regular nail polish cured for 30s for the first coat, 30s for the second coat and 30s for the top coat with no streaks, clean and smooth to the touch. Both polishes can be purchased at Wal-Mart (please see pictures). Both polishes were also applied to natural nails and not artificial nails. The curing time for artificial nails may be longer. Also memorize the curing time of the gel and regular polish that you are using because you don’t want to max out the lamp’s life as the LEDs can’t be replaced and you will just have to purchase another unit. I would gift this item to anyone practicing to become a nail technician or anyone that likes to paint nails.

title: great shaver, cleaning system superfluous
text:
This is my 4th Norelco, going back quite a few years. My last one was not very good, although the first two were great. The 8160 shaves very close and can handle a two day growth. How long an electric razor stays sharp is very related to how clean it is kept, as hair in the heads will dull the blades faster. To that end, Norelco ships this razor with a motorized stand to clean the razor heads. Basically what it does is submerge the razor in the cleaning fluid and turn it on and off occasionally. So you need not buy the XLCC, just buy the 8160 XL. You can submerge the razor in fluid yourself and turn it on and off a few times to do the same thing, and not have to worry about having space to store the stand. I'm experimenting with making my own cleaning fluid, which as far as I can tell is distilled water with a small amount of glycerine and a bit of an additive such as photo-flo which breaks the surface tension of the water so it will drain right off.

One huge improvement over my prior Norelcos is the ability to rinse the razor throroughly with hot water. It does an excellent job of cleaning the razor, and then the fluid bath is only really needed to condition the heads. You can also buy a silcone spray which lubricates the heads to have them wear better. So save some money but make sure the razor you buy is washable and water tight. I highly recommend the razor itself.

Since i have started using these (and its only been like 3 days), I have noticed a lot less bloating - not just in the face but also in the body. For example, if I don't sleep well (due to insomnia), next day I am usually extremely bloated - both in face and stomach. But after using this and basically a sleepless night, I hardly saw any of my usual bloating. I have been using the roller with serums - i do agree it seems to help them absorb much deeper into the skin. I am using the Gua Sha tool with facial oils. I make sure i use both on my neck, not just in the face, because there are tons of lymph nodes in the neck. Attaching a picture - this is after using 3 days in a row in morning and evening. I am in solidly in my 40s and don't wear makeup - I do feel like there is no sign of any bloating or puffiness in the face at all, and my face feels more sculpted, if that makes sense (or may be its just a feeling, but hey thats ok too!). I like having the longer thicker big curls, rather than the tighter smaller and collier curls - and when i air dry, i usually have big thick curls. But with this diffuser, i end up with smaller tighter curls, which is not exactly what i want. As a result, my hair overall ends up looking another 2-3 inches shorter because the curls are tighter and smaller. So if your hair is wavy and you want more curl definition, this might be great - but for me, going from curly to almost coils/kinky is not a plus. But on the plus side, it does give me good volume at the top of my head and the crown.

text:
What I really like about this product:
They appear to be great quality that should hold up to use.
Beautiful colors and enough variety to go with any outfit I would want to wear them with (I got the blue/silver, purple, black and red bows).

What I think could use improvement:
The bow is not as large as pictured and I had really hoped for the size it seemed to be in order to cover a large portion of my hair (see my pictures as reference).
The arm of the clip is very large at the end (see the picture they provide) and it makes very difficult to push through my hair when it is in a tight bun (how I intend to wear it). This would not be an issue if I was placing the clip around my hair.
The direction it opens means you push it into your hair from right to left and that is the opposite direction I am used to making it awkward to put in (this is a bit nit-picky, but it could be relevant to others as well).

Overall I am satisfied with the purchase, though I may look for a way to replace the arm on the clip to make them easier to use as I intend.

If you've given yourself a brazilian at home, fearlessly pluck your own brows, own/have used an epilator and would be open to trying home laser hair removal, you'll do just fine with this baby.

On the other hand, if you cannot stand the thought of your pubes being removed, wince when your brows are plucked by an aesthetician and generally don't gravitate towards the DIY beauty this isn't for you. Beauty is pain ladies.

This is basically a sander for your foot. You have to keep it moving and not concentrate on a specific spot for to long (i.e. > 4 seconds) or your foot will get quite hot from the friction and it REALLY HURTS like a rug burn x 10. This only happened a couple of times and I actually use with a bowl of ice which I periodically dip my heels into to help keep heat from accumulating. The pain dissipates quickly and the "burned" spot doesn't hurt afterwards but just FYI, the friction burns from this thing are painful.

I bought this after no matter what magical foot scrub and/or pumice stone could smooth my feet. I live in a dry cold climate and consequently my feet get very lizard-ish.

Overall, I'm very happy - I used to snag pantyhose on my rough feet and/or just generally feel unsexy and this took care of that issue. I'm very pleased!

title: Self-tanning product masquerading as an exfoliant
text:
For several years, I have used Mountain Majestic Arabica scrub (available here on Amazon). I obviously was quite pleased with it. This past year, I decided to try some other brands of exfoliants - one was a store brand at a national beauty store (blah) and another that was actually a walnut shell-based product by a brand I like (nothing to write home about). So I decided to go back to my old standard but saw this brand and it WAS a bit cheaper so I ordered it.

I first tried it on my face, rinsed it off, and noticed when I towel dried my face there was brown on my otherwise white towel. Today, I used it all over my body as an exfoliant and ended up with a brown washcloth and another brown-stained towel. A couple more washings with soap seemed to get the brown off my skin, but not my washcloth. It will need to be trashed since it is now a reddish-brown mess. The stains on the towels are not as bad, and I can live with them, but I certainly would never put them out for guests. I have no idea how this product received an average of four stars.

If you want to ruin your towels and shower and dye your skin and hairline a reddish-brown, go for it. Otherwise, avoid this product like the plague. To replace my washcloth, scrub my shower (the guy at the big box store told me the $20 bottle of cleaner he sold me will remove anything), use twice the amount of Tide and bleach called for in trying to wash the dye out, it would have been much cheaper to use my old reliable brand.

As an aside, I'm not sure what type of oils they use in this product, but they are heavy and don't leave a nice feeling on your skin when rinsed off. Also, when reading reviews, start off with the bad ones. You'll get a better idea of the quality of the product in question.

title: Quality Product
text:
I wanted to switch to a foundation that would also double up as a sunscreen, I have heard of this brand before and only recently decided to give it a go. Overall I’m happy that I did take the gamble with this product. I have been using liquid foundations for quite some time, but I hate having to worry about touch ups. This is why I wanted something that I could carry around and easily re-apply/touch up in the day with the summer heat quickly approaching. The product arrived neat and sealed with everything that it should include. The compact isn’t too heavy to carry around in a bag and seems sturdy so far. The cushion which I’ve heard is nice has lived up to its name. It truly is a nice spongy bouncy “mochi” applicator, and I’m super happy to have gotten an extra. I purchased the H+ in #21 Light Beige. This is where my only negative feedback comes in about the company itself. The foundation is a slight shade too dark for my skin, I wish they would offer more shades in the line. I went with the lighter shade thinking if it’s too light I could easily fix that. Although, it is the opposite of what I was hoping for. But because I’m impressed overall with the product itself it won’t be a deal breaker for me. I’m trying to keep a simple routine for make up most days after skin care, I apply this and a small amount of setting spray or powder. It lasts me a good few hours depending on how hot the days are. I haven’t found much touch up needed. It’s easy to apply with the mochi cushion with little mess. The product hasn’t caused me any irritation or break outs that I can tell after using it for a few days. Coverage is about a medium for my slightly oily and dry skin. It won’t cover all marks, but does a good job with redness and evening out my skin tone.

I feel the price is about average for most reviewed and marketed South Korean cushions. I was a little hesitant with the price at first, knowing little access also means having to buy the refill online as well. With the slogan of 99% skincare, 1% makeup it was a good buy and I’m happy about the product.

title: Excellent Beginners Shave Brush
text: The Beau Brummell Shaving Brush is an absolute dream to shave with. Today was my first DE shave, and the brush performed pretty well with no experience on using a shave brush. I received the brush yesterday, and decided to follow a tip I'd found to help break in a brush. To remove the scent, fill up a bowl or cup with hot water and a few drops of dish soap. Let your brush soak in the dish soap for about five minutes, and rinse the brush out until no soap remains. This will also help knock out some loose hairs that are in the brush. Proceed to load your brush with shave soap and build up a lather in a bowl, mug, or on your hand. Once you have a nice shave lather built up in the brush, set the brush down next to your sink and let it stay there overnight. This method claims to help break in the brush by imparting the conditioning qualities of the lather to the brush. The next morning, rinse the brush out completely and it's ready to use. I followed the methods described, and still had some hairs coming out of the brush on my first shave today, but I suspect that is normal. The handle was easy to grip, even though I had shave lather covering most of it while I lathered up my face. Overall I'm very happy with my purchase and will continue to enjoy this great shaving brush.

text:
It is a fart deodorant. It prevents the smell from killing those around around you. I can confirm it works with all the usual offenders: broccoli, brussels sprouts, beef, fish, dairy, etc. I don't eat beans but probably works for those too. I have done some research into farts and it appears that the compounds in the food you eat are what make the stench (separate from the gas itself - methane apparently has no odor...), and this does something to neutralize that.

You do need to have a couple throughout the day for it to work - can't just take one and hope for it to work, I usually have 2-3 per day for it to work perfect; 4 if I'm eating a lot.

I will state very adamantly though that I was extremely disappointed that you can buy it direct from the company that makes it, Parthenon I think, for 13 bucks a bottle. Yes, you must pay shipping, but it's highway robbery to charge 50% more for no additional value [as of this writing, I'm only seeing it for 20 bucks per bottle at its cheapest, in a 2-pack]. title: Cute Scrunchies At A Good Price!
text:
I ordered the 2 piece scrunchies in Black and Brown and I have to say, I am pleased overall with the product. The scrunchies came very well packaged - each in it's own plastic wrapping (I like to mention this because some sellers don't care how they send the item).

When I took it out of the package, I noticed the scrunchie is a nice size (about the size of your palm) and the stitching was tight and secure (in other words, not cheaply made). The colors were also a deep black and a deep brown, which is great for workplaces or other "formal" locations. I do wish these scrunchies came in more colors, however, for going out to dinner, parties, or just wanting something different.

Just like with other type scrunchies, I did have to readjust my hair a few times throughout the day to tighten the hold as it tends to slip a bit over time. It's about the same amount of times I do with any other scrunchie, however.

The real test for me, however, was taking the scrunchie off. One of my pet peeves is when they pull at my hair while doing so. This one did not have the same amount of pulling as other scrunchies have, as stated in the description (and why I got them). So I am pleased to report this convenience.

The only thing I found to be a disadvantage (and taking one star off) is that I don't feel these scrunchies will last the test of time. I've only used them about 10 times and I already see they are starting to twist up and not keep their original shape. The other scrunchies I have used have lasted longer in this regard.

But, overall, I think this is a great product and would recommend.

title: Great product, better value
text:
TL;DR - It's cheap and it works.

Actual review:

I have been using Beardsmen Beard Oil for about 4 or 5 months now. There were 3 key factors and things I wanted to achieve in a beard oil (I had never used it previously):

1. I wanted it to stop the itching.
2. I wanted it to soften the hair for less of a "coarse" feeling.
3. I didn't want to spend $15 for 1 ounce of oil.

This bear oil hits all 3 points. Anyone who's shopped beard oils at all already knows it's probably the best value by far, you get 4x as much as what most other companies give you for the same price.

As for the itching, it definitely helps with that. You do have to make sure to rub the oil deep into the beard so it gets to your skin (Beardsmen gives you a link to a very detailed PDF guide on beard care and product use). If you just put the oil on the hair, it's not going to help your itchy skin (this is true for any oil).

Finally, beard softness. One quick anecdote will answer this: About a month ago I got lazy with my morning routine and stopped using beard oil (along with other things like face wash and cologne). About a week into this, I had some contact with my ex-wife (don't ask) and she specifically asked if I was still using the oil, as my beard was not as soft as it had been. When the ladies notice that you stopped using it, you know it works.

Long story short, I would easily consider this the "best buy" in beard oil.

As some other people have suggested, I will probably finish this package and then continue to do it maybe once a week. I read somewhere that to appear natural, your teeth should be no whiter than the white in your eyes.

This product gets 4 stars because of all the gross drooling, I can't imagine using this product anywhere other than behind a closed and locked and mirror-less room. No one was collecting it there though and I only found out later that it was supposed to taste like chocolate which made me curious enough to buy this product. Let me state this vehemently up front: It does not taste like chocolate at all! What's reminiscent of chocolate is the color and the texture when stirred into milk but the flavor surely has nothing to do with chocolate. If I'd compare it in flavor to anything I'd say it reminds a bit of dried fig. Note I am not writing about a roasted/toasted carob product here as I have never tried that. I'm not saying this is a bad product but people should stop describing it as a good substitute for chocolate. That's just a marketing gimmick. If chocolate flavor with lower calories is what you are after this is the better product to buy: Viva Labs - Organic Cacao Powder. title: Don't hesitate if your on the fence--glad I took the plunge
text:
To me, the "high" setting felt exactly like treatments I have received in the dr's office. My skin was very smooth and felt wonderful after use. I was on the fence regarding whether or not to buy this product because I thought that there must be some gimmick-- else why would so many women go to get this done professionally if they could have a machine at home? I'm glad I purchased because I get the same result for much less money, not to mention time wasted making weekly appointments. Keep in mind:

*Crystal refills are an additional expense
*The warranty card must be sent in within 10 days of purchase to be valid
*There are different settings so that you can control intensity
*Comes with instructional dvd
*One application covered my entire face and I still had a bit more than half a cartridge left--so one cartridge could last two applications if you just do your face.

I purchased my machine from a flash sale site so I got a bit of a discount but I would pay full price for this in a heartbeat--it's great. You should go to the manufacturer's website and price shop with amazon to see where you can get the best deal. the manufacturer's website also sells complementary products but I can't comment on them because I have not tried any.

text: This oil is NOTHING close to pure musk oil, which comes from the Musk Deer. Pure musk oil is intoxicating. Just the slightest hint of authentic pure miusk oil(whether on your skin or not) entirely elevates one's spirit and trigges an instant sense of harmony, well being; and self-confidence-- not to mention its magnetic influence (power of attraction due to phermones). This product that is advertised as 87% Black Deer Musk Attar is absolutely NOT what I was seeking. A few years ago, I had already found a musk oil similar to this one but it has a hint of a soft, baby powder-like scent, making it more feminine. title: My specific application.
text: As one always on the lookout for better ways to model "chips" in paint, I chose this product with the intention of applying by sponge, and removing with a Q-Tip or masking tape. Because of the small scale of my project, I used a fine sponge (the type that comes on foam paint brushes). This necessitated that the quantity of Micro Mask be very thin in depth and tiny in area covered. When applied in this way, the film still acts as a barrier to the top coat of paint, but becomes unrecognizable where it was applied, after the top coat dries (as opposed to the chipping by salt technique, where the evidence of salt stays visible after the top coat is applied). And because of the thin layer of Micro Mask and the thick layer of rattle can top coat, only the use of an X-Acto knife was sufficient for scraping off the topcoat and Micro Mask. The Micro Mask did assist to some extent in removing the topcoat, but a lot of top coat that was not covered by the Micro Mask was also removed. However, in a chipping effect, where paint damage is the intended desire, the results overall were actually very good. (The topcoat as the final visible color of one's project has the "chips" in it from weathering, revealing the hidden base coat - which can be reddish to depict rust, or grayish to depict primer.)

title: Nice combo pack. Good overall value.
text:
I like this shave kit for several reasons. First the four products you get (they say 6, but they are counting the cheap dopp bag and something else) go really well together and I think you save about ten dollars by buying it as a kit. I have naturally dry and sensitive skin. So I like a mild facial cleanser and that is what you get here. This face cleanser is not a soapy type cleaner. If you are used to a normal sudsy face wash, then this will take a little getting used to. Basically with this facial wash, a little goes a long way. You will not get a big lather from it, and it does kind of have a slimy consistency but it smells very nice to me. They say it is odorless, but I find it has a slightly medicinal peppermint smell, that I actually like. The shave cream and aftershave actually have the same smell. I like it. It smells manly to me. One warning though. There have been days where i couldn't wash my face for whatever reason and the next day I have used double the amount I normally use, and it has made my face feel extremely dry and tight. So don't use more than a quarter sized amount on your face and neck unless you have oily skin.
The pre-shave oil I use after washing my face. To me it is the pre-shave oil that is the star of this kit. If you are someone who feels that they get a great benefit from using a pre-shave oil, then you will like this oil. I have found this to be my favorite pre-shave oil, even against those that are twice the price. Again, a little goes a long way. You only need to drip a tiny bit on your fingertips for each side of your face and neck. I find using a pre-shave oil gives my face an elasticity that it wouldn't have otherwise. It just seems to make the razor glide more effortlessly than with just a regular shave cream. I also find that since it is an oil (and this is among the thicker shave oils you will find) it tends to stay on your face even after the shave and condition it. If you have dry skin like me, this is actually a huge plus. I have found my skin to have less razor bumps and a more even complexion from using these four products, and again, I think it is the shave oil which makes the biggest difference.
After the pre-shave oil you apply the shave cream. The cream is good but not great to me. It is a cream that doesn't lather, and I actually like a lighter cream with less lather when using a shave oil underneath. The cream has peppermint in it, so you will feel a tingle on your face when you use it. It does a good job on its own, but paired with the shave oil it produces a very clean, calming shave experience.
Finally the aftershave balm. I tend to like balms after a shave more than anything else. Again, that goes back to my dry skin and need for moisture. I find this balm to be soothing and not harsh. These are fairly concentrated products so you don't want to use too much, if you do, then it will feel tacky and not absorb well. If you have used the very popular Nivea Sensitive Aftershave Balm, this product will feel like a more upscale version of that product. Again a pepperminty medicinal smell that I don't mind at all lingers for an hour or so after you are done using the balm with all the other products.
Overall, I find the kit to be a good value and the products work well together to help give you a good shave and a well conditioned face. My only small gripe would be that all the packaging is gray now, except for the face wash. The white packaging looked much fresher and high end then the gray packaging, but no big deal. Just wanted to point that out, so you don't think you received the wrong order when you get a different color packaging than what it is in the pic.

title: Definitely sold on this!!!
text:
I originally bought another highly rated cream that has DMSO in it, but there are also a lot of other strong smelling scents and it doesn't really do a whole lot. I was also a little afraid to try it after receiving it since the small print states that it is being sold as a "solvent". In the art world, that means to me that it will eat away other things (think turpentine LOL), and the warning stated that it could damage the skin. Yikes!

I reviewed this one some while ago. I've now been using this for at least a year and a half and it is the best pain relief cream I've ever used, and I've tried a lot. First, it doesn't have a lot of the medicinal odor that many pain relief creams use due to the camphor and menthol in the others. I don't have to use much before I get relief (although I'll admit that when I start hurting in bed I also use a heat pad)...but it's the use of so little that is well worth the price and recently it was marked lower so I made sure and bought two to stock up on. Every time a friend complains of pain I share some and then they remark how great it was for them as well. I don't ever want to run out of this since it works fast, uses very little, and lasts a long while.

Unfortunately, or fortunately, however one wants to look at it, I have been in extreme pain for years now. I have Plantar Fasciitis on the right foot, a swollen Achilles Tendon (an MRI showed it being strained and my ankles as being torn but the doctor only had me go to 3 months of PT for that), spondylosis in both the cervical and lumbar spines, and sciatica. I was beginning to feel hopeless at ever feeling good again. So then, I thought, with as many people who have touted the wonders of this particular jar of cream, what do I have to lose. Maybe a little skin, but maybe, just maybe I could lose some of the pain.

WOW!!! Am I ever glad I finally gave in! I opened it up 3 nights ago, and almost immediately felt the pain easing away from the areas I rubbed the cream in to. I had a pretty decent night's sleep and the cream seemed to keep the pains at bay for at least 5-6 hours. Yesterday, however, I had to go to town and didn't get around to putting anything on before going. Going to town out here in rural American is a half day affair. The closest grocery stores and such are at least 35-40 mins drive away. So I wound up being back in extreme pain by the time I returned, put groceries away, cooked and ate dinner, and cleaned up from dinner. But I put some more on before settling down to watch a movie last night and voila, it seemed to ease the pains again, so before I fell asleep I put some more on and again, had another more restful night's sleep. This morning, before I even got up and started my day, I put some on my feet and my neck and they feel pretty good. I didn't get any on my lumbar spine and that's beginning to hurt, so as soon as I get this posted, I will be putting some on my lumbar spine area. I am definitely sold on this and will buy more when I start getting low, however, a little goes a long way, so I think it will probably last me for quite a long while. I highly recommend it and will be telling family and friends about it, as well. I am definitely sold!!!

title: Perfect for polygel/gel-hybrid nails
text:
These dual form nail tips are perfect for creating polygel nails. They come in 10 sizes and are reusable. Clean them with rubbing alcohol to keep them in tip-top shape. Simply apply your polygel into the appropriately sized dual tip, press the polygel to the nail, cure with LED light, and then squeeze the dual form gently at the tip to release it until it pops off.

I've noticed my dual forms appear a little "cloudy" after I have reused them a few times, but they are still working well. They create a seamless and beautiful nail for those of us who don't quite have the time, skills, patience, etc. to create polygel nails in buildable layers with a brush. (You can find plenty of tutorials online.)

Filling in the nail after a couple of weeks, in my opinion, is more easily done by simply filling in polygel material with a brush around the cuticle. I tried filling in with a dual form and it turned out okay - but it was just easier for me personally without the dual form.

The only negative comment I have is that it's very hard to read the numbers for the nail sizes because the tips are clear. If you dump out all your nail tips on the ground accidentally, you're going to have a fun time sorting those out. (So don't do that. Keep the lid closed firmly when you're not using them.)

title: Remove the Octyl Methoxycinnamate for a Fifth Star!
text:
I love this product but they should remove the octyl methoxycinnamate!
I would be *in love* with this sunscreen, but the missing star is for the added ingredient: Octyl Methoxycinnamate. Zinc oxide is the other ingredient that acts as a sunscreen, and I wish it were the only one. My background is in science; I'm not just knee-jerk reacting to a long chemical name. The Environmental Working Group (ewg.org) has some excellent databases. Their Sunscreen Database states that this ingredient mimics hormones in lab animals (as another reviewer stated). I wish Oz Naturals would remove this ingredient.

The tint isn't a coverup, but I think it does a decent job as a foundation if you're like me and cannot stand wearing foundation. It spreads on easily; you could get by with very little as a moisturizer, but I put on a fairly generous amount to allow the zinc oxide to work as a sunscreen. Don't worry about turning orange. I should note that I'm Hispanic but my skin tone tans easily but leans toward pale for HIspanics.

I've tried doing the 'smokey eye' look with the standard eyebrow pad things that come in the package with the shadow. Usually I end up looking like I have a black eye. I typically try it every few months, and realize that I'm never going to get it right, and stick the shadow back into my makeup bag.

After a conversation with my hair stylist, she mentioned that I needed to get eye brushes instead of using those pad things. Living in a small town, I was unable to find any brushes that seemed to be the thing (heck, I couldn't even find a blush brush at our local Walmart). Which means, of course, it was time to check out Amazon.

I found the Sephora Collection eye brush set. It seemed to be the thing that I wanted. Heck, it even comes with instructions in the case. I knew that Sephora had a good reputation, while being a bit pricey, but I went ahead and purchased them. I'm glad I did. There are several different types of brushes, as well as a bottle of mascara. There's an eyeliner brush that I'd never even knew existed. I'd always used a pencil (was never very good with liquid liner). The eyeliner brush works great. That was my biggest surprise. The ability to load eye shadow into the brush without overloading it makes all the difference. I can control how much goes on my lid, keeping me from the 'shiner' look. The instructions in the case make it nearly foolproof.

All in all, this is a great set. There are times I'll purchase something like this and find that I don't use it, or regret the cost. As someone who is NOT a makeup fanatic, I do not regret this purchase at all.

title: A true disappointment, read before you buy!
text:
I'll start by saying that I'm using oils for more than 5 years, I know what to look for, and I've used many different companies.

I wanted to try this company for a long time, but I thought the price is too high (more on that later), and I can get a triple amount of oil by different companies for the same price,
After a bit of reviews reading, and recommendations by youtubers (which now I believe they were paid reviews) I decided to try anyway,

The cost of the 4 oils package is 50$, additional 4$ for the "premium" scents, which I took 2 of, and a very high 10$~ shipping cost- when all the other sellers offer free shipping,
Sums out at around 64$~ for 4oz oil (and to be honest, I usually buy grave before shave 4 oz bottle of my favorite smell for 25$ Inc. Shipping).

The delivery wasn't fast, but i knew it from the beginning, but also didn't include any tracking or home delivery(unlike other companies) so I basically paid a lot for waiting a lot and picking it up from the post office without knowing when it will come.

The package was great! It was very well packed, also included 2×tiny branded cloth bags, and I really liked it.

I've ordered those smells:

1.The ladies man- lovely lemon vanilla smell, very gentle but precise.

2.The outlaw- supposed to be tobacco, vanilla and pepper but smells really bad, usually this is my favorite smell from every company, but this one was horrible, something between a sewer and a dirty toilet,
I gave it a chance anyways, thought maybe im exaggerating , 3 minutes after my girlfriend asked me to wash my face.

3.ell burrista (premium +2$)- coffee,
Idk what is so premium about it, smells just like every other coffee artificial smell, not even a true representation of real coffee smell,
Might come in handy for some people but ,not my cup of tea ;), and I'm saying that as a coffee lover.

4. The royal knight(premium +2$)-
Well, I know lavender, I know vanilla and I know earl grey tea smells,
But it not even close,
This one gives the vibes of a chemical air refresher smell (maybe it'll work with the toilet smell of the outlaw), with a hint of a 70 years old man cologne.

Moreover, I'll state that the scents stays for 10-30min and then it's gone, while I'm truly happy that those horrible scents gone fast, I would really like the only good scent(ladies man) to stay more.., some companies have the opposite problem though.

My beard is medium sized, and usually I use 4-7 drops (depends on the day since it's quite hot in here all of the year), but it felt like I had to use around 10 drops to really nourish my skin.

All that being said, The quality of the product itself is great and I do not feel any dryness or itchiness at all.

I really hope the company will see that review and improve over time, really liked the idea of the scents and wanted to justify the price, but I'm too disappointed and I do not think it's even justified to sell those at half the price.

Hoped it helped someone, stay bearded

title: Very good, but the pro-health is better
text:
I've been brushing my teeth wih oral-b for over 10 years now, and they are all similar to the vitality model. I've always used the least expensive model since I see no difference from the expensive ones, unless you are looking for "extras", like timer, lcd screen, etc. The vitality is a very good brush. I use the round head instead of the elongated. I rather brush my teeth with oral-b than any other eletric brush on the market. The sonic kind hurts my gum and it tickles a lot as well. Oral-B, and their entry level eletric brushes are the way to go. I can't brush my teeth with regular toothbrush anymore. Brush heads are cheaper on ebay but I found out they don't last as long as those you buy at grocery stores around $20 for 3. I buy the precision clean brush in bulk on ebay for around $1 each. They last a good 2 months. The ones at walmart/amazon and such last 3 months or more. The bad thing about the vitality rechargeable and all the older oral-b I own is that you need to recharge it after 3-4 days of 2-3 daily brushings. I think this is annoying. I didn't want to leave the brush recharging after every use. So I bought the ORAL-B Pro-Health that uses two AA batteries. It is simply AMAZING. The quality is the same as the rechargeables, but it is even better. The batteries lasts forever on the pro-health. I put 2 rechargeable AA (2000 MA) and the thing kept going and going without a noticeable lack of power for a good 2 months. It is the best. The vitality rechargeable brush gets very slow after 3-4 days. Not with the pro-health. Buy the pro-health. It is the way to go if you like this kind of ORAL-B design. Another thing is ORAL-B equipment lasts forever. I only have one eletric brush where the original rechargeable battery died on me. And since they are the entry level brushes, I just buy another one of the same. No need to buy another battery.
Again, go with the ORAL-B PRO-HEALTH eletric toothbrush.

title: Interesting
text:
My daughter had been asking to dye her hair blue for a while now. I did a lot of research and out of sleep the options this seemed to be the safest, most natural, and most importantly quick to wash out should anything go wrong.
We did get the peppermint blue, shipping was great, the tube is huge, we will get at least 2 full applications out of one tube. Her hair is about down to her shoulder blades. It wasn't highlighted or bleached beforehand and my daughter's natural hair color is a dark blond. There were some natural highlights in her hair from being out in the sun all summer though. After reading the reviews I decided to dye her hair in our kitchen sink. It is a very dark color, so I wasn't worried about stains (and didn't get any, a few on the counter top but those lifted of quickly after soaking them in Lysol kitchen cleaning spray) and we ended up completing the whole process right there. We did the slightly wet hair, applied the gel liberally (no dripping issues) , put on a shower cap, used the blow dryer on high heat for 15 minutes, and then lost track of time so the color stayed on her hair for an additional 45 minutes. We lost track of time because this color does stain the skin like crazy. I even prepped her with Vaseline beforehand but her whole forehead, both ears, and neck were completely blue.
I dye my own hair with permanent color and never have any trouble cleaning spills off my skin.
This was different. We tried wet wipes, lotion and cotton balls, nothing worked. After some time on Google I tried a recommendation to spray a cotton ball with hairspray and rub off the color stains. This worked well on her face, but ears and neck still have bright stains. Not too big of a deal as you don't spot them right away. We rinsed out with lukewarm water and it ran clear pretty quickly, then Shampoo (I used Albany Botanica without Sulfates, etc.) , towel , and lastly blowdryed her hair. The color on her skin was the bright blue it showed on the website. The color of her hair on the other hand is a blueish green. You could tell right after taking the shower cap off, but I wanted to see what the blow dryer would turn it into. The regular colored hair is a milder green color, the parts which are lighter are a deeper green. It looks nice on her and she is very happy with it but it is by no means anywhere close to what the color is supposed to look like. No blue whatsoever. The smell of the product itself was pleasant, even my daughter didn't complain, the application was easy enough with her head being upside down over the sink, the blow drying was a little annoying but not unmanageable, and coloring in a safe area where stains were avoidable, and being sure to wear old clothing and use an old towel made it pretty stress-free.
I am not sure how this color would turn out on hair which has been bleached but the whole purpose of using this color was to avoid the bleaching.
In short. Had she really insisted to get the color we purchased the gel in this would have been a total bust. Since she likes the color as it turned out and the application process itself wasn't difficult I am giving the product three stars. Maybe be flexible with your expectations if you choose this color. Since we are I will probably try some other colors from this brand in the future. If you want exact color results this would be too much of a gamble for me to try.

title: my first experience with epilator
text:
till i was in india, body hair removal was not a concern. all i needed was to visit a beauty salon and shell out around Rs. 150 (or $3, unbelievable right?) for waxing of legs, arms and underarms. but after coming to US hair removal became an issue as professional waxing is hell costly. I tried to do it at home with ready to use wax strips, which are okay to use on legs, but one can not use them efficiently for arms plus you end up in a sticky mess. then i tried shaving. shaving gives a smooth effect to skin but for only a few hours and it also started causing irritation to my underarms may be because of the coarse stubs of hair.
finally i decided to buy epilator and instantly liked the Braun's wet & dry one as it's cordless and can be used in shower. with a pleasant surprise the product reached me within three days of placing order (my first ever purchase with amazon and i instantly fall in love with amazon).

i never used an epilator before and was a bit scared as according to some reviews the process hurts. i decided to use it in shower with the pivoting cap, though i did not use the pre epilation wipes it came with(the pack is still unopened). for the initial 1-2 min it actually felt a bit painful but eventually my skin adapted to the pinching sensation. the most difficult part was to use it for underarms. it was so painful that i had to run cold water (and it really helps to subsidize the pain)after every few seconds of epilation, but this is just the first time. if you can brave that you definitely going to fall in love with epilating ur under arms. it's better than waxing as u don't need to wait for all the hair to grow up to a certain length and even a single visible hair can be removed just whenevr you want. after one month of use i have notice that my under arm hair looks thinner and softer, so it hardly hurts during removal. also it's equally effective for bikini line.
the product is really compact, handy and one can use it just anywhere anytime. the battery back up is more than enough to complete your job in one go. i found the spot light really helpful as it makes even the smallest of hair noticeable, if you want a quick epilation better to use it without the pivotal head and use it dry.

my suggestion would be go for it and simply forget all the hassles and cost associated with waxing or irritation of shaving.

title: Great for Spa Nights at Home!
text:
I love these! They puff up in liquid like little marshmallows, and are easy to peel apart to form the full mask. It works for my face size/shape just fine (a smidge small for men maybe). They appear to be high quality, and I love that they're individually wrapped! I throw these in my travel bags to use with my serums and lotions, and give them away for people interested. I've used these with blended aloe vera, gels, serums, hyaluronic acid, high moisture "lotions" and so much more.

I usually remove the packaging, drop the "tablet" into the well-mixed up liquid/gel concoction I chose that day, and wait for it to puff up. Then I peel it apart to form the full mask, plop it back in the liquid/gel to absorb some more, and throw it in the fridge (because I like the masks cold). I use these after showering and cleaning my face, and watch tv or read with it on. Once I feel the edges start to feel slightly dry, I peel it off and massage the rest of it into my skin, and top off with another moisturizer before bed.

title: Great Soaps that Smell and Feel Amazing!!
text:
I just started using Zum bars and overall loving everything about them. They are on the more expensive side when it comes to soaps, but I feel they are worth every penny considering what you are getting. They are all natural using minerals, herbs, and essential oils, along with pH balancing goats milk. The soaps themselves come in a wide array of scents and textures and do not irrtiate or dry out my skin. I love how they make me feel after use and how they make my whole bathroom smell for the rest of the day. I feel with that alone, it makes it worth the price. So far I've only used the sea salt one and I love the exfoliating properties it possesses with actual pieces of salt embedded in the soap.

One thing I've noticed, is the soaps are softer and while this helps with their moisturizing aspect it also means they won't last long. I found cutting the bars in smaller pieces (in thirds), and keeping the rest in parchment or in a dry place helps extend the life by quite a bit. Also usng a loofah to help with the lather and storing the soaps on or in something to minimize water contact helps too, I feel for each bar, I can make last about 2 months using these extra steps.

My only issue with the ingredients is the fact they do use palm oil from RSPO and unless it can truly be eithically sourced and sustainable without the destruction of forests and threats to indigenous people, it makes it harder to support these products for the long term. Just be wary of that. I do hope some day they can phase that out and find an alternative as I do adore these products

title: NO TEMPERATURE CONTROL. WORTH 20 BUCKS MAX
text:
This thing is absolutely NOT WORTH THE FULL PRICE OF $150. Not even the sale price of $45. If you're looking into getting it, DO NOT PAY MORE THAN $20. There's no temperature control on this, and yes that absolutely is a make-it-or-break-it thing. And this one is presented with extremely misleading wording that makes you think there IS temperature control here (the part that says something about digital temperature control that shuts off instantly? Blatant lie, there's NO TEMPERATURE CONTROL AT ALL, LET ALONE DIGITAL!!) There's no single temperature that works for every hair type. Further, with no screen telling you what temperature it is, you'll never know if something messes up and turns higher, resulting in destroying your hair. Honestly for $45 (which is the sale price) you can get a far better iron WITH temperature control. And the marble look is pretty, but not worth not having control over what temperature my flat iron is at.

So my advice: if you find it for 20 bucks, yeah sure it's worth it as a "for now" item. But if you're looking for a keeper, even 20 bucks isn't worth it because throw in another 20 and you can get a keeper with all the features every flat iron SHOULD have that this flat iron lacks.

title: Adorable Kid-Friendly Unicorn Headband
text:
I purchased this headband for my 4 month old. Her cousin was turning one and having a unicorn themed party. We all agreed that our little girls would dress up as unicorns for a photo op; this was perfect! I was really surprised by how well made the headband was. The tulle on the back (the "mane") is attached securely and flows down the back of the head without getting in the child's face. It's also a very soft tulle that is not itchy and has caused no irritation to my kiddo's sensitive skin.

The ears, flowers, and horn are also all securely fastened to the band. The ears have purple glitter, the flowers are kind of a faux satin, and the horn is a shiny silky pink material that has a plush feeling to it. Definitely VERY kid friendly and I have a feeling this is going to be a hit with my daughter when she gets a bit older and wants to play dress-up.

The actual band part is covered in a really soft white material. It was very gentle on my girl's head and she didn't seem to mind wearing it at all. In fact she was happily smiling the entire time. It was so darn cute! All in all, I'm so happy with this purchase. I'd definitely buy it again and have recommended it to friends and family who thought it was just oh-so-cute. I haven't purchased or seen any of the other unicorn headbands on Amazon- but the quality of this one was way above my expectations.

I've seen these for as little as $40 but most on Amazon are about $60. Installation was simple. I just used a thin flathead screwdriver, popped out one end and used my keys to hold it open (if you don't put something in to hold the one side it will pop back in when you go to open the other side). text: I’m rating this product four stars. I think quality wise it’s slightly above average. The first thing I want to point out is how sharp it is; this is why I’m rating it four stars. The razor is pretty efficient because of its sharpness. My husband felt as though he passed the razor less times on his face; he said the razor was more precise when shaving. I’ll provide additional pictures of the product so you can see what comes in the box. The box comes with instructions, blades, a razor cover, a razor handle, and a small shaving gel. I also liked the razor cover. Most razor covers are all enclosed they will cause the razor itself to not air out and eventually rust; this cover also clips so you’re safe from accidentally cutting yourself. Overall, the biggest reason why I gave four stars was because of the sharpness. However, there are some downsides. In my opinion, the downside to the razor’s sharpness is it can be a hazard if you’re not careful. The blades we received were extremely sharp we had to be extra cautious. We normally buy very average razors. Second, this razor did not seem to provide a smooth experience like others for sensitive skin…at least for us. I believe it only has one moisture strip whereas other razors we’ve tried have more. Furthermore, the small shaving gel provided definitely feels natural; it’s not as thick or foamy as other gels or creams out there. You may have to use your own gel or cream because the one provided in the box is very light. You also need to be cautious when connecting the blade to the handle; we had a difficult time until we finally figured it out. Lastly, we had mixed feelings about the handle…but it certainly adds weight and provides durability which is a plus. All in all, I do recommend the product.

text:
I recently had a facial and they used a sheet mask and used face globes on top of the sheet mask for a massage. It felt so amazing as soon as I returned home I decided I was on the hunt for a pair for myself. I am sure they used a more expensive pair as a professional place, but I wanted something cheap. I searched and saw lots of reviews for glass globes that broke or shattered, which seems scary to me. That is why I decided to go with a metal pair and ordered these.

FIRST IMPRESSIONS
These come in a nice little box but there is no case for them other than that. I do wish they came with a little storage case so I could place it all in the fridge and keep them clean, but I just threw them in a sandwich bag and it will work just fine. I placed them in the fridge (I have no desire to use them in the freezer as I think that would be too cold for comfort). There is a warning on the package that says not to leave them in the "fridge" for more than 20 min, but I think they meant to say "freezer" so that they don't burst or something from freezing. I have had mine in the fridge since I got them and other than the time I used them so far, they have stayed in there and they are fine. I washed them with a little soap when they first arrived just to make sure they were clean before applying anywhere near my face, but they appeared to be clean right out of the box.

PERFORMANCE
I removed them from the fridge and used them on my sheet mask for about 25 minutes and they remained nice and chilly. I am sure you can use them to apply serums or lotions but I don't think I would enjoy direct contact with the metal even at room temperature, not sure why but maybe I'll try it in the future. The feeling when running them over the sheet mask on your face though... so relaxing! I do wish they were a bit smaller, because the larger size makes it basically impossible to run them across my undereye area which I think would be so nice. The rubber pads are nice and keep them comfortable to hold.

OVERALL
Overall I am very pleased with this purchase and would recommend these particular face globes for several reasons. They stay cold for a long time, they are low cost, and they feel safe being that they are metal.

title: ES3831K (Black one) - Excellent value shaver
text:
What a great little shaver for $13! I recommend it.

I have used a blade for over 10 years, and that was after many years of electric shaving (Remington/Braun). I have been using a Fusion for a while, but the price of blades seems high, they last no more than a couple weeks each and I'm always getting nicked around the chin area. (- what a life-saver those Styptic pencils are!). Then there's the foam and the mess. I decided to go back to electric shaving if I could find a cheaper alternative that gave me a reasonably good shave.
The Amazon reviews indicated this series of shavers fit my requirements. I chose the slightly cheaper ES3481K which does not have a trimmer or a carry case (despite what the product description says), but it does have the usual see-thru snap-on, foil cover.
My first impressions were - looks like an electric shaver; easy to access the cutter; once you work out how to open the battery compartment cover, that seems well-sealed against moisture; it's quite noisy with two new AA batteries, but no more-so than any other electric shaver; it's comfortable to hold and about the size you'd expect for a single blade shaver, but not particularly compact for travel - unless you compare it with expensive models that are often very large.
When using it for the first time (a dry shave) at lunchtime after a Fusion shave only 5 hours before, the shave was smooth, simple and fast. No nicks even where I got nicked this morning and the result is actually a really good close shave, especially around the neck area. I have found that even the Fusion cannot remove all the stubble on my neck without creating soreness, yet without much effort, this shaver has done an arguably better job. Not perfect, but who's going to know except my wife and she would like me to grow a beard!!
Overall, this shaver seems to meet the good reviews it has received on Amazon. I'm happy and who can complain at the price? The manual recommends a new foil every year and a cutter every two years - that's cheaper than the blades over the same time period, if it's true. As a reviewer said, it's almost worth buying more; for home, work, the car, etc. You can always have a close shave, because you can then shave several times a day.

I will update this review when I've tried the wet shave and after a few weeks of use.

Update #1: I've tried the shaver for both dry and wet shaves. Shaving was done in the morning both times.

For the dry shave I showered first, dried off and applied AFTA pre-electric shave lotion at the sink. The shave was good, the neck and jaw-line stubble took some extra time as always. Generally happy with the result.

The wet shave was in the shower, at the end of the usual shower routine. I used my body wash lotion - it has olive oil and tea tree oil in it, so provided a good shaving medium and lubrication. I rinsed off the foil a couple times in the shower spray during the shave. I found the shave more comfortable to do than the dry one and it seemed to achieve a much closer shave, even though, again, the neck and jawline took extra time to do thoroughly.
After each shave, I applied some liquid soap to the upright foil and ran the shaver until foam appeared on the foil surface, per Panasonic's instructions. Then rinsed the shaver under running water. This really keeps the cutting system clean and presumably sharp. Much better than brushing and blowing hairs all over the sink that I had to do with my previous dry-only electric shavers.

I really noticed the difference between the wet and dry shaves the following morning. The dry shave resulted in a lot of stubble the next day. The wet shave was significantly less stubble.

CONCLUSION: The wet shave gives the best result and is less irritating to the skin, due to the lubrication from the lotion. This little shaver really does a great job in the shower.

Update #2: Used everyday and I'm still on the same Duracell batteries I fitted when I bought the shaver! More than the 90 minutes battery life in the specs.

Update #3: May 7 2010 - Finally decided to change out the batteries after about 3 months. Noticeable increase in speed of the shaver and it seemed to have more power to slice through those whiskers. Maybe better to swap them out sooner rather than later, but the shaver doesn't really sound much different as time goes on.

I have settled on a dry shave each day using Afta and a wet rinse as described above. Not having a usable mirror in the shower made getting a complete shave tricky. The result is not as good but works well enough.

I saw the price was drastically reduced on the Silver one, as well as the black, in April, so decided to also order the silver one because of the travel case and trimmer option. (there's always one hair that seems to escape the shaver foil and the trimmer removes it easily) What a deal for such a great little shaver - can't beat it for value.

I love this mask! For those who have not yet tried it... You need to first open your pores. I do this with a nice hot shower. Then after my shower, i pat dry my face and apply the mask. You need a good thick coating of mask otherwise it does not work as well and is hard to remove. I found that using a mask brush of some form works best, you can squirt a little right from the tube onto the brush and apply it. This way you can avoid getting it all over your hands and nails because it can be a little difficult to wash off. Make sure it is COMPLETELY dry then peel it off at a smooth steady rate of speed. Yes, for those sensitive types it may be a bit painful, and it does tend to remove your peachy fuzz hairs but honestly, I don't think it is as bad as many of the videos you may have seen. Finally, Make sure that you close your pores after!!! Use an ice cube, cold water, astringent, or whatever you like but make sure you close those puppies or the mask is pointless! :-)

This is a great buy and a great mask! (I have very large pores and rather oily and sensitive skin that is prone to blackheads, pimples, and easily clogged pores as well as irritation)

title: This WORKS
text:
Ok - this is the real deal. It works, and you will get salon results. Unfortunately, things are getting crazy expensive in certain areas of the US leading us all to a strong DIY culture. You will get salon results for a minimal fraction of the cost.
The fumes are STRONG, and toxic, as we all know.
I started the blowout near a window inside my house with a N95 mask. Some of the fumes still made it to my nose. At that point I stopped and continued the rest of the process at my porch.
From now on, I will do the whole process at the porch, AND will always keep lab goggles on (some of the fumes made it to my eyes even at the porch, and it stung bad), AND gloves throughout the process. I got a BAD rash on my hands because I stopped using the gloves after I finished putting the product on. You need protection in your hands while blowing out the hair, and while straightening it, too.

All in all, I feel safer doing this process at home, in my porch, with a mask, gloves, and lab goggles on, than at a salon without any of these precautions. Salon’s “well ventilated” area is usually a joke. Plus the cost for the process at a salon is truly ridiculous. Note: I’ve tried the No-formaldehyde treatments and they don’t work much for me, but it could be worth it to try it first before this one. Also note that many products that say that do not contain the damaging chemical end up producing it when in contact with heat. So I think you can just do this one but with the proper caution.
TL;DR, this product is a dream. It’s life changing for those of us with a difficult hair. I usually just end up with a bun, and even then, my curly frizzy baby hairs come out. This product straightened my hair, and gave it a glow & shine that I have never naturally possessed, even when using the “curly girl method” religiously. This gives lasting results. BUT fumes are REAL, and I will be more prepared next time. I will do the process at my porch while using the proper PPE.

I have extremely oily skin, and this does a very good job at lessening it. When I don't use this, I have to use multiple oil-blotting sheets throughout the day. My usual routine is to use a cleanser that helps with the oil - something with salicylic acid, or lately Dermologica's Dermal Clay Cleanser, then use some witch hazel as an astringent/toner. After that I use a little bit of oil-free moisturizer, then once that's try, I put this under base on. I noticed immediately that it dries very fast. It doesn't make your skin dry, but I don't have to wait forever for it to soak in before I put on my makeup - it helps the moisturizer soak in faster too. My pores looked much smaller, and my skin felt very smooth. Like other reviewers have said, it made a very nice canvas for the makeup.
You may find yourself surprised at the size when you receive it - the canister is much smaller than you might expect, and it's metal. Depending on how much you use, you might want to go ahead and buy two, just because of how long it will take you to receive your next one. Another word of warning - you'll need a lot less than you think. When you press on the pump, you really only need to tap it; it will put out a bunch of mousse very quickly, and it's easy to get more than you need.
All in all, it's a really fantastic product, and despite the price tag it's really worth it.

title: Very strong hold, good fragrance
text:
Bought this as I was looking for a matte gel/wax, and this came up in the recommendations.

Pros:
-Awesome fragrance. It is slightly artificially fruity/floral, one might even say in a slightly feminine fashion, but seriously, smelling nice is smelling nice. It smells of traditional hair spray upon initial application, but that fades away, and the real fragrance lasts all day.
-Very strong hold. After initial styling, hair holds the style and becomes extremely stiff. The hold and texture easily lasts more than a day if needed, and is therefore predictable, and I appreciate not having to worry about re-styling if I have to do something social after work.
-After the initial application, it dries and stays dry. This is unlike wax or gels which stay sticky or wax all day, thereby attracting dust and dry skin, etc.
-Texture does not change after initial application. This is to say that after styling your hair, that texture is exactly how it'll look until the end of the day. This doesn't dry out, matte out, or fade out. Depending on how wet the hair is on application, the texture ranges from matte to taking on a slight sheen. I appreciate not having to worry about the hair looking differently at the end of the day versus when I freshly styled in the morning.
-A little bit goes a long way. I am used to using a dime-sized amount for styling with other waxes, but with this I can easily use half as much every morning, and I still feel as if I have used a bit too much.

Cons:
-Cannot re-style. After the initial application, the hair stiffens, and you are pretty much committed. There is no re-styling at mid-day. While this is a pro to me, I can understand how this may be a con to others. You will not have flexibility with the hair after the style sets.
-It's not as easy to wash off as advertised. Half of it will wash off the hands easily with just water, but then when you run your fingers together, you still feel a slight slippery film left on skin that doesn't seem to come off with soap. Good news is that after hands dry you can't feel it. It also washes out of hair with no issues.
-Like all sticky waxes, it's somewhat difficult to spread around. It's not the most difficult, but also not the easiest. It takes running the hands through the hair quite a few times to spread the product in hair until the matte residue disappears.

This is all I can think of for now. In an odd way this is unlike my previous favorite gel/wax in all aspects, but probably in a good way. I'd happily use purchase it again once my first tube runs out.

title: Nice Facial Cleaning Brush Offers Four Diverse Brush Heads but Only One Speed Option
text:
I'm very interested in trying new beauty products to pamper myself, and I have some dry skin on my face that I'm always struggling to keep in check, so it sounded appealing to give this waterproof facial brush cleaning system a try to compare and contrast to other similar products I own.

This skin cleansing kit comes with one waterproof and cordless rotating machine, one facial brush, one large body brush, one serum and moisturizer applicator sponge, and one pumice stone. This machine requires four AA batteries to run, which aren't included.

The brushes feel pleasant to the touch, and I liked that four different attachment heads were included. They are soft, but have just enough pressure to them to feel like they will exfoliate dirt, oil, and dead skin well. title: Not for frizzy hair
text:
I received this complimentary of Influenster in exchange for my honest review. As someone with wavy, frizzy hair who depends on conditioner, I definitely found pros and cons to this 2 in 1.
When I first opened it, it smelled amazing - fruity and pleasant. It lathered very well in my hair and I didn't have to use a lot. I typically only apply shampoo to my scalp when I wash, then use conditioner for detangling so I had to add a little more through my ends to detangle my hair. It rinsed out well, leaving my hair squeaky clean. It definitely lessened my shower time by not doing conditioner afterwards.
After I was out of the shower I was expecting my hair to be difficult to comb out with my wide-tooth comb but my hair was much softer than I had expected.
When drying my hair, I do the plopping method and use a table fan to air dry. As my hair was drying, I noticed my ends frizzing out as they dried. I don't get this with my shampoo and conditioner. However, my hair did dry with more volume but is more frizzy overall than usual, and definitely not what I prefer.
If you don't have frizzy hair, this would be a great option for you. Lessens shower time, smells great, gets hair clean, and leaves it soft. Still not quite moisturizing enough for wavy/curly/frizzy hair.

Immediately you can tell the quality difference in the product from the Caboodle one. The hinges that hold the compartments are tight when you try to pull them out and the case doesn't 'bow' when you push on the bottom of the case. Bottom is very solid! The compartments are lined with a piece of plastic that is sewn into the box, pretty spiffy for helping w/ spillages, although I'll probably still use plastic bags to hold my makeup. I just received this today, but will update in the future, but I'm positive this is a sturdy case and will only have good things to say!

Now, if I decide not to wear one of my nice pairs of earrings for the day, I wear these studs instead as they look nice and go with everything. text: I ordered these for a costume theme night at Indy 500. We were tailgating for 4 days in VERY hot and humid sweaty conditions, and I was throwing footballs at bowling pins all day (it's called Fowling...pronounced like "bowling" with an F). I put them on my arms after I got out of the shower with a wet hand towel soaked in cool water and wrung out a little. The whole back of the white paper must be completely soaked through for best results. Once the paper is soaked, you can gently slide off or peel the white paper. All of mine completely transfered using this method. After I gently blotted off the tattoo, I used a powder brush and translucent powder to stipple onto the tattoos. Then I gently dusted them off. Out of a total of 8 of these tattoos I aplied to my arms, the first one only started peeling seven days after they were applied, with a total of four showers and more fowling. I eventually had to remove all but one of them due to a life event I didn't want to look like a biker chick at. Old folks n' such. You get the picture. Anyway, I kept one on my right shoulder in 85% condition compared to when it was first administered, for almost three weeks. I just really babied it, washed it gently, and put powder on it. Not only are these tattoos very realistic, and last a long time, people kepts complimenting me, and asking me where I had my ink done. I really like having one on each shoulder. I have always wondered what it would look like, how people would treat me, and even if I could stand living with permenant art on my body. Now thanks to these, I'm thinking I might actually just go get me the real deal. Someday. In the mean time, it's really fun getting the street cred from these, being able to change up the look, and still have the option to go naked when I want. My only wish is that they would make even more designs!
