Before applying, use a nail file to rough up the surface of the polish and allow the remover to penetrate the polish better and have it take less time and applications.
When applying you want the thick stuff that is bumpy, not the thin polish type stuff, so mix as you can. You will also need something to scrape off the polish with (I used a cuticle pusher). It might also take more than one application depending on how thick the polish was applied.

title: Has it finally come to an end?
text:
I've been on a shampoo journey for the last few years....
I used Lush for the longest until realizing that they use Red and Yellow dyes and sulfates.
I've tried random shampoo bars off Amazon and they weren't worth remembering apparently.
I've tried the Love, Beauty, & Planet bar (it's trash and smells awful).
Then I tried Wombar from Ethique, I'm not going to say for certain that it was due to their bar because I can't prove it, but after using this shampoo bar I was losing massive amounts of hair....oddly enough. Also this on made my ends super fried/dry.
Recently I resorted to boiling soapnut berries but it wasn't cost effective considering the sheer volume of hair I have. (My hair down my back, coarse, thich, loads of hair, and dry).

Now I'm here.
And I think my journey is over.

Just with one wash I could tell the difference, after two washes total I was shocked. My once fried hair is SO soft and even looks healthier (allegedly what my kids claim). I got the lavender and pachouli one for damaged hair and it's awesome. Next I plan on getting the Cedarwood one for my wavy hair.

I highly recommend this bar.

title: Not a big "product" user, but I like this a lot
text:
I find it slightly hilarious that the box instructions for using this on hair say something like "apply from middle of strand to end." Given how short my hair is, application is kind of an all-or-nothing affair. I'm finding that about a quarter-pump, or even slightly less, is a great amount for keeping hair neat and under control without looking like I got into either my dad's Brylcreem or my son's "sculpting gel" (disclosure: Dad didn't use Brylcreem, and I don't have a son). I've also used this as a beard-treatment, and while my beard again might be too short to get the full "nourishing" benefit, it does at least smell nice.

And finally, I also use this as a moisturizer from time to time. Obviously — since it's an oil — it will leave a more "oily" feeling on the skin than the moisturizing lotions I currently use from Dove or Aveeno. When once again used sparingly, though, this oiliness is noticeable only to the touch, not to sight. And again, it does smell nice.

I don't use this on either hair or skin on a daily basis. More like a couple of times a week. So think even a two-ounce bottle will probably last me for some time. Given what a nice and versatile treat this has turned out to be — particularly for keeping hair under control when needed — that makes the price much more palatable than it would be if I was burning through this quickly.

title: Nice Smelling All Natural Soap With No Filmy Residue
text:
I switched over to natural soaps a few years back to get away from all the chemicals our corporations drown us in. I've found that most natural soaps are very good, it's the rare one that I don't like, just the fact that they are made with good ingredients makes the majority of the difference. I am never averse to trying a new product in this area so when I was offered a discount coupon to test this product in return for an honest review I was happy to do so.

At 5.5 ounces the soap is a decent size and priced correctly compared to competition. The packaging is pretty nice, although not a reason for me to purchase things but if you are giving it to someone as a gift or to try out it will make them comfortable knowing that this is not a cheap product. The fragrance was a very nice lavender smell that is not too strong and slightly different than other soaps because of the addition of Chamomile Calendula to it. From my standpoint I like the fact that the smell is not too overpowering, I'd rather not smell all flowery from afar. I've got pretty dry and sensitive skin, and after a few uses I have noticed that it does help keep my skin moist, along with the Argan Oil I use.

Washing with this soap was easy, it lathers up well and does not leave any filmy residue that takes work to wash off.

I'm very happy with this product and will most likely purchase again.

text:
I recently moved into a new home with a big master tub after having lived in a rental that didn’t have a bathtub! Gasp. I know it was torture for the two years that we lived there.

On top of that I had a high risk pregnancy where I needed to avoid baths and then I had a csection so I need to heal completely before a bath.

Fast forward to now, I can take a bath….FINALLY.
And I will be taking a righteous bath at that which meant bubbles, hot hot hot water, candles, and of course a bath pillow to fully relax.

Here’s the features I like about this pillow.
Price. It’s affordable. I didn’t want to spend too much and there was no need. This was a good price.
Size. This will fit even the largest of heads. Some pillows are so small that it’s like, why even bother.
Comfort. The two section system allows for the placement to be right where the bathtub starts to curve up so that both your upper back, lower neck and head can utilize the pillow. This is flat and has a rise of about one and half inches which is just enough to get a nice cushion in between yourself and the bathtub.
Suction cups. These are powerful and I didn’t really even have to push down. They just want to stick almost immediately when placed in my bathtub. With five suction cups placed throughout the pillow there’s no way this is going to slip.

Overall this is a comfortable affordable pillow.

title: I just received this product today and as of right ...
text:
I just received this product today and as of right now I'm hopeful, so this'll be a two part review and in 14 days I hope to report results with pictures. Upon opening the box was damaged, but don't worry because the product is within a sealed silver envelope. As long as that seal isn't broken then there's no problem. There is a slight odor to the product as well, nothing harsh but kinda doctor office exam room in smell. As I've said, I'm hopeful because upon taking off one of the booties a few flakes of skin came off.

LONG OVER DUE REVIEW

Overall I'm satisfied with my result. I had EXTREMELY calloused feet from working in boots on solid concrete for years and not taking proper care (pedicures). With that being said, the amount of dead skin that peeled away was amazing. My feet are soft! I STILL have some callouses right below my tools and a bit on the heels, but compared to what was there before its way more manageable. This isn't a miracle one trick cure all for people with extremely calloused feet, but its a great jumping off point to manage your feet. I will be buying a second peel in the next 2-4mos!

Also, yes, there is a LOT of peeling of dead skin. You can wear normal shoes/socks throughout the peeling process and the more you move around the more your feet peel. If you share a shower with someone I suggest showering last an wearing flip flops and cleaning behind yourself cause skin will come off in water.

title: It only made my hair a little softer....
text:
I bought this at Sally Beauty. I am caucasion, in my 50's with blonde/gray fine hair that is straight with some body & has never been colored or bleached; length is 2" below my shoulders.
My hair has been very dry for a long time despite lots of moisturizing, a salon keratin treatment (cha-ching!), argon oil, deep conditioning, etc... This Aphogee two-step protein treatment was recommended to me at the Sally Beauty store, and I figured it was worth a try. I followed the instructions to a T & also watched lots of youtube videos. I used this today exactly as directed & with high hopes. I shampooed & towel-dried my hair, then applied protein treatment, blow dried my hair for 12 minutes w/ the protein treatment in it, then rinsed in shower with warm water followed by the balancing moisturizer for at least 2 minutes, rinsed & used a moisturizing hair mask ("Mystic Divine" Coconut Complex Hydrating Masque), then rinsed again. My hair felt softer, at first, but my frizzies & curly gray hairs are still sticking out all over. I didn't get any more body in my hair either (my keratin treatment was last year 2017). So, all in all it is okay as a moisturizer, but no better than a regular deep moisture conditioner or mask. I'm not sure if I would use it again, maybe. I'm glad I just got the sampler size.
Here are my tips:
1) Use a spray mister bottle for the protein liquid & make sure you get out every last drop from the packet because most of it came out as beer colored water, then at the bottom of the packet was more of a thick cream, so I shook them together in the spray bottle & I'm so glad I used that! Don't just pour it on your head, at the very least pour a little into your hands at a time (after massaging the packet to mix contents) and smooth through your hair that way. There was just enough for my hair length.
2) Don't put a towel or anything around your shoulders, no clothing either because the protein treatment will dry your hair to it. Don't pull your stuck hairs off your skin, they'll come unattached in the shower, no worries. I kept my hair behind me to apply treatment & blow dry.
3) After drying the protein into your hair, don't touch your hair or bend it, (you can very gently touch lightly with your finger, if you hair wasn't already super brittle; it will feel like plastic sort of. 4) Be very careful blow-drying; I pointed the dryer downward alternating between medium & high heat & kept it farther from my hair so it wasn't blowing it around as it hardened. When hair is totally hard & dried through then gently let the shower water fall over all of your hair until you feel no more stiffness, then you can condition.
It's worth a try! The packets were just under $4 at Sally Beauty if you want to try it, or order here on Amazon.

title: DOES NOT CONTAIN HYALURONIC ACID The box and listing description are lying
text:
One of those annoying scam products.... This product states in the listing description and in the actual box front that it contains hyaluronic acid. When you read the ingredients though, it doesn't list it. Instead it lists propylene glycol and glycerin, two cheap clear viscous liquids that look and feel like hyaluronic acid but do not have the same effect on skin.
And if they're lying about the hyaluronic acid, what are the odds that they are being honest that it's 30% vitamin C? Well it lists ascorbic acid as fifth in the list of ingredients. Per law, ingredients are listed in the order of quantity in the product. If vitamin C is fifth in the list, it would mean there are four other ingredients that have more quantity. But if you do the math that's impossible. If all first four ingredients were also 30%, that would add up to 120% of the product, not counting the vitamin C. That is physically impossible.
Not worth the $5.

text: I have tried using soooo many different products to fill in/obscure a deeply indented scar in my cheek. While Dermaflage is a good product, its application process is way too labor intensive for this low-maintenance gal. And most creams don't work well when filling in such a deep scar, as they don't set up solidly. Finally--success with this Ben Nye product!! First, I apply some Aveeno Baby lotion around the perimeter of the scar area. Next, I put some lotion on a little flat-head "tool" (not included) that I use to scoop out a small amount of wax and fill in the indentation. Finally, I put a small amount of lotion on my forefinger and smooth out the edges (if any) of wax extending past the indented area. Luckily the shade of wax I chose matches my complexion almost perfectly, so I don't even have to wear makeup over it. Totally awesome.

title: Simply Outstanding!
text:
As an experienced wet shaver for many years, I have an extensive collection of razors ranging from very inexpensive to those costing hundreds of dollars.
I bought this ACEVIVI, as a friend recommended it. I really didn't expect much at this price point and thought if nothing else I would reuse the handle. What a pleasant surprise this razor provided.
The fit and finish of the razor is near perfect with beautiful heavy chrome plating. The head assembly is aluminum and the handle is heavy chromed steel, but the overall balance is still excellent. The 4" long handle is excellent for those who prefer long handles or who have large hands as I do. The deep but comfortable knurling on the handle is some of the best I've seen, providing an excellent grip.
The blade alignment is excellent with equal blade exposure on both sides using different brands of blades.
The razor comes with five ACEVIVI blades (which I have not yet used) in a very nice black presentation box with a heavy black high density foam insert suggesting a much more expensive razor.
The shave characteristics of this razor are excellent. One side is open comb and the other is closed comb representing the best of both worlds. I didn't note a significant difference in aggressiveness between the two sides. The razor has significant blade exposure and blade gap and is definitely an aggressive razor providing a very close shave. In spite of the blade exposure and gap, it provided an exceptionally smooth and comfortable shave.
Overall, this razor is an exceptional buy and out-shaves most high end razors costing many times more. With proper care, this razor should last a lifetime.
I would definitely recommend this razor to anyone interested in traditional wet shaving.

I have been using the other battery powered brand for over a decade, and decided to try the Sonicare Xtreme. This model cleans better, and is easier to use. Update - We have been using the Sonicare Xtreme for almost two years, and here are some tips: Clean the toothbrush head with the head pointing down under the hottest water out of the faucet. title: Great brush for short money. Perfect for travel.
text:
This sonicare operates like all the others, it just doesn't include the expensive rechargable battery and charger like the more expensive models do. Because it operates on AA batteries, the unit is susceptible to some water entry if one is careless.

It shouldn't be necessary to tell people not to get electric appliances wet, but apparantly it is. The handle should never be exposed to water. It is not submersible. The only portion of the entire device that should get wet is the brush-head. Remove the brush-head after every use, wash it thoroughly, and dry it. Wipe the handle dry. That is it. Take care of it like an electric hand mixer. You remove and clean the mixing pieces, you don't dunk the motor assembly in the sink. You wipe it clean. No water means no corrosion.

The directions clearly state that the motor assembly/handle is not water-proof. Others have found that a #33 o-ring seals the battery compartment very well. It is an excellent, inexpensive preventative solution to water entering the battery compartment.

Phillips does not include the following warning and disclaimer, but perhaps they should:

Item is not idiot proof.

title: Nice oil treatment for your nails while removing polish.

Not to mention that it stinks and can eat the finish off your furniture. I used this natural nail polish to remove OPI Cajun Shrimp polish (a bright coral color) from my toenails. I had on a basecoat, two coats of polish and a top coat. I applied a few drops directly onto the nail. It stayed on the nail without running off. I waited about five minutes and removed it with a tissue. It was a goopy mess but it did remove most of the polish. I applied another drop to finish removing the polish and some of it ran off onto my shoe. No harm done. I don't usually wear glitter polish but from experience that is hard to remove with most polish removers. I am happy that the oils in this remover work to remove polish, you just have to be patient. title: For the price and overall result - you can't beat it!
text: I will give this keratin treatment five stars. It arrived very promptly and no issues with bottle leakage. I started by washing my hair with Dawn dish detergent (as noted by another seller who provided feedback), did NOT condition and blew it completely dry. I then separated my hair into four sections and added the solution to each section separately while combing through with a fine tooth comb. I did my best to get as close to the roots as possible and saturate all strands without 'over saturating'. I chose to leave the solution in my hair and dry it immediately following the application. I dried it straight on the highest heat setting. Once this step was completed I flat ironed while going over sections 3-4 times. I did this step on a Wednesday evening and washed it out the following Saturday. It did feel a bit heavy, needed hot iron touch up each day and smelled a bit like pickles. But I found the cons totally worth it once I washed and styled my hair on Saturday. It looks and feels healthy, is FAR less susceptible to frizz and is holding up quite nicely. This is huge given that I have curly - frizzy hair AND happen to live in humid Florida. For the price and overall result - you can't beat it!

title: Looks nice and easy to use...jury’s still out on results.
text:
This thing looks very nice, and feels even nicer! It’s beautiful, and very easy to use. However, it is difficult to grip at times, especially if your hands are wet or moisturized. There are two clipped corners to allow for optimal grip location, so that is a much-appreciated design feature. Nevertheless, the smooth glass edges can make it tricky to get a consistent, sturdy grip. I wear nitrile gloves while using it, so that I feel more confident in the hold I’ve got on it, especially over a hard surface. So, keep that in mind. That being said, though, it is far more aesthetically appealing, user-friendly, and gentler than the traditional pumice stones or foot graters.

A protective storage case would be a great addition to this item. I saved all the packaging and have been placing the file back into the plastic packaging tray and then placing that tray back into the outer plastic packaging box. Something similar to a travel bar soap container or a retainer case would be perfect (slimmer, of course, to fit the file)! The storage case with drainage holes for drying would minimize the risk of breaking the file during cleaning, drying, and storing it. For the current price point, I personally think a reusable storage case should be included.

All that aside, my only real concern, and the reason for the current rating, is that my feet actually felt and looked dryer and rougher several days to a week after the first use. I realize this may be due to my own user error, as I followed the exfoliation with my usual moisturization regimen. It is reasonable to assume I should have taken extra steps to protect and care for me feet immediately following the exfoliation, as the delicate, softer skin was exposed. So, I am going to try it again, this is over-moisturizing and wearing plush socks for the few days afterward. I will update my review with my new results!

Overall, I currently recommend this foot file. I find it to be worth trying out, and is a better alternative to the more abrasive methods. I have included photos showing the packaging and tray in which I keep it stored, as well as close-ups of the smooth top size and gritty underside. Hope they help!

text:
This feels really soothing, especially around the eyes. I had a migraine with eye strain, and using this fresh from the freezer helped relax my eye muscles. The cold feels really good. Though I suppose I could freeze a spoon and use the back of that instead, the ball works well.

I like the roller ball part, but I don’t think the long, narrow shape of the tube works well. It’s too small to fit an ice cube, and I’m not going to crush ice to put in there. (I grabbed some fresh snow from outside to see if adding ice helps. ). I also wouldn’t store oils in there, because it’s not sealed, so the oil would spill if it tips over. And the long, narrow shape makes it more likely to be knocked over. The tube should be more short and squat, and should be sized to fit a standard ice cube. So I like the roller ball because it feels good around the eye area, but the tube isn’t very useful to me. I have it stored in the freezer so it will be nice and cold when I need it.

title: This is a huge confidence builder for me and my thinning hair, it just takes a little practice.
text: I purchased the light brown. I color my hair with warm tones and highlights, and it worked for me. It is a bit on the warmer side as others have noted. As with the other items I've gotten from this brand, the colors are very consistent and work for me. I use this to create fullness with my existing thinning bangs. It takes a bit of time and practice to learn how to style it and hide the full clip end in my bangs without it looking obvious (it's much fuller than my actual hair...especially comparing the small clip area to my normal scalp). I've also learned to blow dry it out to create a small amount of volume at the clip instead of it lying completely flat. If I part my hair appropriately and place the bangs a bit further back than you might expect, it looks really natural. I did cut the side pieces to be the same length as the bangs for a bit more width. I have added slight highlights to my pieces from this seller, and that has helped me match my own hair even better. Next I will be adding slightly darker roots to the pieces...more like lowlights, so that as my color grows out, it won't be so obvious that the lighter roots of the piece stick out. All in all, totally worth the money for me. My thin bangs are only getting thinner as I age, and this makes me feel more confident and less self-conscious. I will buy these again. For the price, getting a new one a couple times of year is totally worth it for me. I do wish it had two clips instead of one. It stays firmly attached without issue, but while styling, it often shifts a bit, like a pendulum because it only clips on a single point. It is a minor issue, but one I would definitely pay extra for.

text:
UPDATE (05/08/17):

After leaving my initial review, I was surprisingly contacted by the seller who offered to provide me with either a refund or a replacement cap. I wanted to find out whether the first heat cap I received may have been defective so I opted to receive replacement unit. When I received the replacement, the first thing I noticed is that it is a different (seemingly updated) model matching what is now listed here. Compared to the original unit I received, this newer version definitely has improvements. The replacement cap fits much better than the original which greatly reduces the amount of heat that escapes. It also seems that this cap produces a better amount of heat than the original one I received a few months ago. The biggest improvement over the first cap I received is that this heat cap has a built-in timer which automatically shuts off after 15, 30, or 60 minutes of use.

I'm satisfied with the replacement cap I received. Kudos to the seller (Nilmee) for going above and beyond to make sure that this customer walked away happy with his purchase.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I'm torn on this heat cap, when it comes down to it, it's just okay. I've been using it here and there over the past few months and I'm just not impressed. The heating on the cap is inconsistent -- some areas get warm while others have barely noticeable heating. My biggest gripe with the cap is that it seems to be sized either for people with large heads or with an overabundance of hair. I have a shorter hair style and I either have to pull on the chin strap or lay down while using the cap, otherwise what little heat the cap emits just escapes through gaps.

If you have short hair or have a smaller cranium, you may want to explore other options.

I will say that for her recital i will likely try out some kind of mousse or something to keep the curls longer, as they had fallen out quite a bit when she got home from school. However, her hair still looked cute, just more wavy than curly.

Took off one star for the learning curve in putting them in...i realized that if i twisted the hair near her scalp it was easier to get it in the curler. Also took off a star for durability because once the tool got caught inside the curler and ripped a hole in it but it didnt effect the result.

title: Easy to use, does a very decent job.
text:
These electronic foot files seem to be all the rage these days. I have tried doing a foot peel before, which did a really good job, but still didn't get rid of some of the tougher calluses. It's also tough to do a foot peel in the middle of summer when you're wearing sandals. I got this so that I could have something to work on those calluses at any time. This does a pretty decent job - it is easy to use, small (think about the size of an electric shaver), and painless. You don't really need to apply any pressure at all, just move it gently over the area, and it shaves off the callus in a very fine dust. If you apply too much pressure, it actually doesn't work as the file stops rotating at regular speed. The biggest issue is that the dust can be pretty messy, so I recommend doing it in the bathtub or somewhere that you can just wash everything down when you're finished. It uses a USB charger, so I'm able to leave it to charge using my phone charger on my night stand. It's not perfect and you can't expect that the calluses will come off straight away, but I found that filing then washing my feet off, and adding moisturizer, left my feet feeling soft, smooth, and vastly improved.

Note: I paid full price for this product and did not receive any discount.

*Easy to use.
*Lightweight.
*Multiple settings
*Automatic Shut Off (safety feature).
*Fast Straightening.

Cons:
*May take multiple passes on hair...
*Hair not as straight vs turning barrel straightener.
*Finish not as neat (i.e. more "flyaways")

Overall I'd give this straightener a 3.5 stars. I utilized the 380 degree setting. It got the basic job done (meaning it turned my curly 3c hair straight so I could wrap it / put it in a smooth ponytail) but it didn't give me that cornsilk straight look that my Instyler rotating barrel curler gave me.

I DID appreciate that I felt like this straightener brush was "less traumatic" to my hair as far as heat contact (since it wasn't being pressed as with traditional flat irons). I'd likely use this when I want a quick no-fuss straightening. I got it on a lightening deal so for the discount it's not so bad.

title: What you *really* need to know!!!
text:
When you buy a Norelco shaver, the shave is determined by the first digit of the model number. There's the 6xxx series, the 7xxx series, the 8xxx series, and, now, the 9xxx series. With rare exception, all models with the same the first digit in their model number use the same style of shaving heads. Within a series, you get more features as the model number gets greater (from corded to cordless to quick charge with more metering), but the shave within a series is pretty much the same.

Check each shaver's cutters, either by blowing up the picture of the shaver or by blowing up the picture of the replacement heads. The 6xxx series, like those before it, has heads with slots across the entire cutter. With later series, part of the cutter cover contains small holes rather than slots.

When my 5xxx shaver started to lose its ability to hold a charge, I decided to get "the best" and bought a 9xxx shaver. I knew that it sometimes took a few weeks for new heads to seat themselves and give an optimal shave. However, even after this break-in period, I found myself leaving the 9xxx on the dresser and grabbing the 5xxx for a much more reliable shave. This is what prompted me to take a close look at the heads and comapare them.

I can't imagine Norelco made the change to their cutter covers without extensive market testing. When I called Norelco Customer Service to tell them of my disappointment, they had me return the 9xxx for a full refund and told me that I'm not the only one who doesn't like the new heads. They also pointed out that the 6xxx series heads are the same style as the 5xxx heads.

I agree with what others say about the construction of the 6xxx shavers. However, lighter plastic casing is not always bad, as personal computers have demonstrated. More important is that the 6863XL gives me the same good shave I came to rely on from my 5xxx shaver.

title: Really cleans pores and softens skin. Removes makeup easily!
text:
I actually bought this at Walmart for about $6. I noticed it sitting beside my favorite facewash (Neutrogena Fresh Foaming Cleanser) and was intrigued. I have always suffered from blackheads and clogged pores because I LOVE wearing makeup even though makeup makes my skin unhappy.

The first time I used this, I noticed my pores were clearer and smaller. It makes sense. It is kind of like how coconut oil pulling helps clean teeth due to the oil latching onto bacteria. Clogged pores are a collection of dirt, oil and bacteria so rubbing oil into them gives them something to latch onto. I rubbed the oil onto my face for about 2 minutes and then added water to foam it up. After rinsing I actually used my regular facewash to make sure all of the oil was removed because I was nervous about going to bed with oil on my face.

I continued to use this oil to remove my makeup and cleanse my face at night but always followed with a regular facewash. Until one night I was so tired that I skipped the regular facewash and just used the oil. I woke up the next morning and my skin was soft and glowing. I didn't have a face full of zits or a weird rash like I feared and decided that perhaps just using the oil was a good thing.

Since then, on most nights, I only use the oil at night without using a facewash afterward. My skin has been looking great. Occasionally I mix the oil with my microdermabrasion crystals for a deep clean and exfoliation. It works very well with the crystals.

I highly recommend this to anyone who suffers from blackheads, dry skin and/or wears makeup regularly.

title: Ingredients identical to Dr. Bronner's liquid soap, but price is double or higher
text:
So, this product is natural and works well to clean brushes. It is a super basic soap without unwanted chemicals, which is great. However, the ingredients are pretty much identical to Dr. Bronner's Pure Castille Liquid Soap, which costs half as much or less, and does the exact same thing. Dr. B's also comes in numerous scents (all organic) and even unscented. Also, I think Dr. B's is more concentrated, so it takes less soap to clean each brush, making it even more economical.

Bottom line, this "Makeup Brush Cleansing Shampoo" is a perfectly good product, but you can get essentially the same thing for a much lower price by buying Dr. Bronner's Liquid Soap instead.

title: Ouch!
text: I used this for the first time tonight. It was not as comfortable as I would have liked it to be. If you have very sensitive skin it will probably be a painful experience, especially if you're used to a soft wash cloth. I think it may have scratched my back and sides too much because it was burning after drying off. I believe I didn't have enough soap on it initially, which created more friction than needed, so I added more soap and it was a little more tolerable. Although uncomfortable, I endured, and my face and body came out with really smooth, soft skin. After slathering on some lotion my skin feels a little better. It's always a good idea to moisturize after exfoliating. I'll probably use this twice a week. Not sure I would use this before going to bed though, my irritated skin definitely wasn't helping me fall asleep. It is a large, rectangular shape, dries quickly, feels durable, and hopefully will last a long time. I would recommend this. People with very sensitive skin might want to look for something a little softer though.

title: Not bad!
text:
So, this is my first time using this kind of product. I always shaved before (just did not like the sharp stubble afterwards and sometimes nicking myself). The product got all the hair off, but some hairs are still about 1/16" long. I think I may have left it on too long because one spot became red and raw. If you have sensitive skin I would definitely test a small area (which it tells you do anyway) before using it. I will probably reapply to the same area in several days to see if it will get rid of the short hairs that it left behind. The product is thick, easy to spread, and stays on well. Just spread it on with the provided wooden stick, wait several minutes, jump in the shower (do not use soap on the area), and wipe it off! Afterwards, you can apply the Calm Balm which really helps soothes the area. It would be nice if the bottles came in a larger size.

UPDATE: 2012-03-22 After using this product again "down there" I have realized my skin does not agree with this product (I have always had somewhat sensitive skin). Left the product on for about seven minutes and an area about 1" x 1/2" became red, raw, and bled slightly (obviously dissolving more than just the hair). Unfortunately I will not continue using it "down there." I might use it again on a less sensitive area of my body. I am keeping my four star review on it. The product still works well; I just wish my skin was not so sensitive.

title: Jade rolling and Gua Sha - ancient Chinese skincare practices
text:
This roller is much better than other low-cost rollers I've used - there's no squeaking or wiggling, just a smooth and quiet application. The products are finely made with gold colored hardware and soft pink stones, and come in a cute box with some additional goodies! (A few eye masks and a little baggie for storing the tools).

Using the roller was very intuitive and easily done, and it left my face feeling very cool and soothed. I don't have as much experience with the Gua Sha so I looked up some videos on YouTube for how to use it, and it definitely seems like an indulgent practice that I could get used to! It's basically like a home facial massage, and it left my skin feeling worked over but less bloated than it was before I used the Gua Sha.

I don't necessarily think these tools are a necessity but they are really fun, adorable, and the benefits they have are no joke! Jade rolling and Gua Sha massage are Chinese medical practices which have been shown to have beneficial effects on the skin and body, so if you've been looking for a Jade rolling set, this definitely might be the one for you!

title: Amazingly Effective De-shedding Comb, but BE GENTLE!
text:
I ordered the long sparse-teeth comb for my golden retriever. I didn’t expect this comb to be anything special and am still a bit mystified by how effective it is as a de-shedder/de-tangler. It doesn’t look like anything special, but somehow the teeth create a “drag” as you run it through thick fur. I have used lots of metal combs over the years and I have never had one that gripped the hair quite like this. My dog is combed or brushed almost daily to keep the shedding down, but look how much fur came out in 10 minutes! I’m really glad I got the sparse-teeth comb; if the teeth were denser, I don’t think it would have worked at all on thick fur. (Maybe the dense teeth would be okay for a very smooth-haired dog or cat.)

This comb needs to be used with care. The teeth are a little too sharp for my taste, so you need to use this comb gently to avoid inadvertently scraping your dog’s (or cat’s) skin — I would say a *minimum* 45-degree angle to make sure the ends of the teeth don’t make straight-on contact with the skin. Also, you need to go *slowly* so you don’t end up pulling out non-loose hair. As long as I went slowly and gently, my dog did not seem at all uncomfortable with the process, but he is probably the most patient dog in the world and is used to being groomed daily. If your dog is fidgety or you want something for quick daily combing sessions, I would suggest you try something a little less aggressive.

title: Good replacement for my 7735X
text: I picked up this razor as a replacement for my 7735x because the battery finally lost its charge after over 2 years of daily use. I think the moisturizing system on an electric razor is pure genius and I hope Norelco contiues to improve the line. Anyway, the 8060x makes many improvements over the older line but further improvements can be made. First off, this razor is relatively compact over the 7XXX line. The blades sit atop the body making the razor smaller overall but leaves the blades vulnerable to damage during travel. The lotion dispensing is now electronically actuated vs. the manual pumping you have to do with the older line. One thing that irked me was that the lotion didn't always make it to the blade or skin surface. The lotion comes through two stems coming off of the body and then through a hole in the center of the top two blades. Theoretically, the lotion should just come out onto the blades and on to the skin but while shaving the lotion leaks out to the underside of the blade where it doesn't do a whole lot of good. Maybe if you dispensed the lotion while it wasn't pressed against your face but that would add time to your shave to do that every time you needed more lotion. On to the charging and refilling stand. This is a huge advancement over the previous model. The stand not only recharges the razor but automatically refills the razor with lotion! This is much more convenient than either running out of lotion mid-shave or being out of lotion because you forgot to replace the cartridge. The bottles are $10 for less than 3 oz. Kind of pricey if you ask me and I haven't checked what $10/3 oz. would equate to vs. the cartridges. The razor charges in no time. 90 mins for a full charge and it has a quick charge mode but I never seem to let it drain completely. The razor also comes with a travel charging stand for easy carrying. You'll have to carry a bottle of the lotion to refill it manually in this case. One last thing, you do get a trimmer attachment. Just pull the blade head off and snap the trimmer on and you're good to go. I recommend this razor despite the few gripes I have about it. Nothing's perfect but this is as good as you'll get if you want a razor that dispenses lotion.

Step 5. Used a baby whip to remove all the product and then followed through with the t.n Dickinson witch hazel to get an extra clean.

title: Good but could be better
text:
This kit is just what I needed. It was a great price, too! Especially compared to having to pay out the yin yang from the dentist for whitening gel and custom whitening trays. The gel is very gentle on gums and teeth but does whiten. I would like to see more improvement per treatment but I have bad staining from not taking care of my teeth at all for 8 or so years and smoking 2 packs a day on top of it. I did quit last year though but still had massive yellow staining.

The kit comes with boil-and-bite trays which worked great for my top teeth but not so well on my bottom teeth as I have crowding in the front. But those trays were good to use while I waited for the custom trays to arrive at my doorstep. The kit also comes with 3 sets of impression material each set has blue and white material that you mix together quickly and then put in the plastic trays and you bit down on them and hold them steady for 4 minutes till it's set firm. Then you rinse the molds and mail it with the prepaid and pre-addressed envelope to ProWhite. It took exactly 2 weeks to send and receive them. I did get an email from GreenDot (the seller) saying that my trays were done and were mailed, which was nice.

The 22% carbamide peroxide that makes up the whitening gel is very gentle on gums. I've tried another product which was a generic off-brand of aquafresh white trays and it burned the HELL out of my gums. Oh it was awful, but this stuff doesn't even burn or cause any stinging which is wonderful! I leave my trays in for 30 minutes to one hour and see a noticeable difference in the whiteness of my teeth after every treatment. Not a huge difference but it is noticeable.

The custom trays could have been made better. I checked my molds and actually re-did one of them because the gum line wasn't right, wasn't clear enough in the mold material. The custom trays are not cut along the gum line but above the gum line in a straight line. I've heard that doing that helps keep the trays on your teeth better than those cut along the gum line. The trays are very flexible. The gum lines aren't perfect on the trays making me think that the person who poured the stone into the mold didn't do it well enough or something, but to be honest you get what you pay for... A price this good will have some setbacks. I did get to keep the stone molds of my teeth though. They came in the envelope with the trays on the molds. Cool.

Anyway, all in all this has been a wonderful experience. I would buy this kit again if I needed to, I highly recommend it.

text: I was really hoping this product would work and I wasn't disappointed. It's amazing how FAST it works on gel polish! In just around 2 minutes it lifts one to two layers of polish -sure beats the 20-30 minutes of soaking it off with acetone! I expect the people who didn't have any results didn't follow the cardinal rule of removing gel polish - break the top layer of polish first (with a file). If you do that, this product works just as it should. If you don't first remove that top layer of clear polish, you won't get anywhere, no matter what method you use. It even tells you to do that on the little paper included in the box. I expect the people who didn't have results didn't do their do diligence and read the paper. By the time I remove my gel polish I normally have 5 or more coats on, so I use this product two times to get most of the polish off and then gently file off the rest. It's great when you just need to repair one or two nails and take off the polish completely. Makes the repair very fast and easy. I will definitely continue to buy this product to remove my gel polish from now on.

The item is not worth getting. The first 2-3 shaves were okay but after that, it takes foreverrrrrr to trim your head. My traditional foil shaver (the ones with two sets of parallel foils) actually trimmed my head faster. But even then, that took a long time. I really only got this device because I wanted to avoid the bloody mess of shaving with a razor.

Here's the truth... there is really no device that can provide short-cuts or easier methods when it comes shaving your head bald. Nothing will ever beat the results of a traditional straight edge, or double edge razor. I would suggest investing some time to practice the art of shaving with a straight edge, single edge, or double edge razor. Over time, you will actually learn techniques to shave your head faster.

title: Terrific shave soap and the scent is very light. Leaves your face feeling soft and hydrated.
text:
Many shave products have really strong scents. This soap has a lovely scent that is very light and neutral.

With other shave soaps I usually need some sort of moisturizer or balm after shaving but with this soap my face feel soft and hydrated after the shave with no need for any post shave products.

Some people have trouble getting it to lather - perhaps they are used to a softer soap or cream - this is a hard soap puck and you'd have to scrub it with a wet brush for a few minutes before the surface softens enough to start lathering. some people soak the puck in water to soften but my method is to leave the hard soap puck in it's original state and store it separately -- I simply scrape or cut a few flakes into a lathering bowl or mug and compress the flakes with finger or thumb and a few drops of warm water to stick the flakes to the bottom of the bowl. Then I get a ton of thick, creamy lather and the flakes remain stuck to the bottom of the mug for several more shaves until I need to carve a few more flakes from the hard soap puck to replenish the mug.

title: Great scent, great lather. And a great price (at WallyWorld).
text:
Palmer's/E.T. Browne has a lot of above-average products in its line. This is one of them, for sure.

The scent is scrumptious. Not much like "coconut sun-tan oil at the beach" … much more like "fresh coconut cream pie desert!"

I say above-average because, if you scour the ingredient list on Palmer's products, you will typically find SOME natural & luxurious ingredients … and also some fairly common chemicals. So many of their products are of a higher quality than common store-shelf items … but not exactly in the category of seriously premium and/or upscale products.

For example, this product's main ingredient is Sodium olefin sulfonate. That's a common ingredient in bath & body products that used to make them lather. And Palmer's has been very generous with it, in that this shampoo really REALLY lathers up! The next major ingredient is coconut fruit extract. Many manufacturers won't use coconut oils or extracts in their bath & body products because straight-up palm oils and extracts are cheaper. After that there's a list of many other common chemical sounding ingredients. But also there's coconut oil, Tahitian gardenia extract, keratin-protein and glycerin. Those too are premium ingredients that common bath & body products usually won't contain. And this shampoo contains NO sulfates, parabens, mineral oil, dyes, gluten or phthalates.

That's a lot of quality, given the price … that being $4.36 at WallyWorld for a 14 ounce bottle… and, as of this writing, with instant "$2 off" coupons attached. That's a lot less expensive than other "big brand name" shampoos that offer less and cost more.

There's also a matching body wash product. In use, and in the ingredient list, they are almost exactly the same product. And there's a matching bar soap, though I found it far less interesting - meh - than this shampoo and its matching body wash.

This shampoo seems far better suited for dry hair; it conditions, moisturizes and protects. But I have oily hair. So I sometimes resort to using my bar soap on my hair as a first pass, to "cut through" a lot of the oil, before actually using this shampoo as a second application.

In any case, for a mere $2.36, you can pick up a bottle of this stuff at WallyWorld and see how this shampoo suits you yourself.

title: Buyer beware. SheaMoisture products, once high-quality, now made of cheaper, common ingredients.
text:
In late 2016, SheaMoisture intentionally started changing up the formulas in all of its products … for the worse. For example, all the new soap bar formulas have palm oil as their primary ingredient, making them basically no different from most other bar soaps ... except the REALLY cheap bar soaps (like those on grocery store shelves) that use "tallowate" – animal fat – as the primary ingredient.

I uploaded a picture of the old ingredients (in their Coconut & Hibiscus bar soap). The primary ingredients: coconut oil, coconut milk, papaya, vanilla beans, shea butter, cocoa butter, mushroom extract, Vitamin E, hibiscus. Little wonder I once found this bar soap on a beauty magazine's list of five best bar soaps.

Here's WHY they did it. In late 2015, Bain Capital, a venture capital firm, invested in SheaMoisture. SheaMoisture, being a privately-held company, must have "invited in" Bain … almost certainly to help them find a buyer for the SheaMoisture company. Bain makes its money when the company is sold, getting back more (for the percentage of the SheaMoisture company they bought) than what they paid to get it in the first place. At that point, neither Bain nor SheaMoisture had any further interest in the long-term outcomes & condition of the SheaMoisture company, the quality of SheaMoisture products or the integrity of the SheaMoisture customer base. They were "in it to flip it."

They cheapened the product costs with lousy formulas in order to improve the financial statements that would make the SheaMoisture company more attractive to potential buyers. Ruining their products, losing the customer base they built over many years, entirely irrelevant. And that's exactly how it played out. In late 2017 SheaMoisture was bought up by Unilever, turning a tidy profit for Bain off its very short-term investment (less than two years) … and nicely cashing-out the original owners of SheaMoisture … so they can go live in Bali or Monaco or somewhere.

Unilever's interest is easy to guess. SheaMoisture was successfully breaking away from its roots as a ethnic product line and was becoming recognized as a higher quality product in the mainstream market. So the SheaMoisture brand image is valuable to a high-volume mass marketer like Unilever. This is the same kind of story as with Burt's Bees; most people still think BB is some kind of specialty craft/upscale product as it once was, not having the least idea that these days it is nothing more than a brand name owned by the Clorox corporation.

To be fair a lot of Unilever products are of somewhat better quality than the product against which they directly complete. Still, Unilever is high-volume, so they won't ever be able to return to the more expensive, much higher quality formulas that SheaMoisture once used.

As my stock of classic SheaMoisture bar soaps winds down, I am still searching for a high-quality replacement bar soap … that doesn't cost a small fortune. One of the better choices at this point seems to be the "Out of Africa" bar soaps; they are one of the few bar soaps left that do not contain palm oil as the primary ingredient, instead they contain about 20% shea butter.

text:
I really wanted to love this product. I never grew up femme, so the chance to get a cheap starter/sample kit was perfect for me.

Pros: I got the package on time. Everything was in it and in good condition. I was so excited that I rushed to do all the steps to prepare my face for makeup application. I used a primer and everything. Anyway, I love love love the foundation. Both seemed off on my skin, but the package comes with two different shades. I was too dark for the fair but too fair for the darker shade, so I slowly mixed them in a larger jar until I found a great match. It's the best match I've found in my limited experience. It also didn't irritate my sensitive skin which is a huge plus. The concealer worked really well. Nothing looked super caked on, which is a problem I've dealt with due to having a lot of peach fuzz on my face. It looked very natural when I found the right combination. Finding that combination was one of the best parts for me.

Cons: After a lot of research and frustration, I found out why I didn't love this kit: all the eyeshadows, blush, and bronzer/'warmth' shimmer. I have super hooded eyes and (apparently) that's why none of them looked good on me. Shimmer makes hooded eyes appear more hooded. The blush and bronzer both attracted too much light due to the shimmer, making the makeup appear more obvious and less natural. Also, the bronzer/warmth is far too dark for my skin fair tone. I got the lightest one available, so that's kinda weird.

I would buy the concealer and foundations again if I get the urge to be girly after this stuff runs out. I won't buy the rest. All in all, I got a refund. I didn't want to be stuck with a kit where I only liked 30% of the makeup.

title: Works but has its limits
text:
prior to salerm i used the color oops which totally backfired, turning my roots orange [my dyed hair is a dark dark brown with auburn and violet tones and i've been dying my hair dark for over 10 years - dying/highlighting for over 20 years], despite following the directions to the letter. But this stuff, fixed the orange and stripped the dark [almost black but not quite] from the bottom up and fixed the orange somehow. I will have to use a second time after a week or so as stripping your hair is a process, especially of dark colors or red/violets, and it takes many rinses - each time i rinse more comes out slowly but surely. You must be patient especially if you've been coloring for a decade or more and nothing will restore you to your original color if youre using permanent dye and semi-permanent dye - you need to grow your hair out to get to your original color. My goal was to lighten so I could go to a lighter shade, which I refuse to bleach my hair as its not worth the damage, NOT restore it to my orignal shade as that is impossible due to the way the oxidation process of dye on hair follicles.
This is what I did besides following the directions;
1. Mix eq. parts as directed & apply quickly (it's a gel so its much easier and you get a lot out of it but if you have very thick long hair it would be safer to go with two boxes)
- it does stink but nowhere near as badly as color oops which lingered in my hair which was gross - if you rinse and shampoo as I did there's no lingering scent
2. Apply a cap (doesn't come with) but also it helps to throw a towel in the dryer to heat up and then wrap over the cap. heat activates it and makes it work better.
3. Leave in for 20 minutes (some people say they've left it on longer but I have healthy hair and i try to protect it so i didn't want to chance it - I may leave it in longer next time, however).
4. Rinse hair first in shower thoroughly and apply shampoo (no conditioner - not yet) than rinse for 20minutes the first time. IMPORTANT - use a crappy shampoo - the stuff that costs $5 with parabans (etc. the crappy stuff)
- Apply shampoo (the crappy stuff again) again & rinse for 5 minutes.
- Shampoo one more time (yes, still the crappy one), rinse for 5 minutes apply conditioner (I used a nexus keratin conditioner mixed with a deep conditioner treatment) and rinse for 5 minutes (last time!).
It's boring and a process but it pays off! Your hair will thank you if you use a nice conditioning treatment (I used a garnier papaya treatment mixed with my nexus keratin conditioner).

I'd also say keep using the crappy shampoo as it helps strip that color! DONT BOTHER WITH COLOR OOPS - it's cheap and terrible! This stuff doesn't hurt your scalp either and the smell doesn't linger the way i re-shampoo-ed and rinsed repeatedly (which helps the stripping process as well). RINSE RINSE RINSE!

title: An Efile Worth Having
text:
I wasn't sure about getting an efile in the beginning that was rechargeable but the battery life of this thing is phenomenal. I've used it for three complete manicures and a few extra times one week to fix a nail that was being difficult, and the battery still has a 75% charge remaining. I combine dip powder with UV gel which is hard to soak off so I remove as many layers as I can with an efile before soaking, that alone takes 30 minutes to 1 hour.

As you can see in the first two photos there is a digital dial that shows the speed that the file is set on, a feature I never knew I needed. My previous efile had multiple speeds but you kind of had to adjust it as you went. The advantage of having a digital dial is that you can start your work at the correct speed without the need to manually adjust it back and forth.

I was aware that this efile had a higher rpm max than what I was using when I purchased it. How slow the slow speeds are is a surprise though. Speed 01 in the first photo is perfect for the cuticles. With a gentle enough bit it's slow enough to actually touch the cuticles. I dial it up closer to 05 when doing cleanup around the cuticles, or when I want to slightly rough up the. surface with a sanding band but not really buff it.

Then there is the third photo; I'm so happy to see a lock/unlock means of securing the bits. With so many efiles including my previous one you secure the bit by simply pushing it in, sounds simple but if it's not pushed in far enough it can wobble or fly out during operation and cause injury. After pushing shorter bits in as far as they need to go there can be little length left to work with and can be hard to remove. I literally bought a small pair of pliers solely for the purpose of pulling small cuticle bits from the efile I was previously using.

My previous efile was a OK as a beginner efile but I'm glad I was able to make the upgrade.

I was so upset with myself for possibly buying the wrong bottles and I was about to send them back without even trying them. Then I watch a reviewers video and read other review and decided to try the bottles myself. I filled one with a thick oil mixture and the other with alcohol (because ya know, covid and all). Both the spray bottle and the pump worked!! I was so excited. I used to keep my oil mixture in a dropper bottle that was so messy but now with this pump it so much easier. I’m going to place a second order so I can have an extra set.

I’m so glad I tried them. In order for the bottles to work both the pump and stay, they need to be filled to the top so the product can be sucked into the tiny spout. title: Cleansing without dryness...
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect from this facial wash, when I got it. It's labeled a wash, but the instructions state that it is to be used after cleansing. For my sanity's sake, I just assumed it was mislabeled, and used it as a regular wash. It appears I was correct.

It's clear, which is always nice, for me. I have eczema, and the more natural the ingredients, the better. I was concerned that this wash contains alcohol, but there must not be much, since my skin hasn't freaked out.

This wash lathers quite nicely. It rinses off quickly and cleanly. Despite its oil content, it doesn't leave my skin feeling greasy. Despite the alcohol, I'm not left with any dryness or tightness. It leaves my skin feeling soft and smooth.

What's most impressive is how long the softness lasts. It's been a hot summer, and I recently changed my regimen, so I only moisturize at night. In the morning, I just wash and go. The moisture in this wash is plenty, and my skin stays supple, with no flakiness. If your skin is sensitive to alcohol, I'd still recommend giving this wash a try; it seems to be a blend that works really well, with no irritation.

title: Works well, but detailed instructions would have been helpful...
text:
For me, this little nail drill works very well. It's touted as being good for beginners, but I was really nervous about using it for the first time, because it came with absolutely no instructions. Yikes! I'd cut my nails down to nubbins, and have been wearing falsies, so I figured it was a great way to get some practice.

There are a few notes on the product listing about how to insert and remove the drill bits, so with that being all I had to go on, I just went for it.

As I had no clue as to which bits were for what job, I had to wing it. I tried two. The first I tried wasn't quite coarse enough, so I went with the larger, barrel-shaped bit, which worked well for what I wanted. I'd basically put on some stiletto tips, and managed to jab every family member at least once. I didn't want to completely remove them, but I wanted to take them down a bit and round out the tips. Once I changed the bit this drill did a great job.

It got a little warm, but didn't get too hot, and it didn't overheat and stop on me. In my photo is what they looked like right after I was done. I did go over the edges briefly with an emery board for the couple of rough spots left, simply because I'm not yet quite adept enough to get the perfect shaping I want, but practice is key.

It's for the same reason that I haven't yet tried the drill on my natural nails. I will, though, once I get a little more know-how under my belt. So, in summary, I like it, and it seems to be beginner-friendly, but I wish there were detailed information available on its use.

I received this nail drill free to try in exchange for my evaluation and unbiased review. Any opinion I've expressed is purely mine and based on my own personal experience using this drill.

title: A tasty alternative to table salt...
text: I like that this salt contains additional minerals and other nutrients I need. About ten years ago, I stopped using salt at the table. Because of a family history of hypertension, I wanted to start lowering my sodium intake, and just start a few healthier eating habits, in general. I used to sit at the table and sprinkle salt on my food before I'd even tasted it, and I just thought it was a terribly unhealthy habit and that it was time for a change. I'm not sure of all its health benefits of this pink Himalayan salt, or how significant they are, but I like the flavor. The kid in me loves the pretty pink color, and while I know, rationally, that it has no bearing on the flavor, I can't help but enjoy the way it looks in the shaker, with its grains of different shades. I tasted a bit upon opening the bag. To me, it doesn't have as strong a salty taste as regular table salt does, and it dissipates more rapidly on the tongue. In use with cooking, I also feel it's not as salty as my normal variety. It does a great job of allowing my other spices to do the work, and the seasoning blends I use can be better appreciated. I've also found that if I accidentally get a bit heavy-handed with this salt, it's more forgiving, since it's not as salty. Overall, I'm enjoying the way it looks and tastes, and my next experiment will be making my own body scrub. I was able to purchase this Himalayan pink salt at a discounted rate in exchange for my evaluation and unbiased review.

title: Nice brush if your dog has fairly easy to comb fur
text:
[[VIDEOID:d8c4188c3a8b20cec0a8f90c9a1aa483]] So, this is a dog brush with a gimmick. Namely, it has a little push button on the back to clear the fur from the comb. The attached video shows you how it works.

I have a Cavachon (a cross between a Bichon and a Cavalier) which has hair, not fur. The hair is fairly fine and as it grows long, it tangles. The longer it gets, the more snarls it gets so we thought this brush would be great to make picking the fine hair clumps out much easier.

The Good:
1) The push-button cleaner actually does a good job, it lifts the back above the bristles and you can whisk away the trapped hair with your fingers.
2) The soft rubber tips on the end of the bristles are a lot less "poke-y" than metal bristles that are just cut wire.
3) The rubber handle is easy to grip and does not slip in your hand.
4) After just one brushing, my dog's hair is super soft, so it seems to work.

The Bad:
1) This is a pretty expensive brush to be as flexible as it is. The brush always feels like it is just about to break when I pull on snarl. There is no piece of metal or wood in the handle, and it is super flexible to the point that it feels kinda cheaply made. Without stiffness in the handle, you don't get much leverage on the tangles, so it seems to pull more on the hair rather than pulling through the hairball. I seemed to have to tug on it more, which might cause more discomfort to the dog than my wooden handle brush.
2) I don't really need to clean my brush that often, so having to pull out the hair in my old brush just wasn't that hard. I am more comfortable with my stiffer wooden brush with similar teeth for less $$$

The Ugly:
1) After the second brushing, a wire got bent to the point that when I used the cleaning thingee, the bristle got stuck beneath the cleaning thing and bent even worse as the cleaning thing retracted. I figure after several uses, there is a good chance that the cleaning gimmick will be useless.

Overall rating: B- I really wanted to love this brush. All the sadder that it failed to live up to my hopes. However, if you have a dog with fairly straight fur that sheds a lot but doesn't get too tangled, this might just be the perfect brush for you.

title: Pretty good mild cleanser, but not a one-and-done type product.
text:
I have been using this Isabel Fay deep cleansing rose hip seed facial cleanser gel for over a month now, and I do like it quite a bit. I love the minimal ingredient list (Purified Water (Aqua), Sodium Olivate, Glycerin, Rosa Rubiginosa (Rose Hip) Seed Oil, Eriobotrya, Japonica Extract, Chondrus Crispus (Seaweed) Extract).

This product seems to be all around quite mild. The scent is lightly floral, not overly pleasant or unpleasant, not too strong and doesn’t linger. The lather is present but not super foamy. Most importantly for me, the product has not CAUSED any irritation. I have really sensitive skin, and I have not noticed any additional drying or breakouts due to using this product. However, I also haven’t noticed any particularly hydrating or clearing effects either. My skin does feel rather smooth and fresh since using this wash, but I find that I still need several other facial products to achieve this.

I was a bit concerned with the directions stating to avoid the eye area, because many of the healthy-skin and anti-aging benefits of the ingredients in this product would be ideal for the eye area, and I was initially hoping to use this as a make-up removing cleanser. However, I adhered to the directions, and I do not use this as a make-up removing cleanser, and only use it following or prior to make-up removal/application. The good news is, while I don’t directly put this product on my eyes, I am not super careful about avoiding the eye area while rinsing and I have not experienced any stinging or eye discomfort as I have with several similar products in the past.

Overall, I found this to be a pretty good product, I like it quite a bit but I didn’t find it to be a particularly extraordinary product either. I do recommend this product to others as a part of their beauty regimen, but I definitely need (and recommend others) to use a make-up remover prior to use, and a moisturizer following use, so this isn’t a one-and-done type product.

title: I really like this unit
text:
I have been wearing crochet braids as a protective style for a few years now. However, while I love the versatility I get with crochets, without damaging my hair, re-installing the braids over the weekend became a bit of a time suck. I decided to look for a wig that would serve as a transitional piece, that would look natural and still afford my own natural hair protection be allowing me to keep my hands out of it.

Enter this wig. I had never worn a wig before, though I had bought a few, which looked a bit fake, so I to tuck them in a closet. I even bought the half wig version of this unit, but it was too much of a hassle to get my hair to blend with that wig's texture. So when I saw this full wig on offer, I got a bit excited. I watched a lot of Youtube tutorials and reviews before taking the plunge to purchase it. All the while skeptical that it would look as good a reviewers said it does.

As I said, this was my first time really trying a wig. I am such a wig novice that I had the wig on wrong when I first tried it on, without realising where the part was, and was not really impressed. However, once I put it on correctly, I saw it had serious potential. The left side part was a bit odd, but I quickly overcame that once I tweezed it a little bit and cut a few strands to create the coveted "baby hairs" to blend with my own. Then I applied some concealer and powder to the part, so it more closely matched my own scalp and voila, a wig that is so fabu, that I want to buy a second one as a stand by.

The texture is natural looking. Like I blew out my own hair and then put some flexi rods in to create large spiral curls. I chose not to mess with the curls too much because I want to avoid tangles and matting. I figure the curls will loosen up with time. The wig is lightweight, yet the hair is thick enough that you never see the cap beneath. It really looks like my own hair, like it is growing straight from my scalp. I love it. I just added some more hair pins to secure it a bit more, but I am happy with it. It was a great price and a good experience for this first timer.

title: I bought this why...?
text:
The only reason this razor works--and the only reason I rated it with even 3 stars--is because it's a Venus razor. Venus razors work excellently, so when this new version came out I was excited to try it. I've owned mine for over a year now, and was unimpressed with it from the moment I started using it.

The vibrations are useless; I get the same quality shave whether it's turned on or off. The battery lasted quite a long time, but as soon as I replaced it the razor stopped working properly (not that it mattered, since it didn't do anything in the first place). So not only do we have a "power" razor that has no power, but the company decided to charge even more for replacement razor cartridges. I thought I had to use the corresponding cartridges, but finally I inserted one of the old Venus cartridge heads and it worked exactly the same.

I don't know--maybe I'm just a no-fuss girl who really doesn't notice subtle differences in the quality of leg-shaving. I would recommend Venus brand razors in a heartbeat, but I do NOT recommend this particular version.

I have used this in making Poo-pourri, bath bombs, shampoo, lotion, air freshener, glass cleaner, kitchen cleaner, toilet bombs, body wash, hand soap and basically anything I've had to use essential oils, water and oil in. I was a little nervous at first because I wasn't sure exactly how to use it, or how much to use because it doesn't come with any instructions. I ended up doing some research and found that most people use 1%, so in a recipe that weighs a pound or 16oz. I would use 5ml of the polysorbate (I think). However, I personally would just "eyeball" it, and if things wouldn't mix together I would add a little more until things would mix and stay together, and a little goes a long way. I am so glad to have found this stuff and will be sure to always have it on hand. I know that since using this, my lotions have stayed together without separating and so have my shampoos which is a big plus for me. I also use Optiphen Plus to keep any bacteria from forming since I use water in a lot of my recipes, and the Optiphen Plus and now Polysobate have now become staples in my homemade bath and body recipes.

text: I kept hearing about the original, but could not find it anywhere in a color I wanted (black or red). Saw this as a well reviewed alternative, and figured I'd give it a try. I use mine either with a pre-poo concoction before I conditioner wash or during my first conditioner wash. Pre-COVID I had a strict weekly hair washing routine, but that has somewhat fallen by the wayside, and I now definitely have more shed hair between stress and not weekly washing. But...this gets it all out, no matter what. No random hairs still dangling after the wash, after the conditioner, as you move to preparing to style. Gone. I feel like it gets all the shed hair out, allowing me to actually clean and condition my hair even more directly. By the time I get to moisturizing and styling, there is no hair all over my shirt or skin. I also use the brush to make sure that my products are fully distributed, root to tip. The only "downside" is the back bar that I think is supposed to give it structure. It attaches easily, but sometimes by the time I get the entire head detangled, its come off. I don't have a problem with the brush alone, and for my bra strap length, 3b/3c hair, we aren't getting caught or any snatching. Get the brush. My sister stole my second one, and uses it for basic detangling, product distribution and re-twisting her 3c/4a/4b hair midweek. Get the brush.

title: Electrolysis ain't easy but it works
text:
I'm giving this product a five star review because it actually does work. It might not be working consistently or easily for many users because electrolysis is actually pretty hard to do. That's why there are professionals who do it full time as a job. This product uses galvanic electrolysis. There are two other types that professional users and equipment can do. However if people are patient and follow through with good technique they will get good results eventually. And electrolysis is the ONLY permanent method of hair removal that you can do on your own. Anything else, however easy and painless, is just a temporary fix. So the product should not be judged by how difficult it is to use, but by the permanence of the results.
-Hair grows in three phases. Electrolysis only works best in the initial growing phase and sometimes works in the intermediate phase. It will not work in the final, dormant stage because the root, which electrolysis kills, is not active. An easy way to make sure you are only spending time on hairs in the growing phases is to shave an area and wait a few days. The hairs that poke up are growing.
-It only makes sense to do electrolysis on terminal hairs. Those are the dark, coarse hairs. Vellus hairs, the light and fine ones, are not that compatible with electrolysis because the holes they grow out of are small like the hairs themselves and aren't very easy to thread the needle in to all the way. There's also a risk of scarring. So don't go nuts. Just focus on the terminal hairs.
-Electrolysis kills hair roots through a combination of heat and a corrosive, lye-like substance that results from the electric charge coming in to contact with biological cells. That white, yucky substance that people are complaining about? that's the "lye". Don't wipe it off and don't pluck the hairs right away. You want to let them soak in it a while and die. I treat a hair and then go brush my teeth or water the plants before I pluck the hair. The "lye" needs a few minutes to do the job of killing the hair root.
-You need to actually make contact with all of the root area and the sides at the follicle base to kill it. A hair root is sort of an elongated sheath shape not a little pin dot. If any cells survive it regenerates from the surviving cells. It's a good idea to sort of plunge the needle in and out very, very gently or jiggle it a bit side to side while treating a hair. This increases the area the electricity comes in contact with and improves the odds of killing all the root. It's better than holding the needle perfectly still.
-If you've killed the root the hair will slide out without any tugging and will feel almost "greasy". If you need any force to pull it out it's not dead and you should leave the hair in and wait a few days and try again.
-As you might be able to tell from my comments this is a pretty tricky process and the odds are against you. You need to hit the root perfectly, kill the whole root area and get it in the early phases of growth. I think electrolysis only really works well for targeting a few "crazy" hairs growing in weird spots. It's not that great for clearing large areas. Doing it requires focus and precision. And also a bit of luck. I had a half dozen weird hairs and I've used this product to kill them and am rid of them forever. For that, I consider it priceless. But if you are aiming to use it to clear large areas it's likely it will be a source of frustration. Even for professionals, with professional grade equipment and years of experience, clearing a large area takes months and months of detail oriented work.
