The Dr. Oz Show demonstrating the benefits of Tamanu Oil. Dr. Mehmet Oz is an informed and supportive advocate of the safe use of effective botanical remedies. He allows ample time for the health benefits of these botanicals to be presented in a clear and positive way.

The exotic isles of the South Pacific are home to a long-used traditional ingredient which is just now working its way into the US and European topical and cosmetic industries. Since the 1920’s Oil of Tamanu (Calophyllum inophyllum) has been studied in hospitals and by researchers in Europe, Asia and the Pacific islands. The results of this research are impressive. In 1999 and 2000, I travelled to the South Pacific to study the tamanu tree, and the processing of its oil, and delved into its science in earnest. This is what I learned.

Tamanu’s Healing Powers

Tamanu oil possesses a unique capacity to promote the formation of new tissue, thereby accelerating wound healing and the growth of healthy skin. This process is known as cicatrization. For this reason, it is a widely used traditional topical aid. In Pacific island folk medicine, tamanu oil is applied liberally to cuts, scrapes, burns, insect bites and stings, abrasions, acne and acne scars, psoriasis, diabetic sores, anal fissures, sunburn, dry or scaly skin, blisters, eczema, herpes sores, and to reduce foot and body odor. Tamanu oil is also massaged into the skin to relieve neuralgia, rheumatism and sciatica. Tamanu oil is employed by Polynesian women for promoting healthy, clear, blemish-free skin, and is also used on babies to prevent diaper rash and skin eruptions.

Tamanu and Its Dispersal

Calophyllum inophyllum is indigenous to Southeast Asia, but is profuse in Polynesia. The tree grows up to 25 or even 30 meters in height, with long, spreading limbs. The tree trunk is typically thick with dark, cracked bark. The tamanu branches are covered with shiny, dark green oval leaves, and small white flowers with yellow centres. The blossoms give off a delightful, sweet perfume. The fruit of the tree, about the size of an apricot, has a thin flesh and a large nut hull inside.

Yet the tamanu nut is a botanical oddity. When the fruits of the tree are collected and cracked open, the blond nut kernel inside contains no apparent oil. But when the kernel dries on a rack for a month or so, it turns a deep, chocolate brown, and becomes sticky with a rich, pleasant-smelling oil. Using a simple screw press, the oil is squeezed from the dark kernels. The resulting oil of tamanu is dark green and luxurious. Though oil of tamanu is thick and rich, once it is applied to skin it is readily and completely absorbed, leaving no oily residue.

“Tamanu oil possesses a unique capacity to promote the formation of new tissue, thereby accelerating wound healing and the growth of healthy skin. This process
is known as cicatrization.” - Chris Kilham
Anti-Neuralgic and Skin Healing Activity

Traditionally oil of tamanu has enjoyed topical use in Fiji for relieving the pain of sciatica, shingles, neuralgia, rheumatism and leprous neuritis, for which it is effective. In 1918, researchers associated with the French Pharmacopoeia began research into tamanu for topical and subcutaneous use. The French researchers quickly became impressed by tamanu’s cicatrizing properties. In the French medical literature on tamanu oil, several instances of its successful use in cases of severe skin conditions have been reported. In one remarkable instance, a woman was admitted to the St. Louis Hospital in Paris with a large gangrenous ulcer on her leg which would not heal. Though doctors were sure that amputation was inevitable, she was given regular dressings of tamanu oil. The wound healed completely, leaving a smooth, flat scar. In other cases, tamanu oil has been employed successfully to heal severe burns caused by boiling water, chemicals and X-rays.

Novel Constituents in Tamanu Oil

Oil of tamanu contains three basic classes of lipids, neutral lipids, glycolipids, and phospholipids. The oil also contains a unique fatty acid called calophyllic acid, and a novel antibiotic lactone and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agent called calophyllolide. These and other components of tamanu oil, including anti-inflammatory coumarins, account for some of the oil’s beneficial activity.

Based on the known activity of known constituents, it is clear that oil of tamanu possesses antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activities. The unique cicatrizing properties of tamanu oil are not yet explained in existing scientific literature, though this activity is established and accepted. The same is true for tamanu’s anti-neuralgic properties. Tamanu oil is well documented for its relief of neuritis, but the constituents responsible and their modes of activity are not yet known.
Product Applications

Oil of tamanu is suitable for general skin and cosmetic purposes. The oil’s unusual absorption, its mild and pleasant aroma, and its luxurious feel make it ideal for use in lotions, creams, ointments and other cosmetic products. Considering that tamanu is a potent healing agent with proven benefits, it is only a matter of time before tamanu breaks through to more widespread use, and assumes a position among other successful topical and cosmetic ingredients."

text:

Four stars because they change the pump mechanism and now it's darn near impossible to get all of the product out without breaking off the top and using a cotton swap to dig out the last bit. The serum itself has the feel of a primer, similar to the original, clear SmashBox primer. However, the SmashBox product makes me break out horribly with white heads, particularly on my nose. Both products contain silicone derivatives so not sure why one does and the other doesn't bother me (if I'd been that good at chemistry I'd be a pharmacist!). So, I use this at night after my Retin A has fully dried, to provide some light moisture along with an eye cream. In the morning I use it after applying a light sunscreen by NeutrogenA. I let it dry down and then it provides the perfect base for Clinique Perfectly Real foundation, which has very little slip on its' own.

I'm a makeup and skincare addict (maybe there's a 12 step...) and have used everything from drugstore to crazy expensive products. Give this serum a try, but buy it in the store for $9.99. Use it up and see if you like it. If not, TJ's will take it back, even without a receipt so you have nothing to lose. Oh, forgot to mention I use it on my décolleté and it has helped with the texture of my skin after a lifetime of sunscreen neglect in that area.

title: Comparison with two other brands
text:
Have no fear, I’m here with my Consumer Reports /
Wirecutter-style analysis.

Most importantly, these burst on my second use from the freezer. They don’t stay cold long enough. They don’t get into your eye socket unless you have an enormous eye socket. But if you apply even slight pressure while frozen, they burst. Otherwise, they just touch the highest part of your eyelids and that’s it, so they don’t get into the corners or anywhere between the highest part and the corners. The edges were not sharp. I bought for use after eyelid surgery and was concerned about that. While the edges aren’t soft, they didn’t cut or scratch me. I don’t recommend these unless the only thing you care about is how fun they look. If you do try them, put a damp paper towel between them and your eyes if you use an eye mask on top to hold them down.

Comparing them to ASIN B07RW4S11P, blue ones that have more of an eye shape. I actually liked how the CALA ones felt more than the blue ones, something a bit more plump and soft about the CALA ones. The blue ones had empty space for the inner gel to freeze and move around a bit, so they still haven’t burst despite pressure. I think it’s the plumpness of the CALA ones that makes them susceptible to bursting. The blue ones are also larger than the CALA ones so they reach all the way out to the corners of your eyes and up to your eyebrows. Because there is a bit of empty space, you can put an eye mask on top to hold these down, they won’t burst. I used the Bausch & Lomb Therapearl mask but you can also use an airline eye mask or the like. A silk one if you’re fancy. The problem with the blue ones is that they also don’t stay cold long enough.

I also compared these with the Retherm packs. Those come in a set of four with an eye mask. They get tucked inside the eye mask. I like the size but the eye mask material is too thick so I don’t feel the cold enough. I have yet to try them under the therapearl eye mask.

The Bausch & Lomb therapearl eye mask itself is the best experience of all of these but it also doesn’t stay cold long enough and it’s not large enough.

Conclusion: In this age of advanced technology, I can’t believe that the best choice is still a bag of peas. I recommend petite peas, divided into ziploc bags containing 1/2 to 3/4 cup of peas. You can adjust the amount based on the coverage you need. Place a damp paper towel between your eyes and the ziplocs, especially if you’ve had surgery. If you can, put a loose eye mask on top, otherwise the bags will constantly slide around.

title: Nice conditioner
text:
This is the best shoe conditioner that I have ever used. I used to only use mink oil to polish and condition my boots but I found this off of TBC.com. They sell this for all Thursday’s smooth leather boots. It is super simple to use and you only need a small amount to condition the heck out of your boots. Read instructions but it’s simple:
1) clean off your boots with a horsehair brush
2) put a dime sized amount on a microfiber cleaning cloth
3) apply on your boots in a circular fashion.
4) allow to dry-30 minutes
5) using horsehaired brush buff to a perfect shine
6) use any type of shoe polish/wax

I use this on my Thursday Black Classic Captain’s as you can see in the photos and they give a natural shine. I would not use this on nubuck or suede. Only on smooth leather that can be shined to a mirror finish. This is the same conditioner Thursday sells on their website for their boots. It’s great for your leather boot/shoes/bags etc,. As long as they are smooth leather. I don’t know if it’ll darken the leather or not because my boots are all black except for one. I mean, you can but it will change the way your boots look and the texture for sure. They are a matte finished leather. I used a lot of this conditioner to help break in my Classic black captains. If you wear the same boots you want to condition every day you’ll likely need to put more on every month or so but if you have multiple pairs of boots then you can wait months before needing to apply again. title: I've honestly never seen anything like an all natural safe nail polish before so I ...
text:
As someone who paints her nails at least once or twice a week I go through a lot of nail polish remover. I was curious to test out this product as an alternative to traditional acetone washes that I typically use. I've honestly never seen anything like an all natural safe nail polish before so I was skeptical. Before trying this product I had two expectations that it might not work or that I might need to use an abundant amount of it. Beyond that I was looking forward to using something less pungent and noxious than the acetone.

So I tested this a few times since ordering it, and overall I am highly impressed. My two concerns have proven to be null as the polish remover works and doesn't use up a wasteful amount each time. I found that there is a bit of a trick to making it work best for me though. As the bottle says it is best to let this polish sit for a few minutes before wiping it off with a qtip or cotton ball. My tip to you would be to put a couple of pieces of toilet paper over your nails and put a small drop over each one. This allows it to soak into the paper and stay on your nails longer. After that the cotton ball works great or you can even manage with the toilet paper if youre trying to reduce waste.

title: These are marvelous!
text:
What a great idea! I used suggestions from reviewer “mom of 4” with some exceptions. I did not use any OPI branded products to prep my nails. OPI nas 99 is just 99% isopropyl alcohol so I just used that. MUCH cheaper! (Buy it at the dollar store!) I also used Gelish PH Bond Prep as that is what I had.

I watched some You Tube vids before applying the nail guards. I saw that most of the posters used some kind of tool to press down the nail guards and later discovered a silicone nail tool was what I saw; I almost bought one but ended up with really good results using the eraser end of a new pencil. Now, don’t despair if you don’t apply the nail guards perfectly! Mine were rather wrinkledy but the wrinkles were covered by the builder gel. I also found the guards wrinkled much less when I applied them from the cuticle end and put some traction on the tip end, pulling the guard down over my fingertip gluing to my finger skin before filing the excess. Make sure you file DOWN and not across to remove the excess nail guard. That’s a mistake I made when I first applied these. Don’t worry if you mess up the application of these guards. A few times I had to remove the guard just placed as I completely trashed it on the application. I found that instead of breaking into another card, I could just use two smaller guards to completely cover my billboard-sized nails.

While searching nail videos, I stumbled on Liz at The Nail Hub. If you have not seen her videos, do yourself a favor and watch some. She showed a “pushing” technique in which the gel is laid down on the middle of the nail then pushed towards the cuticle end and sidewalls of the nail, flattening the nail brush. I tried this and it resulted in a much thinner amount of product in those areas with a more natural looking nail at the end.

I used In.Hype Camouflage Pink UV Builder Gel rather than the OPI branded product (it was half the cost) laying down two very thin coats and curing each coat for 90 seconds. Then I applied two coats of my color – curing each for 60 seconds. I’m currently in love with Allenbelle chameleon thermic color 5738, a light pink to dark pink temperature changing glitter polish. I then used one coat of Gelish Top It Off as that is what I had, curing for 90 seconds. My manicure lasts perfectly for two weeks which is about as long as I can stand it before the grow-out starts to bug me. When I’m ready to redo my manicure I just pry the polish off with the paddle end of an orange stick dipped in polish remover. The polish pops right off with absolutely NO damage to my natural nails! The popped off polish looks like a press-on nail!

I applied gel nail polish for years but got tired of the soaking and scraping technique to get the polish off, which also damaged my nail beds. So I went back to regular nail polish for a few years. This wasn’t really a fix, as a regular polish manicure lasts less than a week for me before the polish chips or I just peel it off. Now I can have a long-lasting mani that doesn’t ruin my natural nails! YAY for nail guards!

title: Hahaemall Hardware Works Great
text: I searched long and hard for barn door hardware that would look great and not cost too much. The hahaemall hardware turned out to be an excellent choice for my project. The quality is excellent with heavy construction and a durable, smooth paint finish. I was initially concerned about the shipping times listed on Amazon (about 4-6 weeks), but it arrived much sooner than the standard shipping times in less than two weeks. Even better, I had a special request and emailed hahaemall before I ordered it. They totally helped me out and gave me exactly what I needed. A few things I learned from this project: 1) a pre-made panel would have saved me a ton of time. I glued together a bunch of tongue and groove boards and the end result was basically what a pre-made panel would have been. 2) The optimal thickness of the door is about 1 inch to work best with the geometry of the roller hardware. For that reason, a 6-inch cross board aligned at the top would have been better than the 4-inch cross board mounted below the roller hardware bracket. The solution will be to add a small spacer between the door and the roller hardware. Overall, my experience with Hahaemall was fantastic with quick email responses and faster shipping times than expected. Ordering it from China directly turned out to be no big deal at all.

The language was as follows: "Could you please forgive me and help me delete the review? If you can, I want to refund ($28) to you to express my gratitude. Please accept my little wish.Thank you."

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
First, the good: I enjoy the smell of this product. And I'll probably use the whole stick just because it smells nice, and provides a light tingling sensation. Apart from that, I've noticed no difference in moisture (blackhead reduction, or any of the other laundry list of things it claims to cure).

I got a decent laugh out of my first use, quickly realizing you can't simply roll this onto your face for complete coverage. You have to get this on your fingers to cover the contours of the nose, for example. The description of the product mentions "Blackhead Removal Strips", but those were nowhere to be found in what I received. Once this dries, I simply wash it off of my face, and see/feel exactly what I did when I initially washed my face the first time. Lastly, it's a bit overpriced as far as facial masks go.

So look, I like the soothing sensation of masks as much as the next person. Therefore please understand that I far from hate this product. I simply don't think it's providing much value. Even the satisfaction of a peel-able mask is absent here. But if you really want to pay to smell some tingling green tea drying on your face, then this will get you there. I just wouldn't expect much else from it. The laughably fake "before and after" shots should tell you plenty about the true efficacy of this product.

title: Great for kids with special needs!
text:
I work with a lot of kids and adults with special needs and also have a sister who has Angelman's Syndrome. About 99% of the individuals I work with HATE oral care and fight against it every step of the way. I have used these toothbrushes with many of my clients and just recently purchased some for my sister. I'm so pleased with them!

First, it is much easier to get these toothbrushes into their mouths, which are usually almost clamped shut. Second, it is much easier to move them around the mouth to reach all the teeth (even the very back ones) since the toothbrush head is somewhat smaller than a regular toothbrush. Third, since implementing the use of these toothbrushes my clients' dentists have been very impressed with the improvement of the cleanliness of the teeth and gums. This is very good news for people who must be both sedated and held down/put on a papoose board in order to have any dental work done.

I should mention that if you buy these for someone who often bites down on the toothbrush, it may need to be replaced more often than a regular toothbrush ( like every 2-3 months) due to the damage of the head and bristles. That being said, these things are pretty darn durable!

Cleaner teeth -> less time in the dental chair -> Less emotional and physical stress on both patients and caregivers -> greater happiness for everyone involved. If you care for anyone with special needs and are questioning whether or not to invest in this product, just do it. It is sooo worth the investment.

- The jaws are rough cut and work fine (when you finally get them opened) for larger items but for smaller and very thin items (think resistors) they are not what you want. See photo where I had to bend the resistor wire to get it to stay in the jaws.

While these are inexpensive and fine for the non-discerning use they are by no means competent and have serious flaws that prevent one from using these on many fine and detailed projects. Nothing better. Except the thick: depending on your hair. It can be confusing.
Natural, regular: excellent for super powered conditioner, lays hair flat and feeling amazing.
Thick: does NOT mean extra super powered conditioner, it leaves hair lighter, less conditioned feeling, better for full body or thinner hair that needs some body to it.
If I'm going to simply blow dry my long thick locks, I use natural/regular.
If I have a short hair cut, I'm going to style with gel for a messy, bouncy look, I use thick.
My friends with untameable hair also prefer the natural/regular.
Hope that helps!

text:
Yessss, a non-greasy alternative to fading acne marks. My skin is average(not super oily or dry--it varies with the season/humidity level) and it's a toffee color.
I have acne scars and this is one weapon in my arsenal against them. I put it on every night and if I'm consistent--wow.
This product works, although it does take time. Most importantly, it does not cause me to break out.

My usage:
I use this product along with glycolic acid-- and have suggested a similar routine(minus my acne wash) for a friend with melasma.
I put this product on after my acne free moisturizer. So, if you're interested--here's my night routine: wash with glycolic acid orange japanese soap--leave on for 10 minutes, wash off then wash with acne wash, use rest of acne products, then use retinol on face, then use this directly on the scars. I have never had a dry face before bed(ugh), and if I'm consistent this routine works for my purposes.

Value:
Expensive? Slightly, but it's nothing compared to powerful over the counter "scar fading" products. I don't usually spend $27(prime shipping) on skincare, but I took the leap and i'm glad I did.

This is one of the only products without hydroquinone that works for me. I bought this product on August 4th and by this review I still have plenty left, and I've been using it heavily. A small amount will work, but initially I was desperate to "spot" the fading in action(I apologize for the bad pun).

Assalamu Alaikum. If you are a Muslim or another religion that wears a hijab (headscarf) let me start off by saying that this scarf is NOT for you unless you are purchasing for a child that is 6 or under to wear as hijab.

As far as colors, they were fairly vibrant and really that was the most positive part of my experience with this scarf (not shawl). The Chiffon material is decent but a little cheaply made compared to other Chiffon hijab scarves I have had. And before someone gets all gins shooting about price and you get what you pay for, well that isn't always true. I get way better quality at heart hijab website and they are based in the UK and they ship all the way to the US where I am temporarily. And that isomething total shipping, not shipping per item so if you do a breakdown of scarves versus shipping and cost per item I found much better quality and price elsewhere.

If you are just wearing this for fashion to tie round your neck or use as an accent in your hair up-dos than this is the perfect size and you will have plenty to work with. But if you are in the same boat as me, a Muslim or someone who dresses and covers for modesty than you will be passing this off to your six year old for dress up.

I imagined that all toiletries bags were about the same size, but I was wrong. This one is, to my way of thinking, too big for travel. That said, it's probably great for keeping normal-sized containers organized in an apartment setting where you're sharing a bathroom with housemates. There are four gusseted pockets in the main section, three large ones and one small one for, say, a toothbrush or a razor. Each of the two main sections has a full-width zipper pocket at the back, but they're probably best thought of as either/or. Either you put stuff loose into the big pockets or you organize your items into the smaller pockets in front of the big pockets. title: Good for feeling refreshed in-between washings
text:
Nothing matches the clean, refreshing feeling of a good hair washing, but if you need to "freshen up" between washes, this is a great product. It smells good and I think it does make your hair feel cleaner and fresher.

Other users have complained about a lot of white powdery residue, but I haven't had this problem. Please understand that the powder is what makes this product work: you spray it on (read the instructions and don't over-spray) and then brush it through your hair and it absorbs oil and dislodges dirt to clean your hair. I did see some powder on my black hairbrush, but it wasn't a lot and it's not like it stains or is going to ruin anything, it's just powder. Most importantly, I did NOT see any of this powder in my hair or on my scalp at all. Remove your shirt before brushing it through to make sure you don't get the powder on your clothes (which I would do anyway, I don't like to brush my hair while my shirt is on because it gets hair all over it, yuck) and you won't have any problems.

This is an especially great product now that it's summer time...if you have long hair, you know that you sometimes perspire and it just feels icky, especially in the back (I wear a ponytail and that area gets extremely hot on these humid summer days). My hair is way too long to wash every day (and I have a sensitive scalp so that isn't good for it, it washes away the natural oils too much), so this is a great product to spray and brush through on hot days in-between washings just to feel a little extra clean and refreshed.

This product isn't something I need to use all of the time, but it is good to have when I need a refresher, and I have always enjoyed Garnier Fructis products.

text:
I have used the prescription strength deodorants for a couple years now, it seems like my body gets used to a scent and then it stops working. So I’ve rotated. Then I figured maybe my body needs more natural. So I tried to use the charcoals based. It worked for maybe a week, then the issue started again. Vanilla is my favorite scent for any type of body spray/perfume for me, so I figured I would at least like it. NOPE!! It was the worst. I couldn’t wear it for a full 24hrs before I had to shower to remove the smell.

Tangerine- was like my BO had BO. I usually apply deodorant to the groin and under breasts to help with chafing, but I could smell the deodorant from under my breasts and it was awe full. It made me so self conscious that people could smell how bad I smelled.

Lavender sage was the only one I ended up tolerating and using. But even using this one, I ended up going back to deodorant for my chafing areas.

NONE of them lasted a full 24hr, let alone the advertised hours. I was lucky to make it to bed time before needing to reapply. I shower usually every other day….but the deodorant didn’t last. I even tried washing my pits every evening so it could be a fresh start.

title: Excellent for securing hair in bun.
text:
Living in FL with long hair (down below my waist) I keep it up in a bun most months. I used the goody classic claw clips until I was introduced to the Style Spin pins. They often left me with headaches & they didn't last long breaking easily.

A friend of mine introduced the style spins about two years ago & I am thrilled with them. They are easy to use (take a bit longer than the clips but only seconds), they do not pull on my hair so have not given me a headache one time.

I have used both the long pins (like the ones I'm reviewing) and the shorter pins. Both work equally well. Smaller ones are better for thinner and/or shorter hair, longer pins are better for thicker and/or longer hair. Regardless you could probably use even the shorter ones you would just need to use more of them. I have very long but thin hair & use either two short ones or one long one.

The downside is I lose them easily and they are not easy to find in stores.

To Use:
Personally I pull all my hair together like I'm going to put it in a high pony tail. I then spin it until it is in a fairly tight twist, then spin it in a bun. Once in a bun I put spin one or two of the style spins through the bun until it is secure.

title: Great Product - Great Price!
text:
I bought these plates because my daughters spent the night at a friends and came home with the cutest nails. When I asked about them their friend showed me her 'name brand' set that she paid about $50 for. It had two plates some polish, a stamper & a scraper. I thought it was adorable but was not going to pay that kind of money. Bargain hunter than I am I searched for a better deal. Which led me to Bundle Monster and another 'off brand' that I found on ebay for similar value.

I bought both sets. The received the ebay ones first. They were a great value came with some extras & offered cute plates (a few with the same designs from one plate to the next). They even offered the same designs and our neighbor girl had on her 'name brand' plates (none of which were 'full nail' or 'french tip' images). I was quite satisfied but have to say when I received the plates from Bundle Monster I soon realized I preferred their images better. They were larger for the most part & a much nicer selection over all (I hope they continue to add to their designs).

The ONLY Con I would mention is that the edges seem a bit sharp (compared to both the name brand & the other off brand I purchased) so I would keep them out of reach from young fingers even if they are just 'looking at the designs'. My teenage daughter cut herself on one not paying attention.

For those of you who are having problems with them here are some tips & step by step instructions I use (mentioned by others but with so many reviews I will post it as well).

Tips to Know Before you get started:

1) REMOVE the plastic film: They come with a plastic film when you first receive them that sometimes can not be seen. I used something sharp (tweezers) to cut a spot & then removed the rest with my fingers. If you do not remove the film the plates do not work.

2) Use THICK but NOT Quick Dry Contrasting Nail Polish for Images: If you do not have a 'thick' polish & do not want to spend $10+ on the 'name brand' let one of yours dry out a bit or go to your local salon that does nails & see if they have some 'old stuff' that you can buy for pennies on the dollar.

If you use quick dry you may not get the transfer done quick enough before it drys.

I have tried a few variations of colors but for obvious reasons white & black work best. A dark color with a white or light pink print or a light color with a black or similar dark will have the best results. Do some practice ones on something to see what you really like.

3) Use one coat cover for Bottom Coat & Top Coat: I recommend using nail polish that IS quick dry & only takes one coat to cover for both the Bottom & Top Coats (not images). This is because the more nail polish you have on your nails the more likely it is to smear your images. Using quick dry also helps with this.

4) Use a Good Acetone nail remover: It seems this works best for cleaning the plates. Some remover seems to thin out the polish & make it more difficult to transfer.

5) Let the Plates DRY completely: After each transfer you will need to clean the plate (if there is polish in the image you will not get a good transfer). When you wipe the polish out let the remover dry before you put polish on it. Again it will thin out the polish making for a poor transfer.

6) Use Cotton Rounds instead of Balls: Cotton Rounds make it a lot easier to manage the nail remover without messing up your nails. I use a nail polish remover with a pump so (one touch remover) I don't have to do too much with my hands.

7) Between EACH STEP let your nails dry for the best possible results.

8) If you don't have a plate holder (which I highly recommend) use double sided scotch tape to hold the plates in place on whatever you are scraping the extra paint onto.

9) I also recommend the two sided stamper with the smaller stamp. It is much easier to ensure the best image placement for smaller images.

10) If you have larger nail beds you may want to overlap designs. Everyone has different nail bed sizes so it would be difficult to accommodate everyone. With practice one could learn to line up the designs for a fuller image but I would recommend either using more than one design or just overlapping them. It can create a nice effect as well.

10) Clean EVERYTHING thoroughly when you are done: This will be important so that your future painting will be more successful & so that the plates, stamper & scraper last longer.

My personal steps:

1) Wash hands & gently push back cuticles that might be up on nail bed.

2) Get out all needed products & items.

3) Paint nails with bottom coat. Let dry completely (VERY important for best results)

4) Prepare image plate, image nail polish & cotton round with polish remover.

5) Working Quickly - Paint a nice coat of image paint over your image, scrape away extra, stamp with stamper, line up with nail bed, roll on fast, firmly & carefully ensuring you get the entire image to transfer. (If you have never seen this done check out a youtube video on it).

6) After each image you will have to clean the plate completely (especially if you are using the same image for each nail). Be sure to do so carefully not to smudge your other nails. Some recommend using tweezers - I find if I use a Cotton round instead of a ball I don't need to. Again let the polish remover dry on the plate before adding the polish again.

7) I recommend doing all your images on one hand BEFORE putting on the top coat. Just be gentle not to 'bump' them.

8) Once your first hand is complete put on your top coat & let this dry Completely before starting your second hand.

9) Repeat for second hand!

Once you get the hang of it use multiple designs & colors. We have used it to stamp our phones & more (and change when we get bored)

Hope you enjoy this as much as I did! All the little Girls in my life (age appropriate of course) will be getting this for the next 'gift giving' occasion!!

text: I purchased the initial box of 5 May 31st 2018 thinking it was a great bargain for a product I have used for a long time with stellar performance. I cannot think of a reason why the product would break off in the way they do. I will not purchase this product through Amazon again & believe buyers need to understand what they are purchasing if they do: non-fully usable sticks that break off prematurely, smearing your counter (floor or carpet etc. requiring cleanup) & try as you may, trying to stick the broken piece(s) back into the head of the stick to utilize the full stick will NOT allow you to use the broken off part (once broken off they are UN-usable). I don't know if these items are old or if they are simply of lesser quality. They do seem to be less effective as anti-depressant/deodorant protection. I really love this stuff. Just a few tips. First, clean the area. I use accelerator and this stuff may not stick to it very well. Using tape to grab the stuff seems to work very well. I have had some success with I bedding a very fine fishing filament in this stuff as a small ring. If it does not remove the entire thing, it at least loosens the surface and provides an easy break to grab and remove the rest.

title: Lightweight forumla. Not crazy about the scent.
text:
Bottom Line Up Front: This is a lightweight formula that is easily absorbed by the skin. I would recommend this serum for the day time prior to the application of any makeup. I use this in place of a moisturizing since it is not as heavy. After application, you can still feel the serum on your skin but after a while, all of it is absorbed. There is a strong scent that almost resembles eucalyptus but not in a good way.

I like to try out different skin care products and I have been having great luck with products that are serums. I saw this product and decided to give it a try. The following is my thoughts regarding this product.

**Pros
1. Lightweight - The consistency of this product is lightweight but thicker than other serums I have tried. The serum is of a milky white appearance. When applied to the skin, it is easily absorbed. It is perfect for day time wear and I want to believe that at least I am applying something to my skin prior to slapping on a whole bunch of makeup.
2. Packaging - I always appreciate when skin care products include a dropper or pump to extract the product. In this case, the serum came with a dropper. Based on the consistency, a dropper is perfect to control how much you need.

**Cons
1. Formula - Although the contents may be good for your skin, if you are looking for something to moisturize extremely dry skin, this is probably not it and you should be looking for a cream. Like I mentioned before, this serum is perfect for day time wear. There is also a slight residue or stickiness that I feel after the product dries which I am not fond of.
2. Scent - I am not crazy about the scent. This is the strongest smelling serum that I have tried to date. If you are sensitive to the smell of a product, this may one of the serum that you avoid.

Disclaimer: I did receive this product at a discount but this in no way influenced my review of this product.

text:
Having used the "old fashioned shaving creme and razor" for years, I thought it would be good to try one of the newer electric shaving systems. And to be honest, I tried this electric shaver for close to a month. And for two weeks while using it I was away at a para-military camp where while we were in uniform during the day we were not allowed "any sight of facial hair" so you needed a close shave or you'd be pushing (push-ups).

Now the last I used an electric shaver was a few years ago, and it left me with my skin a bit red and I had to pull my skin a bit while shaving to get it close. So then I went back to the razor which has been giving me a close shave that lasts the day.

This shaving system did not make my skin red (I do believe the moisturizing system works), and gave a good shave, but by the afternoon (initial shave around 5 AM) I had to use the shaver again. However in a normal working setting this may not be a problem.

It is much more convenient to use this. The battery lasts.

I'm believing more and more that there is no substitute for the good ole faithful water/shaving creme/razor. But if you do not need or want a real close shave or if you're a teenager first shaving, then I do believe the Philips Norelco 8040x is for you.

Three mornings ago, in desperation, I started using a paste of 1/4 teaspoon of this product with a scant 1/2 teaspoon coconut oil applied directly to the pimples/lesions on my scalp. I left that first application on for 3 hours (1 hour is recommended but I forgot about it) and then washed it off with warm water and a little shampoo. By that first evening, my pimple/lesions seemed to be less visible. Yesterday, after the second morning of this application (leaving it on for only 1 hour) and washing off, my scalp was almost clear with no itching! This morning, for the third time, I have applied the paste for an hour before washing it off. The turmeric paste has been incredible!! However, yesterday my throat began tasting of turmeric (an almost coppery taste with a tiny bit of heat) and I have been experiencing clean-me-out-completely bowel movements. The finger tip (and nail) I've been using for application of the paste is stained orangey-yellow, the other four fingernails of the same hand are lightly stained, and my hair where the paste was is stained yellowish. I will not be using the paste any longer for these three reasons: the pimples/lesions are now completely gone, my colon must be pristine, and the continuing discomfort in my throat is not something I want to repeat or take lightly. All in all, I must rate this treatment absolutely effective but if you are considering its use, I recommend you carefully monitor how your body feels and adjust the use of this paste accordingly. title: Who has good-looking brows?.. I do :)
text:
I will never go back to the salon to color my eyebrows again. This is exactly the same stuff the professionals use. The first time I did it I wasn't able to remove the product completely from my brows. I tried to make a home concoction to remove the dye. Boy, was that the worst thing to do. I only irritated my skin more by doing that. It looked funny for about 3 days and then I was beautiful again lol

The second time I did it I had the best experience. I used Dy-Zoff Hair Color Stain Remover Pads also from Amazon. I swear by these things. Two wipes and all the excess dye was removed.

Now as far as the dye goes which is what I want to focus on...you don't need to use a whole capsule. I poured about half of one and then closed it off for next time. That was enough for both my brows. The longer you leave the dye on the darker they get.

I'm blonde and I have really light brows. you can see about half of the brow without any added color. I like a darker brow look because I have darker roots and I think it really makes my blue eyes pop. I'll leave it on for about 4 minutes and then I'll do touchups after if I see areas should be a little darker. I recommend starting with one eyebrow at a time because it takes a while to apply the color. Don't be shy. Apply it heavy over the brow. you need to make sure all the hair is colored. My biggest mistake is I didn't bring the dye all the way to the ends so I had stray hairs that were left blonde. Not the biggest deal, but it bothered me a bit.

When you do this always start with less time then they say, just to be safe. It's always better to go lighter. You can always add color, but not take away. Have some dye remover (like the one I recommended) on hand, and do one brow at a time. The only reason why this gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because I experiences slight irritation after.

Good luck!

P.s. If I remember next time I do my brows I'll take a pic so you can see exactly what I mean.

title: What they say is true -- this stuff works!
text:
I've been using this product for about 17 days now. To be honest, I haven't noticed too much of a difference. But then again, I don't really pay much attention to my eyelashes. I just decided to try this stuff for fun. So, today at lunch, my boyfriend of 10 years suddenly looked at me and said, "Are you wearing false eyelashes? They really look long! I've never seen them that long before. They look great!" Of course, I sat there with my mouth open, totally stunned. I thought that it must be a coincidence . . . maybe I put on more mascara than usual, or maybe he just happened to notice my eyelashes for the first time, etc. Then I thought that he's never said one thing about my eyelashes in the 10 years we've been together. Now that's either a really spooky coincidence or maybe, just maybe, this stuff actually works. I still think it's too early to tell and I continue to be skeptical at this point, but I thought I would at least put it out there for those who are considering this product. I'm not yet giving it my full endorsement because the verdict is still out, but I was just flabbergasted and stunned that I received such a comment after using this product for a little under 3 weeks. Is that crazy or what?!

UPDATE

This stuff definitely works. My eyelashes are so long that it's unbelievable. I was recently in a Vegas casino and the blackjack dealer at our table suddenly asked me, "Are those your real eyelashes?" I am so pleased with the results. However, I don't recommend using this on your lower lashes (unless you really want them to be just as long as your upper lashes. I tried this and they were getting way too long to look natural). I think this is a great alternative to purchasing an expensive brand name product that requires a prescription. Two months later, I'm still on my first tube (applying it one time per day) and I believe this tube will probably last me another two months. I've never experienced any of the irritation or redness that others have, but I did notice that my eyes were a little itchy the following morning. I do recommend this product and I'm so excited to continue using it and seeing the results. FYI -- a cheaper alternative that works just as well is Rapid Lash. I've since switched to Rapid Lash because I can get about three tubes of that product for the price of one tube of Renew Lash.

Open it up, & you may just swoon! 💖It will be love at first sight! 💓 You will be enamored! And oh yeah.... the shadow colors are glistening jewel toned perfection. A sweep of your finger will give you this shimmery multi-dimensional color, that sort of floats on your skin, like a watery mirage. It's spectacular! You may never stop adoring this treasure like aquisition, with it's mirror inside the lid, & each color inlayed in a cirle around a large iridescent white shadow/highlighter. This pallette reminds me of summers by the glistening water, or a getaway on a tropical island.

You want this pallette! It's one of a kind! You can play all day with the different uses of this pallete. Each color can be layed down over a matte look (from other pallettes you own) to make it shimmery perfection. Use a little, or alot, depending upon the look you're going for. For example, do a matte green shadow on your lid, & then put a wash of the green shimmer from this pallete, over top to pop the color. It is not one of those cheap, call girl looking shimmers. It reminds me of Chanel or Dior's eyeshadow quads. They are multi-dimensional, sheer-like shadows, that can create all kinds of looks.

All I can say, is make sure, when you receive it in the mail, that you have a good 6 hours to play with all the different looks you can achieve! This pallette is an artists dream. It is a luxurious addition to your collections, not a basic staple.

So go......have lots of fun, my dears!🤗

*FYI - this pallete is a 100% authentic Tarte product, offered for a fair price.

title: High Quality Product, Well Designed. Closest Shave I've Had in Years.
text: The first time I used this razor, I cut myself. I hadn’t cut myself shaving in about 20 years. The reason I cut myself is because this razor is engineered properly. This may sound contradictory, so let me explain. In most safety razors, the blade is recessed too much and is at an angle that is considered optimum to prevent nicks and cuts. Because in typical razors the blade is recessed too far, the shaver must press harder to reach the whiskers. Still, the shaver will require two to three passes to obtain a close shave because the angle of the blade is too sharp; this often results in razor burn. If you are an experienced user of safety razors, I’m sure you’ll agree. This razor has the blade at the proper angle as well as at the proper depth. The result is the closest shave I have had in decades. If you’ve used a straight razor you know why the safety razor was invented: 1) There is no need to sharpen the blade because it is disposable. 2) The angle of the safety razor is automatically correct. 3) It is safer than a straight razor because the blade is recessed. This razor will take a bit of getting used to. It took me about three seconds, but I’ve used straight razors, safety razors and disposable razors for about 50 years. So, that’s just me. I highly recommend purchasing this product.

title: How is Bay Rum Popular it smells like rotten eggs!
text:
I’ve been a Lumé user since Spring of 2020. I like the deodorant because most “natural” deodorants really irritate my sensitive skin where it’s unbearable and anything that’s aluminum based destroys my underarms. The formula of this is nice, I don’t find it to clump in my underarm hair like other deodorants do. It goes on smooth and seems to absorb into my arm pits nicely.

Alright so here’s the reasons I scored Lumé Bay Rum so poorly:

I’ve been continuously disappointed because any scent that I like, they end up discontinuing. 😭 First it was Blue Spruce or Juniper something that then morphed into Juniper Breeze and then that just disappeared.

I was in a bind in June and Bay Rum was the fastest scent that could ship so I tried that one. I figured since it was so popular and has been around for a long time, that this scent was going to be incredible! My expectations were clearly set too high because WOW this stuff STANKS! It smelled like rotten eggs. I know I have an aversion to rum after a bad night at my friends wedding in 2015 but I thought I could put that in the past for the sake of my underarms. Unfortunately, this stuff really stunk and doesn’t even smell like rum anything! Not even rum raisin ice cream or malibu or a beautiful fresh bay!

One thing I’ve noticed since buying Lumé from Amazon is that the consistency of each deodorant is never the same. Sometimes it’s an oozing, soupy mess, other times it’s a light fluffy consistency that’s just perfect, then it also can come out like a gritty, frosting that struggled to exit the 3 little holes on the deodorant stick.

I’m a big guy and I sweat a lot and there’s a lot of space to cover on my underarms, so I never have been confident in Lumé’s 72-hour claim however I’ve had success with about 24 hours (not with Bay Rum though). Right now I’m using Tangerine and it’s nice and lasts for a little bit… definitely not as long as the OG scents they discontinued, but I can make it through most of the summer day without smelling like a disgusting heap of trash!

Some of the other scents don’t last that long on me, but when I put rotten egg smelling Bay Rum on me I really don’t feel like I’m covered at all. I used this for a bit of June and had to throw it out because I couldn’t even go a few hours without smelling stinky. As a fat person, I’m very aware of my size, my personal hygiene and of course how I smell.

Anyways, stay away from this gross scent - maybe I got a bad batch of it, but I’m just scratching my head at how Amazon says this is the most popular scent. Maybe they’re all just trying to sell off this disgusting batch.

BRING BACK JUNIPER BREEZE!

title: 4C Dream come true
text:
My 4c hair has destroyed dryer combs on the first use so I got in the habit of buying multiple combs at once. After one use I know that wouldn't be the case with this one.

Using it.
I passed the comb through sections about 4x as large as usual AND used more force than I usually do. It didn't bend and I didn't have use two hands to help the comb get through.

Sizing
It took less than a minute to unscrew it and screw it onto my dryer. There are several smaller, removable rings inside that determine the size of the opening. Take out more rings for a larger nozzle or keep them for a smaller one. Then just tighten the one screw. The comb fits on my dryer with no inserts, so if I need to do a quick pass-through on my previously blown out hair, the comb stays in place without the metal ring. I NEED the ring if I'm drying my 4c hair from wet.

Has a tight hold
The slick surface of my dryer allows its included combs to slide off. The metal ring that comes on this comb doesn't allow that. The comb fits on my blow dryer without the smaller inserts. I noticed that if I don't have to use force the comb stays on without the metal ring, but this may not be true on a smaller barrel that requires the inner rings for sizing. I imagine the comb would spin around the rings.

text:
I was excited to be approved for this promotion, I did receive this kit complimentary for review purposes. These are my unbiased opinions.

I always love to try and whiten my teeth as they are permanently yellowed from allergy shots I got as a baby so trying to keep them as white as possible is something I like to do though the kits are very costly and when on a budget it is not always practical. The Ultimate Smile kit is reasonably priced and you can get multi uses out of the trays, just have to repurchase the whitening gel.

When I first got the kit I wanted to try it right away but was a little nervous as so many of the kits hurt my teeth since I have a sensitivity problem. I read about it and it said " this unique formula has a specific balance of ingredients forming together to create a highly potent but sensitivity-proof product with proven results." So I said ok then, lets give it a try. Well lets say I am glad I did, I have not had any sensitivity with this product. I did only use it once a well for the first 2 weeks and then every day for the last 3 days and all seems ok. Best of all I can see a slight lighting of my teeth. So yes the product does work!

I do have to say that the only thing that I found in the negative was the directions, they are seriously lacking! How often do you do this treatment? How to exactly get the trays to mold to your mouth? They give you some info but not enough, I had to do read around the internet to help with the way to fit my trays properly. (That is why I gave it a 4 star rating)

title: Cute pink hair dryer with a long cord!
text:
This hair dryer is super cute, the color is a rich hot fink with black trim. I received it to review and all opinions expressed are my honest opinion. I already had a decent hair dryer, but was interested in getting a second non-travel sized dryer. I think this may replace my existing hairdryer.

What I like:
*It has the options I use: two speeds, three temperature ranges, cool air shot, etc.
*The attractive appearance is a plus as I am planning to use it in my swimming/gym bag. Yes it is bigger than a travel dryer, but I have found that my travel sized dryer has been inadequate--it just doesn't have enough power to quickly dry my long hair. This dryer has the power and is a little more compact and more attractive than my other name brand full sized hair dryer.
*I like the long cord. It is considerably longer than my other dryer. It is about 89" long. I like this since I move around a bit while drying and have accidentally unplugged my previous hair dryer. If you prefer a long cord, this may be a good option for you.

It came with two concentrator nozzles, I personally would have preferred a diffuser and one concentrator nozzle. But that is a minor preference.

I find this hair dryer effective for drying and styling my hair. And it doesn't hurt that it is very attractive and has a long cord.

Update after returning the defective scraper and purchasing another (identical) one:
At first glance and after first try the scraper looks good and it is adequate to the job. Enclosed instruction for use is written well and wording is clear. The guard covers the sharp blade well while storing the scraper. Finally, I am completely satisfied with this product. In addition, the manufacturer (Werxrite) cares about its reputation and tries to resolve the issues with their product (see, for example, manufacturer comments to my original review below). This is a huge plus nowadays when the market is flooded in by low quality products. My original review below was caused by two reasons: 1. Instruction card was not enclosed in the package. 2. The blade guard cannot stay (defect) in the closed position. Because of all these reasons, please, disregard my original review below.

Update after reading two manufacturer comments for my review may be found in my comment below. Reasons for my review below are explained in my comment. I will update this review later as explained in my comment. For now, please, disregard my review.

Original review:
Multiple scraper pictures don't show very thin (about 1mm wide) plastic elastic rope that is stretched between the black and red buttons on the pictures of the gray scraper. The red button is attached to the red plastic guard (see it on top of the picture) of the blade, and the black button is attached to the body of the scraper. When you push the red button with your thumb down, the red blade guard moves also down stretching the unshown plastic rope and blade gets naked (working position). When you release the red button, the stretched elastic plastic rope shrinks and pushes the guard up hiding the blade. This plastic rope is so thin that it broke at first use. text: I like to use this product for the first 3-7 days after getting a new tattoo until it is through the peeling stage. I've used a wide variety of products over the years and I find this to be the easiest application, least offensive scent, and overall effective. I typically heal pretty quickly so I start peeling at about day 3 and am typically done within a day or two. I will also continue using this if I want a better barrier between my new tattoo and the world for any reason as healing continues. It is a bit greasy but not terribly different than Aquaphor or A&D, plus I find it easier to wash out of my clothing. After the majority of the peeling has occurred I switch to more traditional cream lotions (depends on the local market availability for which brand I use) for the next couple of weeks as I've found my prolonged use of these gel products causes occasional breakouts.

title: Superb product
text:
The thing that intrigued me about this product and what caused me to go for it was that it states they use the Prolong lash cleanser concentrate which is pretty much standard in the eyelash extension community. I was glad to see that they are a product without any alcohol, parabens, pigments, phthalates, or ethylene oxide. Plus that it is formulated with amino acids which gives it an additional boost. I used it on my eyelash extensions and it worked wonderfully. They did not cause any lashes to fall aside from the usual that normally fall off when washing. The tiniest amount goes a loooooong way trust me. Less than a pea size amount foams up so nicely and it spreads very well so you can get every lash. Please note you do have to rinse the product off your eyes because it doesn’t dissolve in its own. Then after you rinse it off you pat your eyelashes down with a lint free cloth/paper towel and brush with a spoolie while lightly fanning them and then let them air dry. I absolutely loved this product for myself and it didn’t cause me any irritation whatsoever. But my sister used it and it caused irritation for her eyes so it does vary from person to person, just a side note.
PRO TIP: Only use a small amount, the size of a pea is already too much so go for less. A little goes a loooooong way.

title: Awesome scrubbies for bathtime!
text:
These are not like anything I've seen before here in America. My friend gave me one years ago and I'm hooked. They are not meant to be soft or thick. They are intended to be "rough" to exfoliate the skin and thin for flexibility and ease of rinsing. I've used all kinds of "scrubbies" or puffs, which are intended to be soft and thick. Those make lots of foam but do a very gentle job. They're great for a relaxing or pampering experience. These "netting sheets" are for when you really want to get clean! I absolutely love them for scrubbing my back. The length makes this job super easy and satisfying! Folding them or using them full length makes them versatile and usable for all areas of the body. I'm handicapped and these make it easy for me to reach and clean everywhere. I LOVE them.

One caution (because we live in a world where people misuse products and then cry and blame the product): these are rough textured; they will scrub with a lighter pressure. If you are used to pressing other products firmly in order to scrub your skin, don't do that with these because you don't have to. Use them as intended. Start gently and adjust pressure to your preference. I never had the slightest problem but there are people who have taken steel wool pads to their skin so I felt I had to say something.

title: Better quality than I was expecting!
text:
First off, the box size blew me away! Quite large, compared to some I've gotten.

The metal ornaments (the roses, diamond frame, hearts, and butterfly) are heavier.. the roses, the hearts, and frame.. than I was expecting! Way heavier! The butterflies... OMG... so delicate, yet sturdy! So in live with the little guys.

That said, not all is perfect. For one, there is no clear indicator as to what is the front of the box. Usually it's pretty easy to tell, but this one.. not so much.
Next thing.. the packaging for the little pearls!! Apparently, they react to the plastic pouch by building up static electricity, thus they stick to the inside of the pouch, or jump everywhere! In short, they were a major pain to simply pour into their little section. None of the others had this issue... just the pearls.

Aside from those two things, which I knocked a star off for, this is an awesome set, with lots of creative potential!

They also pull away from my lid at the outer edges, making it very obvious that the lashes are both false and poorly applied. The second problem is that the magnets on the false lash strips stick better to the metal applicator than they stick to each other; when trying to apply the strips using the application tool, I found that most of the time the lashes would drag away from my lashes and get pulled out of place, rather than sitting neatly where I was trying to place them.

I would not recommend this purchase.

text: Mighty Patch is among the best pimple patches I've tried, so I was eager to try this bigger strip. My chin has been a problem area for me since I was a pre-teen, but lately my nose has actually been the issue. I haven't had real breakouts, but have pores the size of a Manhattan apartment all over my nose that I just can't get fixed. So despite the fact that I don't often have much luck with patches getting anything other than a well-developed white head cleared, I put one of these sheets upside down from the chin direction on my nose for a night. It was surprisingly uncomfortable. Once I put a normal pimple patch on, I can't feel it and forget it's there until the light hits it right. But the big strip across my nose was a very noticeable feeling that I was anxious to take off. I resisted the urge, and fell asleep. In the morning I was pleasantly surprised! There were more white spots than I expected from just enlarged pores without any developed white heads. So despite the discomfort, I will use these patches when I'm frustrated with a larger swath of my face. I have cut this brand's dot patches in half many times for smaller zits, and think you could slice this big patch up into many smaller bits to get it all where you really want it, but I wouldn't count on being able to save any of it for later once you've unsealed the package. I'm always interested in how to use these more frugally, because they seem really pricey to me. I generally don't want to use one unless I'm really sure that it will work.

title: Moisturizing eye cream, irritates my picky skin
text:
UPDATE: I have reduced my rating to three stars after more use. This cream turned out in the longer term to irritate my eyes, make them swollen, red, and painful. It's in good company though; I have found that everything designed to be an eye cream to help skin health and appearance has irritated my eyes (this is one of four products that have recently had the same effect). So while I cannot personally recommend this cream, my experience of it may be far from universal. I did like how it felt going on, and actually liked the jasmine scent.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (4 stars): The Penebella Brighten & Repair Eye Cream includes a lot of ingredients that are really good for your skin: retinol, hyaluronic acid, aloe, and Vitamin E, among others. It does also contain jasmine essential oil, which is an odd choice to me. I am sensitive to scents, and to floral scents in particular, but this jasmine does not bother me at all, which is surprising. I actually find it to be subtle and pleasant, but nonetheless would not choose to have any fragrance added to a product meant for some of your most sensitive skin around your eyes. It strikes me as unnecessary at best.

This cream does feel light and moisturizing. The very fine needle nose dispenser makes it easy to get precisely the amount of product you intend, which is important when using relatively small amounts of relatively expensive products. I haven't ever ended up with more product than I intended or could use well for application.

When I began using this product, the skin around my eyes were swollen and sensitive from the dry winter air and indoor allergies. After about a week of consistent use, my eyes still feel swollen and sensitive. Honestly, the much simpler, cheaper basic lotion I have for my eyes relieves that feeling better. However, this cream has ingredients that make it better for long term use and improvement. So I will continue to use it and appreciate it for the anti-aging effects, but won't rely on it for daily relief from irritated eyes. If using it longer affects my judgment of this, I will update my review accordingly.

title: Started great but went down in experience
text:
If you are expecting Shave which is closer to Blade then stop. No Rotary Shaver will ever will do that. I have used Rotary Shavers for last 20 years for beard and I purchased this product with those expectations only. I bought this product for its high ratings, 5 blades vs 4 blades and digital display for battery life. I bought it for my head not face. I still use my Norelco for Beard and quite happy with it.

It started pretty good and deserved all the high ratings when I started using it new.

5 Blades seem better than four but now I feel four is more practical. It is pain to open blades for cleaning. I can still manage outer four with little effort but middle on is pain in fingers. You are supposed to push outer blades backwards and open those first and then rotate middle one counter clock wise to open it but there is no grip to do that. It is just too small and flushed with bottom surface. Same happens when you try to put it back after cleaning. Guys stick with 4 blades

Battery: This is where it let me down after 2.5 months of use. Battery and its digital display worked just fine for a month and a half and then out of blue it went from 30% to 9% in the middle of shave. Then after a few days I turned off shaver after use with battery level of 27% and couple of days later it won't turn on and forced me to charge. You cannot use this shaver plugged in so if battery dies on you you would need about an hour before you can use it again. I wish I had that luxury in morning.

Now after 2.5 months of use I can hear freshly washed/cleaned shaver struggling even in air. Doesn't look like it will last very long.

I feel that I didn't get the worth of money I spent on this product.

The eye drop solution itself is BRILLIANT! The best I've found so far. No preservatives, no phosphate and feels silky smooth in the eye. No burning - and all drops burn my eyes - but not these. It contains Sodium Hylauronate, the best ingredient for healing and soothing the eye, in my estimation, and that is very hard to find in preservative free eye drops.

The bottle applicator however is bloody awfu! It is very awkward to hold and dispense with one hand, or two for that matter. Your wrist must be double jointed to operate this bottle. It's the only way! The bottle is thick white plastic and you cannot see how much of the solution is in the bottle. You hear NOTHING when you shake the bottle, so the only way you may know that the solution is actually in there, is if it comes out when you depress the plunger. You will most certainly be down to your last drop before you realize that you need to reorder, thus having to wait another three weeks for it to arrive, while your eyeballs dry out like rotting persimmons, and your eyelids suction to them like a squid on a diver's mask.

The bottle says 10 ml, so basically it contains 2 American teaspoons of solution. If you don't want to run out, it's best to just go ahead and reorder the day after you receive your first order to be on the side of caution. Whoever engineered this bottle applicator clearly drinks and thinks he knows things. Worse yet, a ligitimate company with an outstanding eye solution product said YES to this evil little bottle of frustration and buggery. Don't let this stop you from purchasing the drops. Have another person carefully read the instructions and dispense them for you. It's worth it.

title: Im beginning to see the results I have been looking for for a very long time....
text:
Now that I'm in my mid 30's I have started noticing unwelcome changes in my skin. I'm seeing fine lines creeping up and dark circles under my eyes are nearly an everyday occurrence and my skin doesn't have that same elasticity and glow that it did when I was in my 20's. I seen SKEDERM and really wanted to give it a whirl. I have tried numerous under eye serums and treatments, some of them giving me great results and others end up being a complete and utter waste of money.
When my bottle of SKEDERM Ultimate Eye Cream arrived the very first thing I noticed was just how expensive the bottle looked to me. It really did have the appearance of one of those very expensive bottles of eye serums and treatments that you would purchase at a high end department store. I thought that the bottle itself could draw you in and make you want to purchase it. Very pretty.
As for the ingredients, it contains retinol, hyaluronic acid, and something called antarcticine. I had never heard of antarcticine before so I did look it up and found that it is a glycoprotein that is extracted from the Antarctic Sea, and it has anti-wrinkle and restructuring properties. Plus it contains moisturizing ingredients from rare Antarctic creatures that allow you to control moisture balance. Very cool stuff!
It can be used on pretty much all skin types like: dry skin, normal skin, oily skin, combination skin, and sensitive skin. Its recommended for use on aged skin, wrinkled skin, non-elastic skin, stressed skin, and dull skin. And sadly, my skin falls in almost all of those categories. Also, it is formulated WITHOUT synthetic colors, fragrances, parabens, phthalates, and sulfates.
You can use SKEDERM Ultimate Eye Cream every morning under your makeup or use it alone. Then you should reapply it on clean skin every night. It says to apply small amounts around your eyes using your fingertips until it is completely absorbed. And I will add that I little bit goes a long way. Which is good because that means a bottle will last a long while!
I have been using SKEDERM for almost a month now and I can see an improvement in the dark circles under my eyes. I usually have the appearance of someone that's always tired because of how my under eye area always looks, but its really starting to look better. I'm very pleased with that. My eyes are not nearly as puffy. I like that the cream goes on very smoothly and absorbs very well. I also like that it doesn't leave an oily residue after it absorbs. I also like that its fragrance free and my skin is extremely sensitive to a lot of different things and this worked great for me. A lot of times if I use eye serums or creams my eyes will water and my eyelids will get puffy, I don't know what causes it but I didn't experience that since using SKEDERM. I'm very happy with my experience and hope that after continuing to use it I will start to see the fine lines under and around my eyes will start to fade. So given my experience with SKEDERM Ultimate Eye Cream I would definitely recommend it to anyone with the same issues I have.

title: Use it right and it'll work great
text:
I actually like this straightener brush. I had read mixed reviews on them because I've been wanting to try one so I've been researching different brands and reading reviews. This works really well but you have to work with it. You cant just brush it through your hair and expect great results. Thats not how it works. And that's not how any typical flat iron works so I dont agree with people thinking this should be any different. It has it's pros and cons but more pros than cons. I tried this on my straight yet frizzy hair. And I tried this on my daughters curly hair. I had good results with both.

Pros: It came quickly in the mail and was nicely packaged
It appears to be made with good quality
It heats up fast and the numbers on the screen climb up as it heats so you can tell what temp it's at while you wait
It doesnt burn you and all of the heating units are well covered for your protection
It glides nicely through your hair
It makes your hair soft
Works better on frizz than a flat iron
Easier to use than a flat iron
Helps maintain volume

Cons:
It's only in Celsius
If heated all the way to the highest temp it stinks
The cord is kinda short
At times it pulls your hair out

Now if you use it right it will work really well for you. What I did initially was comb it through the hair like a brush. I had combed my hair with a bore bristle brush before doing this. It kinda sets the hair up for you to section well. I sectioned the hair and held it straight up and put the straightening brush right up to the scalp and combed under and out creating an arch with it so that my hair would curl under. I was able to straighten more hair at once with this than a normal flat iron. All I did to finish my hair was to keep sectioning hair and using the same motion by going on the under side of the hair and arching out I created a really nice looking style. My hair had less frizz, was softer, had more volume and more bounce to it than when I've used a flat iron. So I guess I'll be using this from now on. My only concern was the smell that happened when turned all the way up but I've had other irons that smelled too. So I'm assuming it's the silicon or rubber caps to protect your head. You dont need it turned up all the way. I was able to create the style I wanted at the half way mark.
I'll keep using this and if I have any problems I will update this post.

title: Really Excellent for Waves & Curls
text:
I have long hair that's wavy to curly, in layers. It's not kinky, is very thick, and is about average in terms of coarseness-- neither course nor fine. It is prone to frizz, and I live in the South where it is very humid.

Finding a product I like is a challenge, but I really do love this one. In the shower, I wring my hair out, then apply the product--a quarter-sized dollop, then comb it through with a wet shower comb to re-wet as directed. After applying, I often end up wrapping my hair in a towel after I get out so my hair isn't soaking, and I have not noticed this affecting my outcome. In an hour, I've got a head full of soft, shiny curls. There's no frizz, no tangles, no flaking, and no stickiness. And you've got volume at the roots-- no slicked down, weighed down, crunchy roots!

The best part is the next day or two. If I twist my hair up in a bun and go to sleep, I will get a different look in the morning-- looser waves, still soft and touchable without the greasy roots or weird stiff hair that other products give you. I love a product that doesn't require a daily do-over.

I started out with the 2 oz size to try out (I'm jaded when it comes to hair products), but I will be moving up to the 32 oz now-- that's how much I like it!

title: Good nail polish, but still has the nail polish smell
text:
TL;DR: Good choice if you're looking for polish with fewer harmful chemicals and a less intense nail polish scent. Not for you if you need allergy-free or scentless polish.

My partner has always been sensitive to the smell of nail polish and it seems I've developed a sensitivity as well. I tried painting my nails a few weeks back and was super dizzy and lightheaded before I finished.

After a lot of research to find polishes that don't require a HazMat suit, I came across this brand and one other. I liked the color range of Zoya better (400+!), so I ordered this kit and the color lock kit (remover, basecoat, topcoat, and dry drops - https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B005IDHCSM/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o06_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1).

Pros:

- The basecoat and topcoat both went on super easily.
- The dry drops are a little oily, but my nails were completely dry in under 15 minutes (dry enough to do things in under 5).
- The colors are gorgeous. Mia, the second shade, had almost full coverage after one coat and full coverage after two. The color also went on super easily.
- I'm only on day two, but typically by this time I've chipped even anti-chip polish really badly. So it's impressive to me that it's holding out. This kit claims 14 days, I'll update with how long it actually lasts.

Cons:

- The bottles in the Color lock kit are super tiny. The remover is travel size and the basecoat, topcoat, and dry drops are somewhere between travel and sample size.
- While they don't smell quite as bad as other polishes I've used, they still have that nail polish scent. It didn't make me dizzy, light-headed, or cough, so that's a bonus. Nor did the scent hang around or cause my partner to seek me out to ask why I was doing my nails when he was home. But it's stronger than I was expecting and was nowhere near being scent-free.

All in all, I'd recommend this. It's at least somewhat healthier than other brands, the color palette can't be beaten, and the application is great. Just know what you're getting yourself into.

Update: the polish started chipping after 4 days. Not the worst, but not the best either.

title: Easy to use and seems effective.
text:
My girlfriend tried this mask product and she convinced me to try it as well. Overall the instructions and process is pretty easy and straightforward. You can't really do anything wrong. You wash your face first, dry off, and apply the mask. There's a subtle scent that smells a little sweet, but isn't overpowering. The mask itself is wet and covered with a kind of moisturizing gel with little black beads which I assume was the caviar. We lined up the eye cutouts and carefully applied the mask on. It had a really nice cooling sensation. The masks are pretty large so after lining up the eye holes we wrapped the extra material below and slightly beyond our chins and close to our ears on the side. So if you have a normal or slightly larger face the mask seems like it would still accommodate you. The moisturizing gel must be water soluble since after applying the mask it was pretty easy to rinse our hands clean without the need for soap. We kept the masks on for the instructed 10 minutes and removed the mask. We did a light rinse of our faces to remove any of the residual gel.

Verdict: The mask actually seems to work. I noticed that some of the pores on my cheek had filled and smoothed out. Cheeks and forehead skin felt a little more smooth. Overall the skin on our faces around the cheeks looked brighter and ....???....more polished? Not glossy, but just cleaner and I think hydrated. Don't get me wrong, I didn't suddenly become a candidate for being a supermodel, but I did look a bit better. Next morning the effects seemed to still be there, but a tad less. Also there was no nightmare rash, pimple breakouts, or weird reaction so the mask and gel seems pretty safe.
