DMSO has a low toxicity rating and may very well be a “miracle” pain reliever and have many other beneficial uses, but its biggest plus is also its biggest minus—it quickly and super-effectively delivers substances through the skin and into the bloodstream, and magnifies or “potentiates” their effects. This can be beneficial in some situations, but potentially very harmful in others, and that’s likely why the research on DMSO is so contradictory.

DMSO’s super efficient through-the-skin delivery means that it has to be extremely pure to be safe. Any impurities or toxins present will be carried directly into the bloodstream. In winter month the butter is amazing, its thick enough to not disappear in the harsh winds and moisturising enough to keep your skin hydrated and soft. I use it has my night time face cream, it has helped with my dark spots.
There are so many benefits to adding Shea butter to your daily routine:
Shea butter aids in the skin’s natural collagen production and contains oleic, stearic, palmitic and linolenic acids that protect and nourish the skin to prevent drying. With longterm use, many people report skin softening and strengthening as well as wrinkle reduction.
A 2010 study found that due to its cinnamic acid and other natural properties, shea butter was anti-inflammatory.One compound in particular, lupeol cinnamate, was found to reduce skin inflammation and even potentially help avoid skin mutations. This also makes it beneficial for some people with acne.

It could also be that a child might be better suited to wearing these than I am. My hair is a bit thick and long, or at least that is my opinion. These bands are not weak and should last well beyond one wearing. Therefore, there are lots of them for a small price. The bags, too, are cute and have a picture of a small chick on each.

I think it's a reasonable assumption that they are selling the expired products after repackaging them with no printed expiration date where that is allowed. How shady are they deceiving overseas customers like this? Are they inferring that their products are "expired" by adding ("Old"/Korean Packaging) in the product description. title: I finally found a nice, quality large size clip!
text:
I've been happy with this clip. The spring on my old Goody clip finally bit the dust and finding a quality replacement in a large 5 inches size is quite challenging. I find that most clips nowadays are made with a brittle type of plastic that when I inevitably drop it on my tile floor, a tooth or two on the clip can easily break off. This clip seems to be made of the more pliable or soft plastic like my old Goody clip was made of - so drops don't result in a tooth shattering off the clip. I also really like the low profile of the tabs for your fingers on the back of the clip - they don't protrude nearly as much as on a regular clip and I like that. I also like the tortoise shell color - it blends in well with my hair color. I was willing to pay for a quality clip that would last and I am happy with this purchase. I like to have a few around the house for whenever or wherever I need them (cooking in the kitchen, in the bathroom for brushing teeth/washing face, in my suitcase, etc.) I will definitely be buying a couple more.

UPDATE: July 2019 - I still really like this clip and use one every day (I own several) however I've now had two break within a couple of months of purchase. One was at 3 months and one at 8 months. I can't remember what broke on the first one but this last one the spring didn't break - it was the plastic that holds the spring that twisted and will no longer hold the spring (see photo.) I love these clips because I have very long hair and they do hold my hair, but at $10 each I wish they lasted longer than 3 or 8 months. I had a Goody clip that lasted at least 15 years before it finally failed (spring broke) - too bad Goody no longer sells the super large clips. 3 stars off for the poor durability of this product.

title: Excellent, even for a blade-user
text:
I bought this shaver a while ago, but I wanted to wait at least a month before writing my review, since it's supposed to take about that long before your face is used to an electric razor.
This is my first electric, and I was concerned going into it. I looked at the price of good standard blades, though, and saw how quickly an electric razor would pay for itself. I'll never go back. For the first week, the shave was not as close as I had become accustomed with using a blade. After that, though, I've gotten closer and closer shaves by the week. After a little more than a month of using the Spectra, my skin is now smooth even against the grain. I've gotten back to where I was with a blade.
The Pros:
- Shaving takes easily only half the time as it did with a straight razor.
- I can shave any time, any where. With a blade, if I tried to shave more than once per day, I'd cut myself all up into a bloody mess. With this electric, I do notice some discomfort after having shaved a second time in a day, but it gets a nice close shave. A little after shave takes care of the sting, and I'm good to go again.
- No mess. I really don't miss having to use shaving cream, even my nifty hot-lather shaving cream.
The Cons:
- Motor power seems to wind down a bit towards the end of the battery charge. It's not too bad, but it seems to take longer to shave at the end of the charge, and I don't want to charge it early for fear of damaging the battery.
- This is really a minor quibble, but I thought I'd mention it: Since this razor rinses clean under tap water, what few bits of hair are still left over are sitting in water over night. Every time I use the razor, for the first minute of shaving, it smells very strongly of old, wet hair.
Tips:
- Blade users: Apply less pressure than you're used to. I find I get a better shave when the razor is touching the skin firmly, noticibly, but not pressing in at all.
- Rinse it out every day, and turn the faucet up high. If you let it go a couple days without rinsing, it's much harder to clean out. It only takes a couple seconds, so why not?
- Shave daily. I find that if I let my beard get a little longer the shaver still does a pretty good job. However, there will always be a few hairs that grew too long, curling down, that are not lifted by the razor head. Just shave daily, when you only have stubble, to avoid this.
- Get a makeup mirror! These little mirrors are concave, magnifying your face so you can see where you've missed more easily. I mounted mine to the wall, slightly below my chin. Now I can more easily see if I've shaved my neck well.

title: So close to perfect.

I'm still looking for the perfect razor. The Mach3 Turbo comes close, though. I've been using it daily (or nearly so) since its debut. It works, and it gets the job done. It rarely nicks me, but I do still get skin irritation. Down under my jawline, I still feel scraggly by the end of the day, but it's not too bad.
I know this sounds like a bad review, but it really isn't. I mean, it's tough to get excited about shaving, but at least the Mach3 Turbo has me shaving every day,if you want to shave with a blade, this is the blade for you.

title: Just what a natural loofah is supposed to be!
text:
I’ve been using natural fiber loofahs (not the plastic kind) off and on since 2010. By nature there is some variation, depending on the size of the underlying plant, the way it’s made/grown, any bleaching, softening or other treatments applied that may change the texture. This is GREAT value for three medium-to-small sized natural loofahs.

The first time you use it you gotta soak it in warm water to puff up (it will turn into an oval cylinder, rather than staying like a flat pad) and release its seeds. I didn’t find the seed quantity to be gross or unreasonable, though it’s definitely different than most natural loofahs you’ll buy in a drugstore or Whole Foods, say—those tend to be treated and at least prewashed, to remove the seeds etc.

The smell: I have a super sensitive nose. Just speaking for the item I received, this is 100% “normal loofah smell” —a little grassy, kind of like dried clean straw that’s been dampened again—with a bit of a smoky smell. It’s not offensively smoky. Like a lot less than most whiskey. No “funk,” though the natural loofah herbaceous-ness does get stronger when it’s wet.

I didn’t find this too scratchy at all—in fact, by the time I’d finished soaking out the seeds I found it a little soft for my liking. To be fair I do drybrush about once a week, so I’m used to a good scrub. But if you know what a “normal store-bought loofah” feels like, this is no scratchier than that. If you have super sensitive skin, try using this after it’s soaked in a bowl or tub of hot(!) water for 10 min or so, with some emollient body wash like Aveenk.

title: Great, huge clip for the value.
text:
Indeed huge and clippy! I have a ton of hair—like waist-length, super thick coarse Asian hair (versus slippery shiny Asian hair)—and this holds everything. To maximize the clipping action I like to turn it after clipping so the spine faces to the side, not down the center—that way the teeth themselves get more gripping action. Turned to the side, it’s excellent for a casual French twist. Or just make a low poneytail and clip it up the center of your head, for the classic floppy piecey look.

My one gripe is that the spine isn’t as pretty as it could be. (And if you plan to wear it clipped down the middle, the spine is what people mostly see if they look at the back of your head.) The tortoise looks quite lovely—deep and dimensional—from the side. Not quite as gorgeous as my JCrew claw clips, but pretty good. But from the spine, you look through the “back” of the plastic piece so the tortoise colors are less defined and the finish is a bit less glossy. Also, I wish the metal was were a nice gold finish, like Jcrew’s. But for the price it’s pretty great still.

text:
I received this for Xmas (it was on my wishlist). I used my previous Norelco cordless for the past 7+ years with no complaints. I figure the blades are getting dull and had to put something on my wish list so........

One difference from the old to this one: Weight. The actual razor is quite a bit lighter. Not that the old one was that heavy, but there is a difference. Also, the back side of the razor is no longer flat. Must be for ergonomic reasons.

A huge difference is the sound/noise level. The old one you could tell the difference from when it was fully charged versus when it was near the end of it's charge. There was a definite slow-down. The new one, you can barely tell that it's on. Is this normal? I mean, it sounds very anemic, like it's already running out of charge, and I gave it a full overnight 8 hour charge.

As far as shaving goes, it's good, but not a miracle worker. You still have to make a few passes over an area to get all of it clean.

Overall, I'm going to give it a few more weeks to see if I really like it. I will withhold giving it 5 stars until then. I think this was $40 or something at Target.

title: Platinum DZ956F8 Is my unit
text:
I like my steam shower. I agree with many of the prior comments...it is EXTREMEMLY difficult to install as there are virtually NO directions...a weird diagram that's IT....then there is NO operations manual...I STILL can't figure out the aromatherapy after 10 months! The stools are good only to place foot on to shave legs...too small to sit. The 2 person unit is good for ONE. You cannot operate all the water at the same time...I have HUGE water pressure, so that's not an issue...it's the manufacturing. The rain shower will not operate at the same time as the jets (jets have VERY little power...no "jet" there....) Then the cleaning is very difficult...yes, the wooden floor is VERY heavy and has to be caulk-eyed to remove, without hitting any of the plastic handles, or glass....once removed, it has to be scrubbed and it is gross. Then the plastic floor underneath is bad too. I do it once a week (I won't allow my house keeper to touch...too gross to hand to her) and it does NOT smell BUT I had to remove the drain catch...that would just stop up drainage the minute the floor was put on, due to the weight of the floor...the drain catch turned into a water stop which would flood out of the shower onto the floor........so totally removed that....and it drains fine....hence why mine doesn't smell...there is no standing water in the bottom under the wood. The issue is the wood catches everything...soap scum and hair....and that is a chore to clean. is it worth it? YES. Would I buy another? YES...but I'd consider a different style...larger....the 2 person is still cramped...it's too narrow to be comfy or I'd build a shower from stone 5'x5' next with a floor drain. But the music and lights and the rain shower are WONDERFUL. The steam cleaner nozzle fell off mine...seemed like it blew up...no one had used the shower in 12 hours...it just blew off the wall and hit the door....so go figure - company sending free replacement...no explanation. We had problems with the door for months after installation...didn't seal properly...we had to alter the seal and it works fine now.
It took a plumber a LONG time to figure it out and many calls to company to get it installed. It's not easy....even with licensed pro's....so expect to PAY.

For the price....and headaches of installation and the crampedness....I'd consider a custom shower first....I do enjoy this shower but it was a disappointment from what I expected. I expected to use REAL jets and rain shower at same time, or Jets and hand held...or rain shower and hand held...as it's supposed to be TWO person....but 2 people have to take turns in center of shower to get any water.....NOT two person.

title: MY NEW "HOLY GRAIL" OF HAIR CARE PRODUCTS!
text:
My hair had gotten frizzy over the summer. I didn't realize that my bike helmet was damaging my hair. I'm constantly trying different shampoos, but honestly, the stuff at the salon seems grotesquely expensive, and I hate the scent of most of the products.

This stuff is basically unscented. It's not without an odor but it isn't perfumed. And the smell goes away quickly. I wanted to try out the variety of products, so I got the set.

The "0" stuff seems like water to me. The full-sized version is now sold in a spray bottle. Applying through the little applicator bottle is a big mess. But I did it.

After 10 min., I added the #3 stuff and put on a shower cap for about 20 min. while I used my exercise bike. Then I showered, using the #4 shampoo and #5 conditioner. THE SHAMPOO IS AMAZINGLY CONCENTRATED! After using it, I wasn't deterred by the high price. Two teaspoons was more than enough for my medium-thick shoulder-length hair. Liked the conditioner, too.

I followed the whole regimen and used the "mask" after towel drying my hair. Rinsed. It was great. Not exactly magical, but my damaged hair felt smoother. (Note: It would be easy to use too much of the conditioner and other treatments, including the leave-in stuff.)

I watched some of the videos about the product line and decided to buy almost the entire line. I bought the #4 shampoo as well as the #4C, the oil, a couple of things called "serum" which may or may not be magical in the winter. I bought a silky-cap to protect my hair from my bike helmet, and, per various articles I found online, I'll put on a generous amount of one of the leave-in conditioners before biking.

Hope this helps!

text:
Here's the thing: these are SUCH a pain to take off from the little paper they come on. And they are SO FRAGILE. Cut the decal, peel the shiny layer off, wet the decal then carefully peel the decal from the paper without the decal ripping. All of which doesn't sound so bad, however I dont see how any off this is possible with freshly cured gel polish (before top coat) or regular polish for that matter. So like any sane person, I prepped these little butterflies before hand...meaning I did alllll that, had them ready to be layed on the nail. But by the time I had painted and cured (all of what, 7 minutes max?) the little butterflies were dried up and shriveled. I dont know how else to describe it: they literally shriveled up. So! In my stubbornness I managed to unshrivel them, moisten them a bit and then lay them on the nail. And then when placing, a little piece of the wing broke off AFTER it was cured with the gel polish (so if I removed the decal the gel coat is dented/smudged/ruined). And then! Somehow, even after curing quality gel top coat, after a few days bits and pieces of the decal got rubbed off. Not even sure how.

Just don't buy these. Not, NOT worth it.

title: Salon eyebrow-tinting is now a thing of the past
text:
I have brown hair but was born with naturally light and sparse eyebrows. I used to spend obscene amounts of money getting my brows done for up to $20 at the salon (oftentimes they didn't get it as dark as I wanted), but since purchasing this product I haven't been back! Since I know how I like my brows better than any esthetician would, I apply the dye as I would fill in my brows with a pencil or eyeshadow. I let the dye sit for about 2-3 minutes, then wipe it off with a rag (caution: the dye DOES stain rags!). The dye is inevitably on my skin for a day or 2, but since I fill in only where I'd actually put makeup, it's like I have makeup on and they actually look fuller (just use caution when applying). The box comes with at least 20 or so capsules of dye (which are the hardest to open without getting powder in my sink), so that means I can literally dye my brows 20 different times. The dye lasts about 2 weeks at a time. Overall, if you have lightly-colored eyebrows and want them to be darker, I highly recommend this. It's saved me time, money, and hassle!

I attached 2 photos to this review: Picture #1 is my natural brows, before dying, and picture #2 is shortly after dying, with my brows brushed upwards with some drugstore brow gel. The first is taken with my iPhone and 2nd picture with my Canon DSLR, but the sparsity of my natural eyebrows should definitely be apparent in the first photo despite the lower-quality.

text: I decided to give this a try on a whim, I'm glad I did. NOW, if you are looking for something soft or thick, or warm colors, THIS IS NOT IT. It is long and very light weight. It is a Nylon Washcloth I believe made in Japan. This cloth reminds me of a loofah, which I don't mind. You must keep your body wet, when you soap the cloth up you only have to do that once it holds the soap very well. Don't keep it near the water as you wash or it will rinse right away. It is supposed to be very hygienic and durable. So far for me it has proven that. Once you get the feel of it you will know how delicate you need to be on your skin. Extremely delicate on your face and private areas but I am very happy with this cloth. After you rinse it and ring it out just hang it up and it will be dry in no time. I don't use it everyday because it is exfoliating your skin. After using it my skin feels rejuvenated and I do feel clean. Like I said before it is long so you can do your back your feet, everywhere in one swoop. You receive three cloths in one outer bag and they are wrapped individually, the colors that I received were blue, yellow and pink I didn't see any other colors. This is not going to be for everyone, I have very sensitive skin so I take my time when using it. I definitely would not recommend using this on young children it's not a smooth cloth but I'm satisfied with its performance.

title: Grab this gem while you can!
text: This fantastic brush was discontinued from ELF's product line...you can't order it from them any more. But this brush is the real deal. A little known fact about retail...discontinued products aren't usually destroyed. There is a completely legal secondary market for discontinued goods (especially ones that can't expire). Retailers decide to discontinue a low-selling product. They may put it on sale for a while, but usually not very long and Retailers with low price points may not mark it down at all. After a decided date, they gather any remaining inventory and sell it to sellers in the secondary market, who can often find customers for it who may not be the usual company shopper or they're more willing to take a smaller profit margin per unit. Either way, if this brush looks good for you, don't wait. I'm glad I didn't. I haven't seen anything else like it on the market for subtle contouring on small faces. This brush has ELF's usual great quality and super soft bristles that have just the right density to blend a soft contour in the hollow of the cheek, up near the jaw where a soft contour should go if you don't want to look like you have on tan stripes up close. I am so happy I found it.

The silk is quite sheer but strong (you can apply 2 layers, allowing proper drying time in between). Once you cut it, it will fray a bit so make sure to cut a large enough piece. Apply a drop of glue on the area to be mended & place the silk on top (its way easier to use tweezers for this); pat down with orange stick. Once dry trim away excess wrap with nail scissors & apply additional glue to cover. Allow to dry completely before filing/buffing. One thing to remember: do not touch the glue while it's wet...it's not called 'Stick It' for nothing!

title: Holds great, doesn't rip hair with this trick
text:
I bought these a week ago. They really do hold hair much, much better than anything else. The first two times I tried to remove them, they ripped my hair out and I almost gave up. Then I tried doing an extra little step during removal which made all the difference.

Before removing, grasp hair above the Bandz (basically as close to scalp as you can) and hold it (like you would when putting a ponytail barrette in). Roll the Bandz down one time. Then, you can wrap your fingers around all of your hair above the Bandz and continue to roll the the thing down. I've been doing it this way and haven't had any hair come out with them. Right now, these are my favorite ponytailers (and they don't make my head hurt like the regular ponytail elastics do from being too tight).

I’d say longevity is moderate, and I don’t really notice it on clothing day-after, though I’m not trying to directly spray onto clothing. I kinda feel like it’s something good for spraying onto torso area since that’s definitely a place of warmth to maybe kick this into gear and get it to waft a little. title: My whole family loves Organic Sprouts!
text:
I originally bought smaller bottles of Original Sprout at a specialty kids salon, but loved it so much for the entire family that we needed larger sizes. These bottles are the salon size they have at the shampoo sinks, so they will last quite a while. Also the product seems to be the same as the stuff I bought at the salon and at a better value/ounce.

If you’ve never tried Original Sprout, I recommend it. The products have a light, clean smell. The shampoo takes a little more than I’m used to just because it doesn’t foam (because it doesn’t use sulphates and other stuff that dries out the hair). So it’s just hard to spread through the hair is really why it takes more. The shampoo also doesn’t leave build up over time, like a lot of “gentle” formulas tend to do. The conditioner is fantastic! It doesn’t weigh down my toddlers’ super fine hair, and I haven’t had any greasy spots from it not rinsing out all the way - which sometimes happens with heavier products + wiggly toddlers. But the conditioner also works perfectly for my super long hair. I typically don’t even use leave in conditioner anymore, whereas I used to almost daily with various other brands. My recommendation is to just try this stuff!

title: Well Made Front Lace Braided Wig
text: Ordered 18 in braided on Nov 22, 2018 and it was available for pick up at Amazon Locker in less than 24 hours. I was impressed and excited about the purchase of my first lace front wig. Wig was nicely made. I removed the combs and added a 1 and a half inch piece of elastic from ear to ear to keep wig tightly secured in place. I watched you tube videos on how to install and followed the directions by using a stocking cap sprayed with Got2B glue freeze spray from ear to ear in front until completely dry, then I used a seam ripper to cut off excess stocking cap. Then I put a coat of the clear gel, Got2B glue (black container) on edge from ear to ear. I let it dry a few minutes until tacky before attaching the lace front to the glue, while brushing the baby hair toward my eyes. You must work kind of fast to shape your baby hair into the desired pattern because glue dry fast. I added glue as needed and then tied it down with a scarf until completely dry and hard at the touch. To finish off, I sprayed alcohol over the front and baby hair and used a cheese cloth to clean up dry gel from face and hair. I saturate front of wig with alcohol to remove from head and clean off gel from baby hair. I paid less than $60 and received many complements and shock when I tell people its a wig . I have been able to style the hair in many ways and keep it in tact for 3-4 days. I would purchase from this company again. You will not be disappointed.

This just gives me that more pulled together brow look when I want to ramp things up and I'm wearing fuller makeup. It could give someone with barely the brows a genuine microbladed look with practice.

I don't know why, but maybe I'm allergic to something in them? It has really dried out my face to a painful extent, and my skin is red and flaky. I don't even know how to fix my skin from this because it hurts to put any products on it. I wish I knew more about skincare for this exact reason, but hopefully my skin recovers after a few days of not using this product.

Original review: I am definitely a beginner when it comes to skincare, so I like this pack because it tells you exactly how to use the products (bottle 1 goes on in the morning, and you use bottles 2 and 3 at night). That makes it a really easy way for me to start getting acquainted with skincare. All three bottles have a pump top, and the texture of the liquid is kind of thicker than I thought it would be, like aloe or shampoo instead of oil or water consistency. That makes it easier to get it from the bottle to my face, at least for me. Now, the smells of these products are very strange/slightly on the unpleasant side. Like I would be a lot more happy putting a better-smelling or scent-free product on my face than these. I can't exactly describe what the smell is, but it's just something I don't like. Oh well. It takes about four pumps of each one to cover my face entirely, and it does leave my skin feeling refreshed and smooth. They all dry without any greasy or sticky feeling, which is a huge plus. I can't exactly be sure if they're working, since I'm not a skincare expert, but they definitely feel hydrating at the very least.

title: Removes about 30-40% of blackheads and smoothens the skin
text:
I heard about this type of black cleansing Japanese masks from different sources and saw some youtube videos people trying it out and saying that it hurts, but works and some saying that it does nothing and got very curious to try this out myself. My skin is medium type in pretty much all senses. Its not dry, not oily, I have very little acne and some blackheads, so trying this out I don't expect massive results either.

Firstly, I felt a bit weird when it arrived with no instructions at all in the box and the instructions written on the box are not in English. So, not knowing how long should I keep first couple of times I kept the mask for about 15-20 minutes. I put a relatively thin layer and it got dry pretty quickly. I felt no pain at all taking it out and had very little effect if any at all in a sense of getting rid of blackheads. The main struggle with the mask is that you are not sure how much to put to keep it "whole" on your face, so that you can peel it later, but I feel like no matter how thin the layer is, and sometimes it might seem it gets disconnected, but actually it will be peeling off altogether.

Another thing is that after listening to all these scary reviews, I was worried to try out on all of my face, so first few times I put some only on my nose. I only have blackheads on my nose. The effect was there, but very weak (I kept about 15 mins).

Today I decided to try it out for all my face and keep it longer. I shall say, that my pain tolerance is higher than average. This time I understood why people were complaining about pain, but still I would definitely say that it is very much tolerable pain, and nothing even close to extreme. In a scale from 1 to 10, where one is a touch and 10 is a bee sting, it would be a 2,5. But this time again the results were not super massive, but better than I expected to see (after first few times my expectations went down). I feel like it handled maybe around 30-40 percent of the blackheads, but also made my skin softer and smoother. Also while applying you should be careful not to put any on your hair or eyebrows, since you might have them removed with the mask. :)

Overall, though there are no super extra massive effects, considering the low price, I would recommend people to try it out!

text: These just don't work well... In theory, I LOVE them, but the acetone evaporates before gel polish will dissolve... I'd buy the silicone "Soakies" instead and see if those do a better job at preventing the evaporation. I haven't used these on regular nail polish because it comes off so easily anyway... so, If they don't last long enough to dissolve gels, I can't endorse them... I also tried wrapping the fingers in foils and using a regular thick cotton round ( both cut and folded). Still, the acetone evaporated before the gel was coming off... and the very thin pads included wouldn't work AT ALL... I even took a bottle of acetone, warmed it (carefully) in a pan of hot water & soaked cotton pads, wrapped fingers in foils & continually re-wetted with additional acetone... THAT finally worked, but by that point, I could have just done it without the clips. And, for self-use they are less than worthless... trying to get them on and keep working is comedic. Everything else is great. I was skeptical that the USB charging would work, but the mirror charges very quickly with the provided cable. If you happen to lose the cable, it's a typical micro-USB that will work with most other products. The light is activated by touching the bottom icon on the mirror itself, and I was surprised how responsive it was for a product this cheap (you have to firmly press it, but it doesn't take a ton of pressure, and there's no risk of accidentally turning it on by brushing it). You can also adjust the brightness, which is really nice. The bottom tray underneath holds a decent amount, but considering how lightweight and nicely portable this mirror is, I would recommend you hold put light objects in the tray to take advantage of how portable this is.

text:
For what I paid, I am pretty happy with the purchase. A few of the labels on the brushes were mislabeled or mixed up, but that's not a big deal unless you don't know the difference between a fan brush and an eyeshadow brush. :)

There was indeed a strong chemical smell/mothball smell. It was more prominent on the case than on the brushes. I had planned on washing the brushes with a brush cleaner anyway before using them, and would have washed them even if there was no smell, but after washing them the smell wasn't noticeable on the brushes at all. The case, however, was much more pungent than the brushes and I'm not sure how to make the smell go away. I'm taking the product page's advice to air it out, and we'll see how it works, but if anything I'll probably just end up wiping the case down with cleaning wipes to cover up the smell.

The bristles on the brushes I received were not falling out and none of the handles were loose. While washing them, I did tug on the bristles and none fell out at all. There were some stray bristles/bristles that were longer than the others, but it was no big deal. I had to trim them, so that's a very easy fix.
No, there isn't a brush for every occasion, nor did I expect every kind of makeup brush known to man in the set. Look at the photos if you want to know what brushes are included in the set. This is a good "basics" set. I purchased it solely to replace some of my everyday brushes that have seen much better days, and I don't like spending a lot of money on brushes from big brand-name companies, I'd rather save my money for good makeup products.
I've used some of the brushes and they get the job done. The pony hair and face brushes pick up product very well, so I'm happy.

All in all, for such a reasonable price, this was a worthwhile purchase.

title: My new favorite wig. Great if you have a big head.
text:
This arrived a day sooner than expected, in less than a week! I am so happy with it. It is the second lace front I have bought. My first was also from Amazon, but it had a middle part and was completely straight and very long. It looked pretty, but it wasn't right for me, and tangled so so much. I realized I needed something closer to my preferred look when I have long hair, with a side part (I buzzed my real hair recently to remove bleach-damaged hair and a cut I didn't like).

PROS: This has the perfect round-brush blowout look, and the hair itself is a mix of dark purple and dark brown, very cool and subtle. The layering is PERFECT, and the hairs are soft but realistic, with a slight kink that keeps it from looking too fake (although I still chose to mist it with some dry shampoo to tone down the shine a bit). Most importantly it DOES NOT TANGLE. All the wigs I have tangle SO much and its the one thing I can not stand about wigs. It also fits my head really well. I have a big head and usually have to do some fiddling with wig caps and lace to get it to fit right and not squeeze my head too much, but I practically just popped this on and was good to go, no glue/tape needed!

CON: It sheds. I cut it a little around the hairline to make the all-important baby hairs, and later when I brushed it I thought I was just brushing out the long hairs I had cut, but the more I brushed it the more I saw hairs were falling out around the whole wig. This doesn't bother me too much, as long as not too much comes out. Overall, I love this wig and I intend to buy it again in other colors.

EDIT: I took this on vacation soon after receiving it. I wore it every single day of my trip and it looks so great in my vacay pics and random people would compliment the purple highlights.

[[VIDEOID:e7a30e00ac346d7528a89979e60ae651]] This curler is big in size compared to most classic curlers. That doesn't stop us from using it in our house though! It does come in a variety of colors and I chose pink because it is my favorite color. It just takes a couple of minutes for the curler to get hot and the best part about that is you can control how hot you want it. The curler has a nice display to show you what the temperature is and there is a nice on/off sliding switch to it as well. The other buttons on the handle are for the temperature settings, curl direction, and the time setting. The curl direction is pretty flipping neat as you can control which direction it will curl your hair. You can have it make your curls go right, left, or set it to auto curl. The time setting is pretty easy to figure out, it controls how long you want the curler to actually hold the hair and how much of a curl you want. You can set it to hold the strand of hair that you are curling up to 15 seconds. You hold the blacker part toward your head when you are curling and you can start anywhere you want to. If you want more of a curl, you will go closer to the base of the strand. If you don't want a lot of curl, then you can start in the middle. It is pretty simple to use, all you have to do is slide the strand of hair into the curler and clamp it down. It will automatically gather the strand on the inside of the curler and set the curl. It is quite an amazing little gadget! You always want to make sure you are using a type of heat protectant on your hair to keep it healthy. The other thing is that it will automatically shut off after non use but always try to remember to unplug your stylers. I honestly wasn't sure what to expect but now I am going to have to fight with my daughter to use it!

text:
This review is for "Herbs Botanica Alum Powder Alumbre Potassium Alum Fitkari Fatkari For Skin." It asks for a star rating for "flavor" but the packaging specifically says you aren't supposed to consume this product orally so I have no idea how good it tastes.

The weather? I have no idea. That's the trouble with reviewing a product like this - if it doesn't work, is it the product's fault or is it user error - did I measure something wrong, does it just not work well when it's cold out? I have no idea.

So I decided to give it 3 stars - average. Because it does appear to be alum powder, but it being inside a plastic bag instead of another plastic bag seemed stupid and wasteful, and it didn't work for my purposes but as I said I don't know if that was my fault or the product's fault. This was a fun sampler pack. I felt it was a little over priced. $20 would have been a better value. The box includes 12 different scents all individually packaged. The scents come on a towelette which is a really convenient was to sample the different scents on your skin to be sure when you make an investment & buy a full size bottle, the product reacts well with your body chemistry.

Many perfumes smell wonderful in the bottle but once sprayed onto my skin, they smell peppery or spicy. Not a single Pinrose scent smelled peppery once applied. I rubbed the towelette onto my wrists, inner elbows, all over the tops of both arms, on my chest, around my tummy, & the top of my hair.

The scents were all pretty short lived BUT!!!!! ....... This is not a eau de toillet! These are lightly scented towelettes. Same scents but made differently using different concentrations of each formula. Expect a SAMPLE from this package, not the full experience.

I liked most of the scents & the ones I didn't (just 2 or 3) I tossed & my bathroom got a little scent boost for a bit. No big deal :) Good products. Good packaging. I'd definitely trust this seller again & am now on the hunt to complete my Pinrose collection of preferred scents.

One thing I saw with using this cream regularly is that when I worked out I would not get red stretch marks anymore... I guess that could be explained by the fact that the skin was hydrated but I am not 100% sure. They have a few golden strands that didn't look tacky, and really made them pop. It took me about 10.5hrs to do them, because I did them myself, and it was my first time doing them. I was able to wear them for about 6wks, before they had to come out (this is through no fault of the product-- people are generally supposed to go 6-8wks with them, and my hair is pretty silky, so it doesn't hold braids well... after the 5th week, they started slipping down, and I had to randomly do touch-ups to keep them looking nice). The only criticism I have for this product, is that it would be nice If they came with a crochet hook, instead of random false lashes. I haven't used the false lashes, but I really needed that crochet hook. They aren't expensive (about $1.97, I think)- and your local beauty supply store should have them-- but it was an inconvenience to have to go out and get one. Also, the locs are really small and thin, so you have to braid your hair really small to pull the hair through the middle with the hook (which is the best method for these locs). You can also unwrap them a little and then re-wrap them around the braids, but they aren't as neat that way and also get fuzzier when you do that. Overall, I got tons of compliments on this style and I really loved how they looked on me. I only need 2 packs to do my whole head, and I have plenty left over! So, for the price, the quality, and the results, this product is definitely worth it!

title: Nice close shave
text:
I used to use a $20 rotary electric I bought from Wal-Mart, but after getting red-neck after every shave, I finally decided to upgrade. This shaver gets extremely close... similar, if not exactly like a Mach 3 Turbo shave. My neck still gets irritated, but I'm not going to blame that on the razor, but rather my own physiology. Besides, I haven't tried this one shaving gel I've heard about that's supposed to completely snuff out irritation. It's called Coochy Cream and it's designed for... well, you can probaby guess, so I've heard it makes for a really irritation-free shave.

This razor deserves a 5-star average. Every customer review I read that was less than 5 stars was because of stupid reasons... like the lotion button being placed strangely, an 8 hour charging time, or that it feels cheap. The lotion button is fine. Why should it matter if it feels cheap? Isn't the shave what counts? And I don't mind an 8-hour charging time, since even if I shave every day, there are at least 18 hours between my shaves. I wonder if the 8-hour charging time is too long because the one customer was letting his friends use it or something.

Anyways, this is a five-star razor. If you buy it and aren't satisfied, that's fine, but please don't give it unwarranted reviews based on really miniscule details.

title: Shifts beard length setting without warning
text:
My T980 does almost everything perfectly: it holds a charge for weeks; its vacuum reduces the number of trimmed hairs around the sink by about 70%; it feels wonderful and it works quickly.

However, my T980 does NOT stay at the level I set it at. If I don't firmly grip the length setting wheel it will jump from, say, a 5 to a 3 -- as it did this morning -- embarrassing me either by giving me a patchy trim or by forcing me to shorten my beard length.

This problem doesn't seem to be a result of the way I'm, say, holding the trimmer -- I used the [[ASIN:B0001HYL0M T765]] for four years without having this problem -- but rather a flaw in the trimmer itself. From these reviews, it seems like only a few of the T980s have this problem; still, you might want to try the [[ASIN:B000FED5D0 T780]], which doesn't seem to have this problem -- I wish I had.

Update 3/12/08: Make me look like a fool once, shame on me; make me look like a fool twice, shame on you.

I've used this trimmer about 12 times since writing this review, and by a combination of duct tape, a pinch grip, and a good deal of vigilance I had been able to avoid too many embarrassing shifts in beard length.

...until this morning, when it shifted silently from a 5 (Late Winter Academic Beard) to 3 (Peach Fuzz) in mid-shave. Two options: shave my entire beard to a 3, which is inappropriate for my face type, or look deranged because half of my face is at 5 and half is at 3.

I threw my T980 in the garbage ten minutes ago.

title: These Fun Rods Will Deliver Curls
text:
I've used these flexible curling rods several times now. First, I practiced wrapping my hair up a few times at home without waiting the required time to get the curls. (I was so excited to try it out when they arrived.) I also tried it with both wet and dry hair. The hair wrapping goes pretty quickly because there are no fasteners or clips to worry about. That was a key factor in my decision to try these. You just roll up the hair from the bottom up and then bend the long ends up over the curl to secure. And they do stay put, once you figure out which way to bend them. Wrap tightly and bend the tips over the hair closest to the scalp. There are a few videos on YouTube that can help show you how to wrap your hair using curling rods of any kind, if you want to see it in action.

The rods are long and have a nice, slightly grippy texture on the surface, which is good for gripping the hair a little. But it's not too grippy that it would prevent easy removal from the curled hair.

They have a bit of cushioning to them, too, which means there's a little bit of give to them when you curl. The cushioning is also handy if you sleep in them. In general, it's not great sleeping with stuff stuck to your head. I managed to avoid getting a headache when I slept in these, though, which surprised me.

The ends are covered with little caps that keep the wire inside, and they kind of pop out of the rods a little, but not off. You can easily pop them back into place without any problems.

There are 6 of each size/color in the pack (7 sizes!) and you can choose a differing variety every time you set your hair, for differing looks. I have shoulder length hair and liked the smaller ones for the shortest hair at the nape of the neck, and graduate to larger sizes toward the top of my head. But I have used larger ones all around as well. It depends what kinds of curls you're going for. You can also use larger or smaller sections of hair to wrap each rod, for more variations.

The design of the clear/blue carrying case was also a factor in my decision. I like the upright design, the little zipper cap, and the handle on top. It's compact for the quantity of rods it contains, which makes it easy to travel with, though the vertical design can be difficult for getting all the rods back in and fitting well. It helps to straighten out the rods before putting them back in the container. Not a big deal, just a small struggle if you're short on time.

I have gotten crazy curly results from these after sleeping in these the other night. I was so curly I didn't recognize myself in the mirror! These rods will deliver! The key is to wrap moistened, but not sopping wet hair, wrap tightly and consistently. Mind those pesky ends and make sure they are held under the hair in the right direction, and leave these rods in for several hours until the hair is all completely dry. Overnight is best, but I've seen results in just a couple hours with only slightly dampened hair.

I'm still learning how to best curl using these, but I'm very happy with my investment. I think you will enjoy playing with your hair using these.

I'll be honest - for the price, I wasn't expecting much. I bought this thinking that if the tool for cleaning under the toenails was usable and didn't snap off the first time I used it, I'd consider it a win.

title: Etched well with some minor issues
text:
These stamping plates are not the best quality in the areas of fine detail, but they are not the worst either. I used many different stampers and the firm stamper it comes with really worked the best. You can see this on the swatch sheet I did; the two boxed in areas were done with the stamper that came with it. I was pretty shocked it worked so well and did not need priming. So, I'm quite happy to add this stamper to my collection. The white stamper shown is the Uber Chic XL Non-Sticky stamper that usually picks up everything in great detail.
I tried using these plates with Wet N Wild black first, and not stamping polish, to see how well the images picked up. The detail did pick up well but I found that some of the plates had large areas that were etched next to really find detail areas so sometimes the card would get stuck. The metal scraper that came with the set was not helpful at all. It is metal and as I feared completely scratched the plate and got stuck in some of the large areas I mentioned. I just used a gift card like scraper and got better results.
This is also not a set from one manufacturer. It appears it’s a hodge podge of collection of plates and my set had a duplicate which is pictured below. Also, one plate was rusted under the blue film. I have not contacted the manufacturer about this.
I tried to go for the finest details on each plate for the swatch and for the life of me I could not get the suckers from the octopus to all come out. The blue portion of the swatch is Mundo de Unas stamping polish which did not even make that portion better.
Most of these plates stamped well though, you can see this on the swatch image. I was impressed that I was able to get the watermelon seeds with regular nail polish. I was however really dissapoined that one was damaged and I only received 9 distinct plates.
I received this product at a discount for a fair and honest review.

title: AWESOME FOR NAIL ART!
text:
I use this liquid latex for nail art and it is FANTASTIC!!!! Some of the things you want in a latex product for nail art are that it dries quickly, leaves no staining on the skin, spreads easily and comes off in one piece. Another good thing would be an indicator that it is dry. This liquid latex does ALL of that. The purple gets darker as it dries. It is dry in like a minute as long as you don't apply globs of it, it spreads like a thin polish and it does not stain the skin.

I got this for my nail art in white originally and the white did not change color much and it was a little confusing since it was applied around a white base coat at times. This is like 100 times better and my favorite color. :-)

Four ounces will last you forever if you're using it for nail art. I usually use a children’s medicine syringe to put this into an old polish bottle that closes well, if not your latex will dry up in the bottle. If the brush gets gunky, I just use a toothpick or an orange wood stick to remove the gunk and it leaves the brush like new. If you quickly wash the syringe with water, you will be able to use it again and again.

I will definitely be a lifer with this product for my nail art. Pictured below is the water and hairspray method and you can see how much polish this kept off of my skin! Love it!

title: GREAT FOR NAIL ART USE!
text:
I bought this for the purposes of nail art. I use it to cover my skin when I am nail stamping or water marbling. Let me tell you, it is excellent for this. I would probably go with another color in the future, but it works well and comes off in one piece. I cleaned out an old polish bottle and used a kiddie medicine syringe to fill the bottle with the latex. Works great.
Note, if the polish dries on it and you try to peel it away, the polish will flake off and still hang off of your design in pieces. Before removing, make sure to run a brush dipped in some acetone around the edge of where the latex meets your nail (careful not to run your design). This will ensure the excess polish comes up with the latex. It really has made clean up so much easier for me. Sometimes I want to skip using it and then I'm angry at my laziness because it takes me forever to clean up otherwise.

title: Excellent Product on Second Try
text: My first order of this product was returned because it did not meet my expectations based on the product description. However, I took a second chance, ordered it again and found it very helpful to soothe the severe radiation burns on my neck. Not only was it soothing to those very painful burns, but it absorbed into the skin and was not difficult to remove accumulations when further application was needed. It worked very well for this purpose, whereas I found Aquaphor too greasy and too difficult to remove. Other products I tried either did not soothe the pain or were difficult to clean off the skin to make fresh applications. Although expensive, Mannatch's Emprizone proved to be the most helpful product for those highly painful, severe radiation burns on my neck. Therefore, although I did not like it on my first try and returned that first tube, the second order turned actually out to be what I liked best of all the different products I tried. This experience has shown me that sometimes it pays to give a product a second chance. I now consider this a high-quality product and recommend it.

title: Actually lasts 2weeks+ better than regular dye
text: I NEVER write reviews but this one is so worth it since the reviews on this product are varying hopefully this can help someone decide. I have been doing my brows for almost 15 years, so I am very particular about them. I’ve tried almost every brow product, from pencils to pomade and even wonderbrow (which sucks don’t get it). I’ve also dyed my brows with regular hair dye before and stopped because it only lasted a few days and not worth the continuous effort. Well let me tell you this product is still on today and it’s been two weeks! It was quite dark the first few days and then I had to use my Anastasia dip brow pomade to lightly outline them but I only have to use like half the amount of product I normally do. My eyebrow hairs are very light naturally and my hair is dark, I’m so happy to say that they finally match! And it looks so natural, I could go without the pomade if I had to. One tip though, leave it on for 20 mins or more. I love that it’s individually packaged too, this will last me months. I wish I had before pictures so you can see how bad my natural brows are lol but I attached a pic of them right now on week 2 with some pomade and as you can see the actual hairs are still quite dark. (I’m growing them out right now so don’t hate on the strays) anyway sorry for the long review but if you’re like me then I’m sure you read all of them. There are no cons, I love everything about what this did and the longevity of it is amazing. Do yourself a favor and try this out, I would reccomend it to everyone who colors in their brows!

title: Darling, fun wig.
text:
Fabulous quality for an inexpensive, synthetic wig. I'm giving this wig 5 stars because it's so adorable, is of very nice quality and looks exactly as it does in the online picture. This is my first experience with a wig and I'm planning to just wear it on "bad hair days." I'm letting my hair grow back from a not-so-great hair cut and I don't do well with some of the awkward "stages" associated with growing one's hair out.

Before using, I gently washed the wig with a few drops of mild, shampoo in warm water, and followed that, in the same way, with the conditioner product that came with that shampoo. I gently soaked it again in clean warm water, as the conditioner is a rinse-out type, then wrapped it in a terry towel to blot out most of the water, after which it air dried it on an open construction wig stand. With super gentle handling, it came out looking perfect.

I like my hair to be more sleek and smooth than puffy and wispy, so I even finished the little wig's salon treatment with a tiny bit of my favorite coconut pomade smoothed on with my fingers. Worked like a charm and looks great!
A major plus for this wig is that it has never shed at all through washing and subsequent styling. Several other inexpensive synthetic wigs warn that they will shed at first, and they do. Key concept here is: for optimal effect, be gentle, especially when brushing.

One challenge is that, like a couple of similar wigs I tried but did not keep, the inner woven cap is too big for my head. So, I took a few hand stitches in the nape area of the inner cap to shorten the distance of the cap from the front hair line to the nape area. That's where the problem is for me. It worked because the wig's hair is not really very thick and the cap is made of a wide-weave, soft mesh in the back, allowing me to create a one-inch, horizontal tuck across the whole back, between where the cap meets the ears. Don't know how long this will hold up, but inexpensive wigs like this one are not expected to last for ever, anyway.

And, I'll just repeat that this wig's hair is actually rather thin, so that if the color of your own hair does not readily blend in well with the color of the wig (for example, light blonde wig over dark brown natural hair) you could find some dark hair showing through, especially in the back. Mine is close enough that I'm not experiencing this. So, it's all good and tons of fun!

title: Slow and painful, but it really does work.
text:
Ok, so this thing really works. Simple and permanent. Appears like it is just as good as professional electrolysis.
Now here's the catch. It is really, really slow and tedious. After cleaning and sterilizing the area with alcohol, and sterilizing the tip, I find a hair, carefully insert the tip, and it starts to work. I count to 20 and stop. Then I try to tweeze the hair, and usually it doesn't come out. So I try again for 15 seconds, and then it usually does come out. So averaging out prep time and zapping time, it is about a minute and a half per hair. (Count how many hairs in the area you want to zap, and do the math).
It also can be painful. Most hairs it is fine, but in sensitive areas like the lip it really hurts. If I rub ice on the area first, it is tolerable, but of course that takes even longer.
Overall I am pleased, especially for the price. If it breaks before I'm done with it, I will probably buy another one. But hopefully it will last long enough to do the small areas I need to do.

title: Well made, quality built antenna
text:
First, let me say that I was under no illusions as to what this antenna could or couldn't do.

On with the brief review:

After viewing a ton of YouTube videos on various MLA's I figured that I would home brew one myself. A month after that, and after acquiring only a few of the items necessary I figured it would take months to get this done (that's how things are at this moment, so when Chameleon antenna ran a big sale on the P-loop (<$350) I jumped on the deal! Less than a week later it arrived and I threw it up on it's selfie-stick mount and plugged in my antenna analyzer. Tuning was easy and the bandwidth, while small, wasn't really as bad as I thought it would be during operation and tune-retune. Note: I didn't try to make a perfectly round loop, nor did I get scientific about where to put the aluminum loop. I just eye-balled it. My initial testing was on receive using my FT-817. I noticed a tremendous difference in signals received compared against other indoor antennas I've tried. Today I made a 1500 mi. contact with 0 sunspots while using this antenna indoors, and in the middle of the room, and I am happy about that!

Things I like:
1. It's easy to put up and/or take down
2. Very portable. Everything fits into the canvas bag it came with.
3. It's pretty much a no-brainer to use.
4. Because of the nature of the loop it's very selective. What I mean by that is - by turning the antenna one way or the other it's easy to zero in on who you want to talk to while cutting out stations on nearby frequencies, or atmospheric noise.

Things I don't like:
1. As it comes, it will only take up to 25watts (SSB).
2. You can't tune it or rotate it remotely. This means the antenna has to be close enough to re-tune when changing bands or frequencies

(I do remember seeing a remote tuner/rotator on their website before, but apparently it's no longer being made/sold.)

For field day or other portable communications I think this would be ideal, and I plan to use it outdoors before it gets too hot in Texas. If I could put up something outside I would have gone a different route, but things being the way they are, the best antenna for me to use is the P-Loop. For a good loop comparison do a search for OH8STN on YouTube. He does a good job of reviewing this stuff. I knocked off 1-star for lacking remote tuning ability.

title: Not 100% Human Hair, but decent quality
text:
Things to note: I waited 5 months to review the hair so I could give a fully informed review. I've colored, curled, cut, styled, washed, deep conditioned, blow dryed, you name it! Here's my review:

Pros-
• Affordable hair, 30+ inches will definitely cost more elsewhere, upwards of $350
• Takes coloring very well initially, I've only used watercolor meathod on any of my 613 hair.
• Straightens without much effort
• Holds curl but ONLY with flexi rods and mousse applied
• True to length with no odor or bugs after inspection
• Hair retained similar quality after being washed with swimmers shampoo (to remove gold tone/clean hair).

Cons-
• After 2-3 months of consistent wear, brushing and styling (Heat used sparingly, always with heat protectant) hair sheds uncontrollably. We're talking hair all 9ver every place I've stepped foot inside of.
• Hair will not hold heated curls, they fall within minutes
• Hair tangles and matts fairly easily in the nape
• Tons of split ends resulting in stragly looking hairs everywhere
• This is NOT 100% human hair, it is mixed with synthetic fibers, (I did do the burn test to confirm my suspicions).

Overall if you are looking for something cheap and quick with minimal styling, this is it..
If you want an investment, hair you'll be able to revive and re-wear for a few months, baby, this ain't it. I'd recommend this hair for an event but not for a unit/ like in you want to get the most out of. Hair performed as expected for the price.

title: I love it!
text: I've tried multiple magnetic lashes in the past (upper/lower magnetic pairs, and magnetic liners) but the magnets can always be seen and not at all easy to apply. HOWEVER, 1 year later, here comes this product. They have figured it out and perfected it! I read all comments and reviews before purchasing and discovered all are true. Here are my lessons: 1st: make sure you apply your mascara before or after applying the magnetic liner. I didn't do that and ended up pulling the magnetic lashes off with the mascara brush. 2nd: Fit the lash you want to use to your eye. You'll want to see where to start it and end it. 3rd: Shake and apply the liner ONLY to the length and desired placement on your lash line. Make sure to apply liner as close to your lash line as humanly possible. If you lay down a thick line, you'll regret it because the lashes will have a large area to stick, then you won't be able to move them down to your lashline without stripping the liner off. You'll have a noticeable gap between your lashes and the magnetic lashes. 4th: WAIT until the liner is COMPLETELY DRY. It's a much better application! 5th: The kit comes with an applicator, but it's METAL! If you get too close to the magnets, it'll stick to the applicator and then you'll either disrupt your liner and have to reapply, or you'll just get frustrated. I have a plastic applicator already, so I used that. Lastly, I finished lining my eyes with my regular black eyeliner. Once I figured these things out - POW - dramatic and TIGHT lashes. I cant be more happy.

title: Excellent source of food quality (i.e., edible) cocoa butter
text:
As I learn more about chocolate and becoming an amateur chocolatier, I found out about this product.

Women (and men) have been using cocoa butter to soften their skin and it's used in some expensive soaps and shampoos -- but you can't eat that stuff!!!

Expensive Belgian and French chocolate (used by world class pastry chefs) are developed with at least 12% more of cocoa butter than normally available.

These chocolates are also more refined and are called couverture chocolate - google it :-)

I use NOW Cocoa Butter for cooking, to increase the fat content of (cheaper American) semi-sweet dark chocolate.

I put in 20 oz of Ghirardelli Semi-Sweet 60% Cacao in a double boiler and add 1.3 oz of NOW cocoa butter and it all melts nicely together.

I then temper (google this too) this "couverture'd" chocolate to dip the hand piped ganache portion of truffles.

title: Tiny plastic covers on the bristles make it more comfortable for some cats
text:
We have three cats with three very different coats. The black cat's coat is sleek, shiny, and seems to have fine little hairs. He barely sheds, and his hairs are short. He loves being brushed with just about any brush, for the interaction, the petting/grooming connection and the scratching action. However, he doesn't really need to be brushed.
Our medium-to-long haired snowshoe Siamese seems to have sensitive skin; she Hates being brushed near her achy back hips, and will complain and whip around to smack at you if you brush her very hard at all. However, she sheds a TON, and needs to be brushed almost every day, so she doesn't get clumps by her arthritic haunches (she actually gets dandruff flakes that her hair clumps around and knots up). She is at least 14 years old (we're not exactly sure), and just can't reach to groom her back end well, any longer. She loves being brushed around her head and neck though, even with our old "scratchier" long-tined brush. You can fill that brush 2-3 times easily, brushing her for just a few minutes, every day. This one, because of the tiny soft covers on the ends of the tines, doesn't seem to dig at her as much, and you don't have to brush her nearly as gently - meaning that you get far more of the clumps out when they are small and just beginning to build.
Our orange cat has extremely soft, short-to-medium hair, and you hardly notice that she sheds much. But when you brush her with the longer-tined, flexible but sharper-ended bristles of our old brush, you fill up the brush surprisingly quickly, and she lets you brush all over. So, she may be the only one that we continue to use the old brush on.
Our old brush sort of pulls the bristles into it, towards the handle, when you push the button on the back of it, to clean it off. The bristles disappear inside the brush, and you can peel the hair off like a little blanket and throw it away.
With this new brush, it is more like the flat base with holes around the bristle seats, comes forward, to the end of the bristles; when you push the button on the back, it pushes that base away from the handle. This may end up bending the bristles less, and keeping the brush usable longer. But it also doesn't compact the hair and make it just "peel off" in one fell swoop. It is more likely that you will leave some hair behind on the brush with this one. It is Worth the trade-off of it being slightly less easy to clean well, because our older, sensitive cat likes it soooo much better, and she is the one who really needs to be brushed the most. This brush is lighter, and feels less substantial than our old brush. Again, we will keep the old brush for the kitten. But this new one is perfect for Sagwa (the old cat), and I am very glad we tried it. If it does crack or bristles break off, because it seems less sturdy, I would buy another one just to keep her happy.

Everyone reccommends a certain $40 razor butthe best one I have had is the dirt cheap Viking Jr butterfly top. Bought because I couldnt afford expensive razors and it is the best shave with great construction compared to cheaper brands butterfly razors. It's not about spending money for a a good shave, it's about the right equipement. I finally got a good brush and stand too because the one I got years ago on here was STILL losing hairs. What a difference. Better lather, better shave, and I just wish I could afford the Proraso pre shave, never tried aftershave but seems like another money pit just like $50 razors or the expensive soaps that do the same thing. I'll try Taylor of bond street some day but I don't trust reviews anymore. I need a fatty shave soap for my skin, last I used theHare brand with Tallow and it was great. This was cheaper I think but also great. I use blades once or twice an recycle, but Astra is nice and getting super cheap. Would never pay for Feather but maybe they are better, I just want a good cheap reliable shave.
Been using safety razors since like 2014 and took my until recently to realize:
1)Fat based creams are best for my skin, I thought I was just destined to get red bumps on my neck forever but they do not happen now.

2) Preshave is more important than post shave, I started wth tallow soap so IDK what made the difference but cheap preshave makes my face feel great after shaving.

3) more$$ doesnt mean better razor or better shave soap. Reviews clear indication: Viking sells so many expensive razors but I will never buy another again after the $17 one. People say 34C or whatever is best first razor, but nope I am fine with my less aggressive cheap, well built razor. My last/first one cost$50 and the threads wore out. No thanks.

4) IDK figure out yourself. Crazy my shave is PERFECT with tallow, wool fat, fat fat fat. I used water based brands before and INSTANT improvement when I used tallow. This stuff is just as good and will buy again for the price (seems to last forever too). I will buy this exact one when I run out most likely

5) spend more if you want, but dont expect a better shave. When I have money again I will buy 3 Viking Jr razors in case I break or lose mine, some may disagree but no matter what FIND WHAT WORKS

6) Also, the shave bowl, stand, and brush make a difference, wish I knew how HORRIBLE my brush and set up was. I had a wood stand that would leave stains and couldnt handle getting wet. This time I bought a brush+stand combo and both are fantastic. After 6+ years of finding hairs in my soap from old brush I found a few at the start (they all lose a couple) then haven't had to pull hairs out since. I think it's synthetic badger too, but works great. Or maybe my old one was synthetic. IDK but this about the wool fat and this was a great buy with my little metal shave bowl (also cheap and IMO good investment and looks nice)

But yeah this is some good shave soap! Coming from a picky shaver. Crazy how I spend less money and get a better shave... seriously better stock up on those viking razors because I tried other brand butterflys, they worked but were cheaply constructed and the Viking is perfection. I thought butterfly=bad. And expensive crap = good. Wool fat puck fit perfectly in my cheap stainless bowl, get a bowl, try something like this (vegans try with some oil to replace tallow/fat) and try other stuff too. Just dont think that you need that one super expensive brand and 10 products for a good shave.

title: Thicc enough to fool my own mother 🤔
text:
Still getting the hang of how to properly apply this, and get my parting juuust right so it will all fit on my head.

I was skeptical at first because it was synthetic hair...but I wanted to try it out and wow! I received nothing but compliments while wearing it! I was afraid of it being able to pass, from how shiny it was compared to my own hair (I'm black by the way haha), but it worked!

I love how wide it is near the middle, to simulate hair body, and the way it tapers at the end with a very slight curve.

I have to press my natural hair with heat in order for it to be straightened, so my hair texture is different from the wig--but applying some oil (Africa's Best-Ultimate Herbal Oil...which ironically, is made in America lol), really helped add shine to my own hair so it matched with the wig's shine.

My only gripe is my head seems to be a bit too small for all the clips to fit perfectly around its shape--but that may just be me getting that U shaped part all wrong haha So I'll keep working on that!!

Oh yeah, this wig is pretty weighty, but thank goodness the clips feel heavy duty-ish to handle it. They are definitely felt throughout the day while wearing, but once I get used to their tug, I should end up forgetting they're even in my hair.

Edit!: After a month + of use, I noticed the clips may have been pulling some hair from my scalp out and left it a little tender.

Overall, this half wig is fantastic for short term use. As for long term, a full headed wig is a lot less stress on my hair and my noggin.

And yes, the day my mother saw me wearing this half-wig in a braid, she thought it was my real hair. When I undid the braid and wore it as a straight ponytail, I thought ‘This is it. She’s going to notice how thick and straight it is and KNOW it’s not real.’

I spent the whole day waiting for a call out that never happened. She probably just thought I grew my hair out.

title: Questionable ingredients
text:
When I read the product page, it sounded like this foot cream had some of the same ingredients as some of my favorite lotions, so I thought it would help soften my rough, cracked feet. It wasn’t until the package arrived that I saw what was REALLY in this product, and I was NOT pleased. However, I was willing to give it a try.

Aside from the aloe, green tea leaf extract, water and coconut oil, many ingredients in this cream are kind gross or not helpful. The complete list is: urea, salicylic acid, deionized water, green tea leaf extract, coconut oil, dodecane, cetearyl alcohol, polysorbate 60, clyceryl stearate, PEG-100 stearate, cetyl alcohol, aloe barbadensis leaf juice, tea tree oil, glycerin, propylene glycol, carbomer, xanthan gum, ethylhexylglycerin caprylyl glycol, hexylene glycol, phenoxyethanol.

The gross part is the main ingredient: 40% urea—a major component of urine. Salicylic acid is used in wart-removing solutions because it exfoliates your skin. Dodecane is a chemical used in jet fuel which can cause skin, eye, and respiratory tract irritation. Alcohol dries out your skin. Xanthan gum is just a thickening agent made of corn. I am personally allergic to that and stearates. And the other chemicals are kind of sketchy, too.

I tried this stuff on my feet for a couple of weeks, applying before I went to bed and wearing socks to protect my sheets. I really didn’t see any significant change in the condition of my feet than when I apply regular alcohol-free lotion. It makes no sense to me that anyone would use this stuff so full of questionable chemicals, paying $27 for a little pot of this cream, when a regular bottle of lotion works just as good or better and goes for a fraction of the cost.

title: STICKY SITUATION
text:
When I first received the item I was pretty excited. Tried opening it out of the outer plastic bag, but it was sticky. I thought it might have been a leak, and sure enough the product had sticky goo all over the cardboard packaging. It was pretty bad even for a leak, so I examined it over the sink, but then realized the ENTIRE top half of the spirit gum adhesive bottle had broken off and half the glue was filling the clear plastic cover attached to the cardboard.

At this point I was worried about glass cuts but I tried to salvage what remained of the glue. Using a scissor, I tried extracting the glue remover so at least I can use it to clean up all the stickiness resulting from the sticky situation. When I cut the packaging open, all the glue started dripping out into the sink. Long story short, the glue got everywhere and it was a mess cleaning up because THE REMOVER DIDN'T WORK EITHER! As there was a lot of glue, I also applied the remover liberally, including pouring out enough to cover my hand and soaking a cloth to scrape with. I had to later resort to using citric acid using lemons and that seemed to work better but still tough to remove.

I considered buying a new one but at that point I really didn't think it was worth it given my experience. All in all it took maybe 2 hours to clean up, and to begin with I have an extreme dislike for sticky substances on my hands.

title: Recommend!
text:
First of all, picture is just for reference. The actual color under sunlight is very close the picture on the box (to me).
"Everything is Japanese in this box." Check a YouTube tutorial video before you place your order.
My original hair color is black. I have very healthy and soft hair. Didn't dye it perm for at least one and a half year.
Here are couple suggestions if you are interested in it and didn't use it before.
1. If your hair is longer than shoulder, buy two bottles. My hair is a bit over my shoulders and I finished the entire bottle.
2. If you want to trim your hair, dye it first and cut it later.
3. Don't wash hair for at least 2-3 days before you use the bubble foam dye.
4. Make sure to test if you're allergic to it at least 2 days before you use it.
5. Don't rinse your hair when you start applying the foam. Apply on dry hair directly.
6. After 20-30 mins, rinse with "just" water. Do it couple times until the water is all clean.
7. Apply some Vaseline on your forehead, ears, etc. So the color won't stay on your skin if you accidentally touch your skin. Wrap your ears is also recommended.
8. You will need color protect shampoo if you want to color stay on your hair longer.

Hope these help!

title: Is there really a blade in this thing?
text:
I'm sixty-four and have been using Norelco shavers all of my adult life. When I needed a new one, my wife wanted to get it for my birthday. I specified a Norelco Arcitec, mostly because its looks made it look light and handy, and I anticipated that I would get my usual Norelco shave.

Was I ever wrong. From day one, I had to check to be sure there were blades in this thing. It's like a kid's toy shaver--it buzzes and runs around over the stubble, but gets very little of it after several passes. I kid you not, I can go over the same spot 6-8 times and then test it with my finger tips and not notice any change. I generally shave during a one-hour commute. With the Arcitec, it takes me a half-hour to get the job done--and poorly. The Arcitec has a tiny capacity to hold shavings and when it fills up (half way through one shave) it shaves even worse. If I skip shaving for even one day, the Arcitec is essentially useless against my two-day stubble.

I have a really OLD Norelco Speedshaver that I bought at an estate sale as a backup. This thing was old when I bought it twenty years ago. The previous owner used it to shave her legs. It's a model number SC7830. It looks like a style from the 1940s or early 1950s. It doesn't even have an on-off switch. I have no idea how old the blades are in this thing but it shaves circles around my Arcitec. I now use it instead of my Arcitec, which I threw away. (And my wife complains that I never throw away anything.)

Edit: I just came back and read a couple of glowing reviews of this Norelco Arcitec shaver. One of them accused reviewers like me of being employed by the competition. Well, I'm not. Like I said, I've used Norelco shavers for 40+ years, and I most likely will again. After my experiences with this model, I think those who claim to love it must work for Norelco--or they have peach-fuzz for whiskers, maybe. I have to wonder if the Arcitec was designed by a Norelco employee who was about to quit and go to work for a Norelco competitor. This Norelco Arcitec was just a complete waste of money. I'm still using my backup Norelco Speedshaver from the 1940s or 1950s. It shaves. Maybe if you're very young and still have peach-fuzz whiskers, the Arcitec would work for you, I wouldn't know.
