title: Works quite well. KVD products are very good quality.
text:
I purchased the creme contour palette, Light/Shade, by Kat Von D. I use Bare Mineral Original powder foundation, which is considered a no-no with creme products. I'm told that with creme contour you should use liquid foundation, powder contour with powder foundation. I have an oily/combination, mature skin type. There is a learning curve to mixing the mediums, but the contour eventually tightens up and does not feel oily, and I needed the creme contour to offset my mature, dryer portions of my face. It is important to use a face primer. I also begin my eye makeup after contouring, to allow the creme to absorb and turn to a near powder form, so I can apply my powder foundation to control the build up. My skin is prone to absorbing color so I apply contour and blushes darker initially. What I really like about this contour product is that the oily portions of my skin do not look or feel as oily as it would had I not used it at all. I call that amazing.

I still might purchase the powder form of the contour at some point now since I am encroaching on the summertime Florida weather, but so far, even at the end of the day, my face is reacting well to this product. I highly recommend KVD Light/Shade creme contour. The compact is refillable and is a high impact plastic that is very substantial. I have already purchased other refills to trade out with what was provided in the compact. The white is a must for highlighting, and is not included in the compact. Buy, buy, Bye!

text: So far so good! I've been using the serum for about 3-1/2 weeks. I just placed and received my second order because I did not want to run out. So far I like the results. The results are subtle but progressive; I can definitely see and feel a difference in my skin tone and texture. The serum feels good going on and a little goes a long way. It is very light and refreshing - not sticky and it is not leaving a residue... My first container is not empty yet so I anticipate that one 30ml container lasts for at least 30 days. So I ordered more before I ran out so as not to have a gap in use. I use about 1-2 "squirts" once a day in the evening. The instructions state "drops" but that was hard to gauge... Anyway, it might also be helpful for me to note that when I started using this product I also made some other changes in my daily skin care routine. I was unhappy with some other products so I did a little research and decided to add a vitamin C serum to my routine. I also increased my water intake to about 60-70 oz. per day and started to take a phyto-ceramide supplement. I was already taking supplements of Vitamin E, Ester C, B Complex and Krill Oil which I continued to take. I also drink green tea and rooibos tea fairly regularly. I reduced my coffee to only one stiff cup in the morning (that was difficult). As far as topical applications I continue to use a mild cleanser followed by an alcohol-free, pore refining toner (both are Neutrogena). Then after the toner thoroughly dries (which takes like 5-10 min) I apply the Vitamin C serum and let that dry as well (dries quickly in 5-7 min). I then put on moisturizer that is targeted for the eye area and another for the rest of the face and neck (also Neutrogena). I make sure to use the SPF 30 "day" moisturizer and because I have some sun damage (brown patches), I also started to use a spot treatment for lighting (AlphaHydroxy-SpotLight) only every other day. I additionally use an exfoliator about 3 times a week with the spinning brush thingy (also Neutrogena). I make sure to use that before a shower and rinse it off while in the shower (the steam seems to help open the pores so everything else penetrates better after). The reason I do the whole routine in the evening is because of the little dry times and the mornings are a bit rushed for me... BUT... I think I may just give myself some extra "me time" in the AM and up my full routine to twice a day. Right now the morning is just cleanse and moisturize! I guess it would be about time anyway because I didn't want to go over board in the beginning with the additional stuff I added. I'm definitely not promoting any particular product here; I only mentioned the other stuff I'm using for reference and also because I'd tried the more expensive moisturizers and they were not any more effective at moisturizing than the one I'm using now. I know maybe it sounds like a lot of changes but actually, after the 1st few days, it just became part of daily habit. I really think the water is contributing significantly - although I do go to the bathroom more often; it's probably flushing my system and getting rid of toxins. I hope to see continued results. I am pleased with this serum and I'll come back with an update in another month.

text:
First, I bought this for what was left out of the ingredient list. I started occasionally painting my daughter's fingernails and wanted a safer way of removing the nailpolish, since I'm aware of the negative effects of the chemicals used in traditional nail polish removers.

As far as how this product works, I want to start by saying that I've been using a generic non acetone nail polish remover, so my comparison is with this type of nail polish remover and not an acetone or other "fast acting" one.

As recommended by other reviewers, I ignored the bottle's instructions for use and instead used like any other nail polish remover. Since I typically use a flat round cotton face pad, I kept with my normal method of covering the mouth of the bottle with the face pad, tipping the bottle over quickly to soak a circle into the pad, and then rubbing the pad over each nail until clean. I was surprised that not only did the polish come off just as easy as when compared to generic non acetone remover, but I didn't have to change the pad or add more remover to it for both hands! With non acetone remover I typically use both sides of 2 to 3 soaked pads to get all of the residue off, but I was able to use both sides of the same pad to remove the polish from all 10 of my fingernails and feel I could have started on my toes if I was going to change that polish too, though I doubt I would have gotten through those without at least a few more drops added to the pad.

BONUS:
1. This is very mild smelling!! It smells (to me) a little like black licorice, but the scent isn't overwhelming and definitely doesn't leave me dizzy or desiring fresh air like when I use the generic non acetone remover.
2. Doesn't weaken my nails. In fact, they feel a little stronger since switching to this type of remover!

I'm SO happy with my purchase and will keep coming back!

title: This smells so good!
text:
I am kind of in love with this soap! Charcoal is definitely in there! The soap itself is not 100% natural. Not with the perfumey scent.

Oddly enough it is the perfumey scent that draws me to the soap. It reminds me of a perfume that I remember having in the late 70's or early 80's. I have been racking my head for a week trying to place the scent. I just really love that scent!

It is a very smooth although small bar of soap. It feels really good in my hands. It has a nice latger. Do not be alarmed by the color that will appear on your skin. The bamboo charcoal will make it look like you are smearing black dye on your skin. It is not dye and simply washes away.

Overall my skin feels the same as it does with other more natural soaps. Soft and not dry. Yet not greasy feeling.

I purchased this Phaii Bamboo Activated Charcoal soap in return for providing my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: It does actually work!
text:
I don’t wear nail polish all the time. Usually just for special occasions. Although, gel polish does seem to last a bit longer on me so I may start wearing it more often. This nail polish remover does work.

I like that it is Non-Toxic and Bio Certified. Acetone free is super, because I have less to worry about if it were to accidentally spill. There really isn’t much of a scent from this product. No harsh chemical smell, which my entire family was thankful!

I tried it on standard nail polish and home gel polish. It did eventually take both off, but I found that I really needed to soak and rub at the polish to get it off. This really isn’t an issue for me since it is a safer alternative. I also like that it doesn’t leave my nails and cuticles all dried out. Instead it seems to provide n3eeded moisture.

One thing that I don’t like is that it does not provide a complete list of ingredients that are contained in the product. They state “proprietary” botanical mixtures. I am apparently not allergic to anything in the mixture, but people are allergic to botanical substances!

I did receive this Pure Body Naturals 100% Natural Nail Polish Remover for free in return fro providing my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: Scent is Overpowering
text:
Let me start by saying I love french-milled soaps. I love scented soap. I love guest/sample size soaps. I adore the delightful concept and packaging design of this set. It was on my wish list and I received it as a gift. I was looking very forward to having these soaps to add some holiday cheer to my home.

Here's what happened. The person that purchased it for me was so overwhelmed by the strong scent that he had to triple bag the box and store it in a vacant room until Christmas. Each soap is individually wrapped. They're wrapped in plastic. Then in a box. Then they're double bagged in two ziploc bags. Then placed in yet another box, wrapped with wrapping paper. The box was under my tree for two days, and scent still managed to seep out and perfume all the other gifts under the tree nearby - but not in a pleasant way. When this was unwrapped Christmas morning it was so unbelievably overpowering my eyes watered. I didn't even bother to look closely at them - I could not get them back inside their ziplocs fast enough. People got headaches and complained loudly.. The entire downstairs smelled like a soap factory instead of the fresh cinnamon rolls I baked for Christmas morning. The soaps are now safely contained in their hazmat bags and stored in the laundry room instead of the guest bath. :(

I'm really kind of bummed about this because I was so excited about these soaps. I want to try them or at least take them out and smell each one on its own, but I'm afraid to now.

Greenwich Bay, if you read these reviews: please, please, PLEASE turn the scent levels down several notches in the recipe for these soaps. I think the scent must develop stronger as the soaps "ripen" because it's just much too much. Way more than any other french milled soaps I own.

Also included is a 7x4in drawstring bag. It's made from very soft, velvety material and it is light pink with the company name "Chialstar" in a darker pink.
The lip gloss goes on easily and smoothly and lasts for quite awhile; I usually only have to reapply once or twice at most. The only thing I dislike about these glosses is the slightly glue like texture while the color is drying and still tacky. title: Great e file with a dust collector and light, all in a compact package.
text:
I do my own nails at home, and this item is perfect. When I tried a different e file I learned really fast that a dust collector was essential — the dust got *everywhere*. I thought having everything in one machine would be a compromise, but all three functions work great. The light is nice and bright and I can put it exactly where I need it, for both application and filing. The fan is a little loud (too loud to hear the tv), but I don’t have anything to compare it to and I don’t mind anyway because it does such a great job with the dust.

The e file is way better than the cheap one that is the most popular on here (you know the one). I bought and tried both and kept this one, so I will compare the two. The hand piece on this one is smaller, lighter, with less vibration and it’s quieter too. The speed adjustment is incredibly smooth and accurate, and it will spin at a very low speed. The other one will spin slow but it’s tough to adjust the speed accurately, and the lighted display on that one doesn’t tell you anything. I also like that this one has an “off” position on the rotation switch in between “forward” and “reverse”, so it’s impossible to harm the motor by switching too fast between forward and reverse. The motor is plenty strong too.

If you want a less expensive e file then this is the one to get. If you get a cheap e file and a dust collector separately it would be the same price, and with this one you have higher quality and a lamp too.

title: Great eyelashes for a beginner
text:
I'd never work fake lashes before. I've always been curious but was scared off by the adhesive and the need to carefully place them, etc. Then I learned about magnetic lashes. These are great! You need to be pretty good about applying liquid eyeliner in order for this to work, since the magnetic stuff is a liquid liner. I pop that on my eyelids and then let it dry entirely. Make sure you use a fairly thick strip of it, otherwise the lash strips can start to pop off at the edges. Then you can pop on the magnetic lashes and voila, you're ready to go.

The magnetic liner hasn't given me any reactions or issues thus far, and the lashes themselves look great. I use the ones on the lowest row, which create a very dramatic effect that's just slightly larger than my natural lashes. The other two are far more dramatic. My natural lashes are thick, dark and long, so I didn't trim and they still look pretty normal.

Now that I'm more comfortable with these, I'd consider getting another set and cutting them so I can place individual lashes or pieces of lashes. But overall these are WAY easier than adhesive, and I like using them as an alternative to mascara lol (I love mascara but HATE removing it) I use a makeup removing lotion followed by micellar water, on a soft cloth, to remove. It comes off pretty easily, although sometimes a little clumpily.

The only reason I'm not giving these a higher review is because the magnetic liner has a terrible smell. They've put some kind of perfume in it that's supposed to be floral? I don't know but it smells like a chemical bouquet and the scent lingers even after the adhesive has dried. They should absolutely make this unscented if they can.

Other than that, good product and a great way to try magnetic lashes if you're curious about them.

title: Great Product; Great Value; Cool Features; Read Below!
text:
The Arko shaving soap stick is one amazing "big bang for the buck" product. I decided to try this highly rated product as part of my venture, right of passage, etc. into DE (double edge/safety razor) shaving and believe cartridge razor uses will also greatly benefit from this minimal investment.

Since it is a stick, it allows me to use it in different ways from a traditional soap or cream. It provides a luxurious lather with very good cushion. I apply it as many shavers do; wet face and soap stick, and rub the soap stick on my face (with grain as much as possible). Generally, I will use a pre-shave oil after rinsing my face with hot water, after a hot shower (if possible), before applying the soap. Then I gently squeeze out excess water from my shaving brush after soaking it and face lather. After my typical 3 passes, I take advantage of the stick feature to use it to its fullest potential. I can't recall if I saw a DE shaver on YouTube or read about this additional technique on a blog. What I am referring to is the rewetting of my face and soap stick, and reapplying without brush lathering. The thin coat of the concentrated soap to sit on the skin for a touch up pass against the grain provides excellent cushion and protection to get a BBS shave. I believe the ability to use it in this fashion combined with the ingredient, tallow, provides a super slick, protective barrier that is close to some expensive artisan shaving soaps which have tallow (Stirling). Yes, artisan soaps are better (and have many great scents) but you can't beat the price and benefits of a shaving soap in stick form for a great price.

As far as scent is concerned, I like it. It is reminiscent of the complimentary soap the motels would provide when we went on vacation when I was a kid, which I think is cool. Reviewers from several sources seem to be divided on the subject. There isn't a lot of middle ground; it's kind of a love or hate when it comes to the scent.

I think everyone should at least try it once, to experience the lather and features the soap stick form can provide. It's also pretty cool to try an international shaving product (Turkish). Using it the way I describe above doesn't take very long, so you can face lather quickly for a morning shave before work.

For cartridge shavers, this will help reduce the pulling of the hairs, which is inherent to multi-blade cartridge razors. I would also suggest looking into DE razors, if you have razor burn and ingrown hairs. If you are intimidated, try a OneBlade Core to transition to DE shaving. The single blade with pivot helps to provide a close, but mild shave. I use it now when I'm in a rush, or recovering from a DE whoops, as I am still developing my DE shaving technique. The Arko is definitely helping add insurance when my DE technique is off.

title: Helpful stuff
text:
So my 10yr old daughter is mixed and we needed to try a summer camp approved style because her INSANE but gorgeous curls are barely manageable by her mother (me), and I wasn't trying to have anyone else mess with her hair. After texting with a braider we settled on trying the crochet. She wanted unicorn/mermaid hair, and I came across these because they were only 18" while everything else was 24" and the braider worried it would be too long/too much.
Facts:
~It does have a chemically smell. It does lessen with airing them out a few days before you plan to use them, but THE BEST thing is to soak them in fabric softener. Even that doesn't fully remove the smell, but it really did help and the braider commented on how shiney and improved-looking they were versus their standard packaging.
~ The braider thought 6 bundles (2 packages) would be enough, but it looked insufficient,ZERO so I ordered 3 for her mountain of hair JIC, and she used all but 2 braids. Her hair is halfway down her back, and there's a TON of it, so if that's you, ORDER EXTRA. This is also why she was able to distinguish between the hair soaked in fabric softener vs the original because I ordered the 3rd package simply as a backup.
~ My 10yr old is 5'4" tall, so use the photo to gauge the length on you.
~The braider was super happy with this hair and quality, and requested that I send her the link 😂 So if you're skeptical like I was because of the great price, and half questionable reviews, don't be.
The hair went in this morning, so I'll update if anything changes with how I feel about the product.

text: The New Speed XL systems work ok but remember, this is very subjective as faces differ. I've tested several of the Speed Xl series and found them all adequate provided I don't press too firmly. You might need that much time to adjust but you'll know up front how any shaver will perform new as it is the sharpest. There is a lot of plastic and cheap feel but the heads and motor seem well built. I compared this shaver to my Panasonic pro curve linear and Braun activator. Both shavers did much better overall than the Norelco. The Braun is decent but the head quality is not the best. The Panasonic, on the other hand, did very well and seemed much better in quality. There's nothing really wrong with the Norelco and I can recommend it if you must have a rotary. If you don't, the Panasonic is the best going. Meanwhile the Norelco must be used with care and they're a bit pricey. Make sure to stock up on Remington's shaver saver spray. It sharpens and lubes the heads of any good shaver and lengthens life of the head. As always, follow the directions.

title: Not 100% human hair
text:
This wig isn't 100% human hair.
I tried to lighten it with powder bleach using a strong developer and saw hardly any results at all.
It lifted / lightened maybe 2 shades after processing for almost an hour.
To no avail, I covered the test strand with foil and used my blow dryer to help it lighten. Nothing happened.

Using the same formula, I would've gotten completely different results on a 100% human hair wig or on living persons head of hair.
I have 39 years experience in the hair industry, including coloring human hair wigs and hair extensions. I have never had this problem before.

I wanted the wig for a chemotherapy client who had curly hair, same length with a center part. The only problem was the color.
Unfortunately, I went by what the description is of the wig, which is 100% human hair. I ordered it, recieved it on time. Tried to lighten it as promised for my client with a disasterous result.
Now I have the upsetting task of telling my client that I can not achieve the same hair color she had because the wig isnt processing the same way human hair should.
This is after I reassured her I COULD achieve it given the facts stated and description of the wig.
My personal conclusion and professional opinion with 39 years experience is that this wig is not 100% human hair.
Theres no reason why I could not achieve a lighter color for my client other than that the wig is made up of something that resembles human hair, and not 100% human hair as the description states that it is.

It's not an overly thick wig, but has enough hair to scrunch and create a full look.
Curl formation is smooth.

3 stars for the style, curl and length of the wig. Pictures of it are somewhat accurate.
0 stars for the misrepresentation that its 100% human hair.
In addition to me, I will have a very upset client.
I'm at loss as to what to do now as she wanted and I reassured her that she could have this wig for the holiday.
It's too late now to order a different one and start this process over again.

title: Helpful tips for how to henna
text: This is Cassia Obovata which is also called "blonde henna". Same product. It 'stains' proteins with a yellow molecule. So white hair turns yellow, not blonde technically. I wish. I mix this with strawberry blonde (75% this product, 25% strawberry blonde) on my white hair in the front, weird charcoal grey in the back. It makes a perfect light strawberry blonde in the front (the product called strawberry blonde makes my white hair orange) & coats the dark in the back making have reddish highlights. It's a perfect combination & I get lots of compliments. Don't bother with the mixing it & letting it "steep" (some people even say for as long as over night). It's totally unnecessary. I've been using henna (I used to use regular red henna on my mousy brown hair) for over 40 years. I have to re-do every 3 weeks (still-even tho I'm old & grey, my hair still grows out fast). Mix with hot water & lemon juice (50/50). I recently started using a water/lemon juice/aloe vera liquid (which I drink every day-eliminates constipation even with medications that cause that) & will always do so from here out. Wish I'd tried it sooner. Great extra conditioner! I've tried different teas (chamomile-yellow tea, hibiscus-red tea) & didn't really notice a difference but it can't hurt if you're going for one of those colors with an extra boost. Worth a try. Mix until the consistency of thin-style yogurt. Henna is always an experiment the first several times till you get it down. I put the henna on (you have to get every strand of hair so take the time to make small sections to coat) then a shower cap (you can wrap your head in plastic wrap) then a big towel on top of it all. I use a close pin to hold the towel. Henna is done WHEN IT STARTS TO DRIP DOWN THE BACK OF YOUR NECK. In the summer that's about 2 1/2 hours, in the cold of winter (I don't keep the temp up very high) it may take 3-3 1/2 hours. I then wash it out easily using ONLY CONDITIONER- NO SHAMPOO. Slips right off. Be sure to use henna on clean hair that you DIDN'T condition while showering. You want your hair to have NO products on it or the henna won't stick as well. Hope this helps ladies.

title: I am SO glad I did
text:
I change my nail polish often and have been concerned about the effects of acetone polish removers. I saw an Instagram video featuring Pure Body Naturals Nail Polish Remover and decided to try it. I am SO glad I did! This polish remover is unlike acetone and even unlike the typical non-acetone nail polish remover you can buy in stores. First of all, the fragrance is light and fresh - no chemical odor at all. It is similar in consistency to cuticle oil, so it actually made my nails and the surrounding skin feel hydrated instead of dried out. It doesn't evaporate like my acetone does, so a little goes a long way.

Instead of using it as directed (applying directly to the nail with the included dropper), I applied a half dropperful onto half a cotton ball. Then I applied the cotton ball to my nail and let is set about a minute. Then I rubbed the polish away as I would with acetone. Pure Body Naturals Nail Polish Remover takes a little longer than acetone to remove the polish but it is faster than the non-acetone polish remover purchased from a store. Best of all, since it doesn't evaporate, that half cotton ball lasted for all ten nails. My nails had a minimum of a high-adhesion base coat, two coats of nail polish, a holographic top coat, and a quick dry top coat (5 coats total). Four accent nails also had nail polish nail art designs that added another coat of polish (6 coats total). This product removed everything cleanly, with no trouble, very little time, and my nails felt amazing.

The bottle is 4 ounces, doesn't evaporate as I'm using it, and requires a small amount of product, I am confident that I am getting a good deal. Since it's all natural and non-chemical, those who are concerned about what they're saturating their nails and the surrounding skin with can put those worries aside. I will absolutely be repurchasing this product.

P.S. I paid full price for mine and my recommendation is entirely voluntary and unsolicited.

title: Must have product
text:
I've used this brand of calendula gel for years, but only recently put it to the test. The first time was a minor, but ugly cut on a finger, from a serrated knife. After cleaning the wound, I kept calendula gel and a bandaid over the wound, applying the gel twice a day. At first it looked like the wound was not healing, but then I realized it was getting smaller and less red every day. It healed from the inside out, and never developed the ugly deep scab I normally get with cuts to my fingers. It was amazing. Then, just a few weeks later, I got bit by a dog on the back of my hand and fingers. I put calendula gel on my fingers twice a day, covered by a bandaid, and the bites healed just like my knife cut had – amazing! Since the bites on the back of my hand weren't as serious, I pretty much ignored them after a couple days. In contrast, as those bites healed they looked unpleasant and develop ugly scabs. This all happened a few months ago, and I can still see where the wounds were, but I'm so impressed that I will always use calendula gel on all my wounds.

Not long after my injuries, I showed my Dr. how well the wounds healed, and mentioned that about 8 years ago my sister used calendula gel while she had radiation treatment for cancer. It really worked well, limiting the damage done to her skin. She applied it three times a day, but always had clean skin when she went in for her treatments. My Dr. was surprised that she had known to use it, and said that the hospital he works with had recently started giving calendula gel to patients who are going through radiation treatments.

Every first aid kit should have calendula gel!

I was worried because my hair is so fine that straightening it with this brush would take away any body that I had, but I was pleasantly surprised. While my hair wasn't quite as full as it was with the John Frieda brush, it had some good body and was smoother with this EnPoint Anion Hair Care brush.
The instructions are good and I'd suggest reading through them before trying the brush, especially with regards to the temperature settings to use for your particular type hair. Since my hair is so fine, I use a lower temperature. I set it to about 165 and it worked great for what I wanted. I'm really anxious to try this when I've been out in the humidity and my hair is a massive frizz ball. I will update this review when I have that opportunity. As a daily tool I think it could dry out my hair, even using the conditioner they recommend. However, I was very pleasantly surprised that my hair still looked good after sleeping on it (that is a huge rarity for me), so it doesn't need to be used daily, just between washes. Regardless, it's a great tool to have for quick fix-ups or when I want a more glamorous, smooth look.

text:
First off I must say this is my first electric razor that I have owned. I have been wet shaving for over 8 years now and tried an electric razor once before and hated it. I first started looking at an electric razor as wet shaving seemed a drag, a waste of time and just a pain. I have to be clean shaven for my job so I have to shave. First I had to decide on a foil razor or rotary razor. As I had such a horrible experience with the foil razor the time before when I used it I decided I defiantly did not want that type so I opted to try the Rotary razor and have been very well pleased. Some things that drew me to purchase this razor were
1. You can use it in the shower.
This to me seemed very convenient as I could shave as I'm getting showering which in my eyes saved some time from having to do the traditional way.
2. Applies Moisturizer while shaving
This was another seller point for me as my face dries out very easily and I hated after wet shaving take more time to apply aftershave so to have a system that applies it while I'm shaving seemed like a bonus.

The size of this unit is great it fits in my hand just right and is easy to grab. The only complaint I have of the body itself is the charging prongs on the bottom back side of the razor stick out and can poke your hand while using the razor. Another downfall with this razor is that it does not have a tray to collect the hair as it cuts it so at least in my experience I have to wash my face afterwards as to get the little hairs off of my face that it has just cut.
One thing about this razor and I noticed other people complain about is that it does not do well as a dry razor. In the instruction manual it actually says to wet your face before using it ultimately meaning it is not a dry shaver, but it does not take long to splash water on your face.
So if your looking for a good razor that will apply moisturizer as you shave, that you can use in the shower and ultimately if you want a razor that does an excellent job (in my experience just as good as a wet shave) this is the razor for you!!

I have long, thin hair and ALWAYS have had a very hard time finding a good brush that wasn't too heavy, too rough on my scalp, or too hard on my hair. title: It's an alright little balm stain...
text: I got this balm stain with a few other options to try for my wedding this fall. I wanted something with a rich color, that lasted more than a couple hours, and wouldn't come off on my new husband's face!! While this is a great little balm, it's not the one I think I'm going to go with. The color of this one came out quite a bit brighter pink than I'd expect from the color of the product in the tube, but it's not bad. The opacity of the color does leave a bit to be desired, it's not quite as opaque as I was hoping, it's a little on the translucent side, but I expected that of a balm. However, the color does last quite a while even after several hours of answering the phones at work and talking around the office. It feels a little drying, but as a chapstick addict myself, almost any lipstick/stain feels drying because I'm not reapplying every hour or so! Although, when I rub my lips together even a couple hours after applying, I can still feel there's a moist layer of product on my lips...so I'm sure it won't feel drying to all. As far as transfer is concerned, I haven't noticed any color coming off on the back of my hand when I "test kiss" - possibly a little right after applying, but several hours in and there's no transfer (even with that moist feeling I was mentioning earlier!). Like I said, it's a good little balm stain, and is probably great for day-to-day wear, but not my choice for my wedding!

title: I want it in a larger size. Good product, otherwise.
text:
I think this is a superior secure headband for people who wear wigs and don’t want them to slip. However, I have a larger than average head ( some, but not all, “average” wigs are too tight for me) — and I really could use a larger size since my hair grew back after chemotherapy. Unfortunately, It only comes in one size.

The silicone band is mostly comfortable. It feels too snug when I put it on, but then I get used to it. I can wear it for hours. Just wish it were a tiny bit bigger. When it has rolled off my head with scarf hats, it has been a bit embarrassing.

One size really does not fit all.

I was hoping that I could rely on this silicone band to always keep scarfs on my head on “bad hair days” — so when it rolls off my head, it is embarrassing. I have used this for silky scarf-hats with mixed results. When it works, the silicone nubs hold a hat or scarf on my head VERY securely, but now that I have hair, I would rather just use a bobby-pin on the scarf material. I like things simple.

It has worked very well for me when I was wearing wigs when bald. Very secure! Security and comfort when I was having chemotherapy and shaved my head.

However, I really think it is best for people with average and smaller heads. Larger heads may be able to use it depending on shape, hair thickness, or maybe with a bobby-pin on the silicon band for extra security.

Not expensive, so worth a try if you want to keep your wig secure!

title: This would make a GREAT gift!
text:
In an effort to stretch the amount of time in between haircuts for my husband, I've begun giving him little beard trims here and there to straighten it out or shape it up. I'll also trim some of the curls around/above his ears and at the neckline so that it's less messy for work. I don't do anything drastic by any means, but I have a steady hand for that sort of cut.

Before, I was using whatever scissors I had around (I know, that's blasphemy in some circles). The most recent were KitchenAid kitchen shears (that I don't use for food items because I like my other kitchen scissors better), believe it or not. They are pretty sharp, so it's not quite as bad as it may sound.

At any rate, I knew that made for a sad hair trim, so I decided to upgrade. This kit happened to also have a beard comb, so that was just a bonus.

Oh man... I've been impressed across the board here. When I opened the Amazon box, there was a very nice display box by the manufacturer, with a magnetic lid and an opening made perfectly for the items. It makes for a great first impression, so this would be awesome as a gift.

You can tell just by looking that the scissors are nice, but when you pick them up, it's like the metal is buttery and soft to the touch. It feels classy, if that makes any sense. And while I've barely used them so far (I trimmed him up super recently), let me tell you... it's like night and day. It's such a smooth cut. This is how it's meant to feel when you cut hair - I just know it. I've never looked forward to giving a hair trim so much!

He already had a wooden beard comb, so I personally wasn't all that enthused about it like I was the scissors, but I have since been informed by him that the teeth are smaller on this one than on the other, which makes for a different beard combing experience. Now he has options, which he appreciates.

Oh, and the case is nice as well. :) Seriously, you'll feel good about giving this as a gift. From the moment they unwrap the box, they'll be pleased with what they see.

Please note, I received this item at a discount in exchange for my honest, unbiased opinion. I wouldn't steer anyone wrong, so if you have found this review to be helpful, please click the Yes box below. Thanks!

title: Wow!
text:
My sister just got one of these Emjoi Micro-Pedis from Amazon, and told me about it. Love it!

I have included a photo of my actual feet's results. Note that my "before" is NOT me neglecting my feet. On the contrary, it was taken just days after I spent half an hour on my tiring old razor, Ped-Egg, rasp, pumice stone routine. (And sometimes I would rasp off too much, then it would hurt to walk a few days. Ouch!)

This product seems designed to prevent removing too much skin. If you push too hard the machine will basically stop. So, I find it best to let the machine do the work for me, just let it spin and spin, and I only apply gentle pressure…just enough pressure that the spinning slows slightly. It's so easy to use that I can do it almost without looking while watching TV.

I like the extension handle, particularly because it catches the powdered skin that comes out the holes on the device's underside. I just empty it into a small garbage can periodically as I go. The handle also makes it nice to reach around the far side of my foot since I am definitely not a contortionist. Make sure you firmly snap the device under the ridge that holds it into the extension handle: then it holds it nice and snug.

Overall, a nice little device. Reasonable price, too.

title: I like this but...
text:
My only complaint with Zest isn't unique to that product: it has to do with the downsizing of consumer products so companies don't have to raise their prices; they just give us less.

Zest comes in a 4 oz bar, common in most "bath sized" bars but smaller than I remember bars of soap when I was a younger man. The smaller the bar, the easier it is to drop it when it's wet.

If you get beyond that, Zest has two strong positives: the scent is pleasant without being overpowering. It is appropriate for men but I don't think women would object to using it as well. Also, it appears to be less caustic when you wash your face around your eyes. I made the mistake of getting Coast Soap in my eyes once and almost had to see a doctor; this is much milder.

The bottom line: I will continue to buy Zest and will keep whining about small bath bars. This is a decent soap brand.

Update: I originally wrote this about the 4 oz bars and the review somehow got applied to the larger 5 oz bars as well. Please allow me to make this clear: the 5 oz bars answers all the negatives I had about the smaller bars. This is finally what I've been looking for and I couldn't be happier with the larger size. title: So far, nothing to write home about.
text:
I am a self imposed victim of over plucking my brows, and of my lashes seeming to become shorter and more sparse as I'm aging.

I've been wanting to try some of the many lash growth serums for a long time. The first thing I tried was Castor Oil. It seemed to help my lashes grow, and look a bit thicker. I then got this LashRevive serum, and another serum at the same time. I used LashRevive on my right lashes and brow, and the other brand on the left lashes and brow. I will only be discussing results for the right eye, with the LashRevive serum in this review.

I noticed a lot of wonderful reviews for this product, lots of pictures of the bottle, but no before and after pictures.
I received my product on the 11th of June, and today is June 25th, so I have been using this product consistently for 2 weeks.

First for the lashes. I am including a picture of before and after so you can judge for yourselves. The left side is before, right side is after. I really see little difference. When I look in the mirror, I feel as though they are more noticeable, maybe a tiny bit thicker, or darker, but not by much. But as you can see, the picture reflects none of that. Maybe it's just wishful thinking. I can say that on my lower lashes, mostly toward the inner corner, I have seen growth. They are much longer. It's weird that they are only on the inside though. I do not have before/after pictures of that, as I was not expecting this to effect the lower lashes.

On to the brows. I can see a difference in my brow. It appears fuller to me. I'm a natural blonde, so the newest hairs that are growing in are very light, almost white blonde, and difficult to see in the included picture, but I do believe you can see a tiny bit of a difference. Nothing dramatic. It's enough for me to continue to use it for my brows. Again, before picture on the left, after on the right. Judge for yourselves.

Application was super easy. It's a thick, milky consistency, and has a nice large applicator brush to easily cover the lashes and brow area quickly. I experienced no irritation to the skin, or to the eye. Never felt any sort of sting or burn at all. I did have gunk in the corners of my eye in the morning, and weird white stringy stuff in my lashes. Easy enough to remove when I washed my face in the morning. I did notice what seemed like more lashes than normal actually fall out, in the beginning. Maybe it was only because I was paying more attention to my lashes though. It was about 2-3 per day. Obviously not enough to be noticeable as you can see in the before/after pic.

I'm confused with this product. I did not see enough results to give this 4 or 5 stars. But saw enough of a result on the brow to think (hope) that I may get better results with continued use, so I did not give it just 1 star. I am going to continue to use this product until I run out, and I will update this review with any positive/negative results.

I received this product for free in exchange for my review. I hope this was helpful for you.

title: 4.5 Stars - Above Average Performance
text:
After hearing many times of "the fat" I decided to buy my own puck of Mitchell's and see what the fuss was about. It turned out to be a really great soap though not my favorite.

Lather:
Doesn't bloom into a full lather avalanche like TOBS does for me but isn't too thin either. Certainly adequate.

Face Protection:
On the slick side, good blade glide. Just for face protection alone this is a great product.

Cost:
A little on the high side. Razorock has similar soaps available for a third less. I'm not sure that they preform to exactly the same level but since I own some I will be putting this to the test. Not super extravagant though.

Scent:
This is where Mitchell's really loses me. I like strong scents with my shave. TOBS Mr. Taylor is great for a classic yet clean scent that sticks with you. Mitchell's smells like a bar of Ivory Soap. Clean for sure, but nothing to get excited about.

Overall:
I wish I could give Mitchell's 4.5 stars. It will give you a great shave. The price isn't that bad and the lack of strong scent may actually be preferable to some people. If you haven't tried it I suggest giving it a go.

I'm not the type of guy who gets manicures, so I just want to do clean, even clips and be done, and not spend time filing if I already did a good, even cut...but I know women are particular about nails, so it bothers me that they may notice these white spots if I don't take the time to get rid of all of them.

title: Gentle and not super strong, need several applications but easy to use!
text: I have dark, thick Asian hair. Love this product, it’s quite gentle and so easy to apply. Does burn your skin so be sure to wipe off the foam from your neck and face, don’t let it sit. That being said, as a gentle foam bleach it won’t make Asian hair blonde after one application. You need several. And it does make your hair the same as the box. Same color and tone, so sort of peachy and orangey. You can make it lighter than the box with more applications though. In the end it’s not quite cheap, but cheaper than going to the salon, and if you’re doing it yourself, foam is WAY easier. The foil and paint on method is sooo hard to do on yourself. Ive attempted it before and it took forever,and I had to use so many mirrors. Results are stronger (lighter) on first round of bleaching but margin of error is bigger. The foam is so easy to end up with an even application. I add in 2.3 ml of olaplex no 1 to each bottle I use, rinse after 30 mins, and do a hair mask with olaplex no 2 for 15 mins. After that I again rinse out. I do that for each application of this bleach, and my hair has turned out really healthy looking and not fried! Also Olaplex 03 (bond maker) hair mask 2x a week. I’ve used olaplex with the usual powder + developer bleaches and my hair didn’t turn out as soft and healthy looking as with this foam bleach!

Overall, this mask does exactly what it says. I love this product and would highly recommend it.

*** Update 1/11/2017 - I've been using this about two times a month, sometimes twice per week. It has kept my complexion clear, my skin so very smooth and radiant. I've tried using it with the Apple Cider Vinegar using the encapsulated kind (just one capsule), with hot water and a small amount of the mask (you'll have to mix the apple cider capsule together with the water, discard a good amount of the water and then mix the mask in. The very small amount will work to cover your face. I also started using a rubberized basting brush and the mask goes on much smoother without any clumps. I found in using these steps the mask performed much better and the clumpiness was very minimal.

This is going to be the one beauty product that I will repurchase to have on hand. It has very simple ingredients and performs quite well!!

title: Less than Great....
text:
I really wanted to like this product, but unfortunately, it was less than great quality, and one of the brushes I received was broken. Quite a few of the brushes had frayed bristles and had uneven thickness to them, which made even application hard to come by.

When I used some, it didn't seem like they blended the colors together well (mainly for eye shadow). I wish there were smaller round brushes for blending out shadows on your eyes because I feel like all the flat brushes are just about all the same. There is barely any size difference between three of them, and they can all be used for the same things so why not replace those with some rounder ones?

I tried to contact the seller about the problems I had with this product, but, after two days, I haven't heard anything back from them. I was waiting before putting this review up to see if there was anything they cared to do to help with these problems (new brush that's not broken, or a new set all together that has better quality to them), but I have gotten no response back from them to lead me to believe that they're willing to do anything to help.

I have attached photos to this post to show the problems I got with these brushes. The broken one was a foundation brush so I didn't get to try that one out to even see if it applied the foundation well, so I was a little disappointed with that. The larger powder brush seemed to do ok, but it didn't pick up powder that well. The larger fan brush I tried to use for contouring (I saw someone use a large fan brush for this purpose in a tutorial so I wanted to try it out), but even though the brush picked up the color, it didn't seem to apply it very much at all. The contour powder I used is super pigmented so I shouldn't have had that problem. The eye shadow brush I used (one of the smaller tapered brushes) actually worked pretty well so I don't have complaints about any of those except that some of the smaller brushes had frayed bristles, too. The smaller fan brush I used for highlight, and, though it did well with applying it, the unevenness of the bristles made it apply in a weird and uneven way, One of the larger tapered brushes I used to pack on a setting powder, but again, it didn't seem to pick it up well and left a ton of fall out once it hit my skin. I understand setting powder typically leaves fall out, but I've never experience so much before using this brush.

Basically, the best brushes in this set were probably the eye shadow brushes.

I hope this review helps give some insight on this product. I also hope the seller finds a way to fix the problems I had for future customers.

title: Excellent Wet/Dry Electric Shaver
text:
For more than a few years I had been using the [[ASIN:B00008DQJQ Factory Reconditioned Braun 7526 Syncro Smart Logic Shaver]] I purchased on Amazon. Prior to the Syncro, I had used a [[ASIN:B000GCQF4M Gillette Sensor Excel Razor For Men - 1 ea]]. Clearly, the Syncro could not give me the close shave of the Sensor Excel. Still, I liked the convenience and the ease of the Syncro and the fact that it held up to rough use.

I had the opportunity to try the Philips Norelco 8040X and have been blown away. My first usage was dry and without the application of the moisturizer. At first, I was slightly disappointed at the whisker tugs and slight razor burn and the ergonomics but decided to give it another chance since my first usage did not use the moistureizer and the unit had not been completely charged.

My second usage was dry and with the use of the moistureizer and the unit was fully charged. The whisker tugs and slight razor burn were gone. After my first use, I was used to the ergonomics (it is a completely different design from the Syncro), facial coverage was exceptional. I also found that one push of the moistureizer button was sufficient for one half of my face. After the use, my face was smooth and soft and, unlike my efforts with the Syncro, very few missed hairs.

My third usage was wet (int he shower) and with the use of the moistureizer. Again, the results were fantastic. With the excellent coverage of the razor head, my shaving time has decreased significantly.

My only two complaints (if they can be called complaints since they are so minor) are (1) the scent of the moistureizer and (2) the charger. Another reviewers have aptly stated the deficiencies with ths scent so I will say no more. As for the charger, you have to place the razor in with some care so that it makes contact with the recharging points. Also, the light signifiying that the unit is re-charging is muted (which is both good and bad) so be alert. Other than those two trivialities, I am extremely happy with the Philips Norelco 8040X shaver.

title: Cute, Functional and High Quality!
text:
The Choo Choo Stripes Adult Shortall is an amazing, cute, functional product from Baby Pants! I bought these as a birthday present to myself a year ago and they have held up very well through play and washings. After looking at the sizing chart on the website I had originally ordered a medium, but had to exchange them for a large because even at the lowest shoulder strap length they were too tight around the waist and too short on my legs. I had to cover the 25% restocking fee and return shipping, but Baby Pants was very professional, and quick in processing my exchange. That being said, I would consider choosing the larger size if you're on the fence about what size to order.

I agree with LollyLaLaz's comments in her review about the Baby Pants patch logo on the back and recently decided to remove it myself so that I would feel comfortable when discretely wearing these in public. This is a common feature in the few Baby Pants products that I've bought, but it is very easy to remove without damaging the fabric.

There are six snaps in the crotch and three on each side by the pockets, each labeled with the Baby Pants logo. These logos on the snaps are a nice touch and are not noticeable unless seen up close. Also, the five pockets are deep and functional as well.

Overall, I would definitely recommend these to anyone considering buying these super cute, childish, practical shortalls! Enjoy!!

text:
…which is hardly more than a sleep or two at most, but that's okay because there are approximately a gazillion of these cute, kid-friendly tattoos, or so it seems: four themed packets (sea life, circus, zoo/wildlife, and insects) each contain ten tattoo sheets, and each sheet contains a dozen or so tattoos for 430 total.

Sheets are not perforated so individual tattoos must be cut out—carefully, by an adult or older child.

No instructions are included but they work like any temporary tattoos: after cutting each one out, peel off the plastic and apply face down (i.e., with blank paper backing on top), saturate with water, and, while holding it still, apply some pressure to facilitate the transfer—a thumbnail will work, as will any smooth, rounded hard tool such as a worry stone or a gua sha body scraper.

These are not super-durable; I was able to remove one pretty easily an hour after application by rubbing my bare fingertip back and forth over it a bit of force. Careful children may make them last a couple of days by guarding them from unnecessary contact; more rambunctious ones will likely discover they disappear much sooner.

Bottom line: Great at a party or to give out individual sheets as party favors; we'll be using them at "cousins' camp" for a dozen boys and girls ages around 4 to 10, so the variety of styles and subjects is a major plus for wide-ranging appeal.

title: Good. However, probably not for oily skin
text:
This foundation has potential IF you use a good primer with it. I have combination skin and, like many foundations, this can settle into pores and creases. Some foundations are better than others in terms of this tendency, and I'd say this one is about "par for the course" with regard to settling in pores and creases. Primer will help.

This does seem to have a lot of moisture in it (as I've found with many foundations that have "satin" in the title). For me, I feel a bit dewy and not quite clean enough in this -- especially when I look in my 10X magnification mirror.

However, I'd venture to guess that people with dry skin might actually appreciate this. Whereas people with oil prone skin and/or visible pores -- will NOT appreciate this so much.

I ordered the Fair color and I'm an NC20 or NC25. The color is great (not orange and not pink). Nice neutral color. It was just slightly lighter than my natural skin color and looked great with a light dusting of bronzer / blush. I always prefer to err lighter than my natural color than to go to darker, and end up looking like and orange pumpkin.

NOTE >>>Be sure to shake this well before each use<<< I noticed if I don't shake this, the first spray is mostly moisture and has a shiny greasy effect. Product applies much better if it is well shaken first. This should be in bold print on the front of the can.

I spray this into a little eyelash tray (or back of hand, or where ever) and dab my make-up brush into it. Then, apply to face.

Its a good foundation. However, getting up into this price point, I felt some of the above minor gripes warranted removing a star.

title: Hands down best quality for the price point. No brassiness. 1B to 8ash & 22 medium blonde
text:
I buy clip-in hair to add color depth and a little bit of drama, so this is not a review to add length. This hair is perfect to blend in with fine hair or hair that is smooth (looks like you can use right out of the package). The hair has healthy "bounce" or body.

This is a review of 1B/8A/22 (dark black going to 8ash with 22 medium blonde mix)

This hair provides hard to achieve drama, going from deep dark brown/black to a lighter shade, without ANY brassiness. This is nearly impossible to achieve on real hair (without ruining the cuticle), yet they did it and the hair appears HEALTHY.

The hair also appears relatively thick on the ends, unlike another recent purchase I made.

NOTE: Sadly, I might be returning this, so I did not disassemble the hair pieces from the package or even try these on (because another reader might receive my return). Right now, I'm undecided.

Defining color over the internet is difficult The ends are supposed to be #22 with 8A. In the picture, it looks like a light blonde of 8.5 or even maybe a 9. I decided to roll the dice in hopes that the picture would be more accurate than the description. Upon receipt, this is a medium blonde that even leans a bit dark blonde...perhaps a level 7.5 at the lightest last few inches.

My natural hair color is a medium brown and I bleach it to a level 9.5. Uniformly bleached hair, especially right after a root touch-up can make the face look washed out. So this would have been perfect to add some interest and depth except I fear that the medium blonde-dark blonde will detract from the nearly platinum hair that I've worked hard to achieve.

This color is versatile and would be great for someone with medium blonde hair or any shade *darker*. Unfortunately, for someone with level 9 or above, probably best to shop for a level 9 or 10 ombre.

Bummer, I really think this is gorgeous hair but it will not work for me.

text:
I would have posted a picture but it looked too graphic to post online.

I went back and forth for weeks debating whether or not to purchase this product. I had gotten my teeth professionally whitened at the dentist a few years ago and it worked beautifully; however, could not justify spending several hundred dollars on doing it again. In lieu of spending a ton of money on professional whitening, I researched at-home whitening kits. Glo seemed to rank high with at-home whitening kits and Amazon offered a coupon for it so I had finally decided to go for it.

I received the item pretty quickly and charged it right away. The first 2 days were fine, albeit tedious. On the 3rd day, I started to get a sensation on the underside of my top lip even though I applied the lip balm generously. By the 4th day, the burning sensation was intolerable but I pushed through it until I finished the session. By the end of that 4th day, the pain was enough for me to decide not to continue using the product. I flipped my top lip up and there is a long, white burn all the way across the length of my lip. It lines up exactly the way the gel would leak up out of the mouthpiece. All this for not even a slight change in the shade of my teeth.

I am returning this product and applying the money towards real professional teeth whitening at the dentist. I gave 2 stars for quick shipping, nice storage case, and the option to be able to return product.

title: Recommended by a speech-language pathologist to help feeding skills
text:
I don't know about this product being a "toy", but it was recommended by a speech-language pathologist (SLP) to help with some mechanical feeding problems. Our little one has had a hard time with textures in food, among other things.

It's a great teether, and has actually helped with feeding, too. I use one of those sippy-cup straps to attach it to the high chair, and he'll chew on it between bites. I could see using it as a toothbrush, which is probably its intended purpose, but for now, it's helping immensely with development issues. There seems to be something to chewing on it that causes the tongue and jaw to engage in ways that chewing on a baby spoon doesn't do. Plus, he seems to enjoy chewing on it and turning it over in his hands.

Sanitation/safety issues: I inspect it regularly to see if any of the "nubs" have been damaged or are breaking, but the entire item has remained intact for the few months we've been using it. Another plus is that the entire item is a one-piece mold, so it's very easily sterilized (there are no holes or hollow places for water or bacteria to hide). I haven't placed it in the dishwasher, but I could see it going in with those rubber baby spoons and faring well. I usually just handwash it w/a good soap and sometimes a very diluted bleach solution w/a LOT of rinsing, like other hard plastic toys. The rubber head has some give but is not so soft that it bends, and the handle is very firm. He has NOT placed it so far back in his mouth that he could gag on it, but like anything else w/young children, it's a possibility and not an item that I would allow him to use w/o direct supervision or where I couldn't easily grab it (i.e. in a car seat).

text:
I wore acrylic nails for over 30 years until I developed the allergy of all allergies. I didn't want to give up my beautiful nails but after trying gel nail products (applied like acrylics), gel polishes and other things I wasn't getting what I wanted. My nails were in such horrible shape then I found another powder system at a local salon and fell in love! After paying $40 and $50 a crack for someone else to do my nails I thought, "I can do this, it doesn't look that hard." But I didn't want to pay for the pricey other systems out there. Then I saw an ad for Revel on Facebook and while there IS a bit of a learning curve to this product, my nails looked great the first try.
Some hints:
Powder colors aren't quite the same in the jar as on the nails. Colors also look a bit different on a computer screen as opposed to real life.
Before beginning read the directions thoroughly more than once. Be sure you fully understand what you need to do because once you get started you need to keep going to get the best results from the product.
Don't get too close to your cuticles. It does make a difference.
Have several good files of different grits and a good buffing block

Now I can't wait to try more colors!

I personally prefer the cream to the oils (I don't care for the feel of oil on my skin) but all of the products work well. The cream is not oily, and absorbs nicely into the skin. They are light and not overwhelming. However you can also get it fragrance free. I honestly can't think of one negative thing about this product (and believe it or not I am picky). title: Fine for sanding light calluses. Poor for removing heavy calluses
text:
If you have calluses that are a few millimeters in thickness that just need to be made smooth, the Emjoi may be the perfect solution for you. However, if you have serious calluses that actually need removal, rather than just minor shaping, you will find the Emjoi to be very, very slow, about 10 times slower than the product I eventually replaced it with, the Microplane foot rasp.

The Emjoi works by literally sanding the skin, something that requires the skin be dry at the time, and therein lies the problem. The Microplanes, which work by slicing away a tiny layer at a time, work on skin damp from bath or shower, and that skin is much easier to remove than hard, dry skin. Removing my thickest callus on my male feet took close to 20 minutes with the Emjoi. The Microplane eliminates it in fewer than two minutes. The Microplanes are also a lot cheaper: The one I use, the Microplane Colossal Pedicure Rasp, is currently listed for $9.50 on amazon. The more feminine versions start at $8.95.

No, I have no connection with the Microplane company. I just found it shocking when, after spending a whole bunch of money on the Emjoi, I discovered an alternate technology that was so much better. I just wish I'd found out sooner. Do make sure you have dampened your feet before using the Microplane. Otherwise, much of the advantage disappears. (Don't dampen your feet before using the Emjoi: it has no way to clear any dampened removed skin, so it just fills the nooks and crannies in the sandpaper until the cylinder is perfectly slick.) If you search amazon for "microplane" and "foot," you'll find the full line.

title: Firm Tree Sap LikevHold But Very Sticky Messy
text: I have used this before in the past. I used to buy it at my local beauty supply store the owner recommended it to me once and that’s how i was introduced to it but it was in a bottle with a brush. I have used this tube before and it’s really really messy and sticky with the brush too. However, it does give a good hold and will rip your hair out of your head when it comes time to take it out without proper removal treatment. It dries up hard like beeswax or tree sap. It’s about the same color too so that’s what it reminds me of. It does have a chemical smell but goes away with time. It can and will slightly burn the scalp/skin if it is already irritated and maybe even when it’s not irritated but the burning feeling is quick and goes away once applied for 3 minutes or longer. It’s not a unbearable burning sensation but can be annoying. I have considered that as a slight side effect and the firm longer hold on my tracks outweighs the burning side effects. It is my favorite extension hair glue but you will suffer some hair loss when taking your hair out, the benefits, again outweigh the risks and side effects in my opinion which is why I continue to use it. However, i do not use it every time i wear tracks. I only use it when i need the extra hold or want my extensions to hold up for longer. I don’t remember how well it stands up to moisture and water but it does well with perspiration which is totally different compared to dumping a bucket of water on your head, dip in the pool or washing your hair in the shower or something like that. I’m considering using it again now because I really don’t feel like going through the process of finding someone to sew in my extensions and I don’t feel like sitting in a chair for hours getting it sewn in. The only time i sew in or consider using this stuff is only when i get a wavy or curly weave that i will need to keep wet and use a bunch of wet styling products in it. If my memory is correct, i think it might have done well with water and wet hair. I’m just not 100% certain. It was a long time since I last used this stuff. You might want to get 2 tubes because of the amount of stickiness and how messy it is, you will get a lot of it wasted while using it.

title: Quick and easy to use, great color, does not stain skin
text:
UPDATED. I've now purchased this twice and to my surprise - it's even better now. The small capsules that contain the dye powder was very hard to separate without crushing. With this recent purchase (6/2021), the capsules are now more substantial and way less fragile so it's easy to separate the two halves w/o making a huge mess or crushing them. I have thin aging eyebrows and this product is so easy to use, does not stain the surrounding skin and works well. I used dark brown and left it on for at least two minutes. I wipe it off with a wet cotton pad and it comes off easily with darker brows.

ORIGINAL REVIEW. Better than expected. My brows are thin because of electrolysis in the 1990's (it was the style then). I got the dark brown and it turned out darker than I thought, but I quickly got used to it. It does cover the gray brows too which are gnarly and like to stick straight out.

I was surprised how quickly it worked. I left it on for 2 minutes and then removed it with a damp cotton pad. My brows were quite a bit darker. I was NOT careful where I put the mixture, I just brushed it on and got quite a bit on the skin. It didn't matter, no burning at all and easy to wipe off w/o staining. I first did it three weeks ago and my brows still look good.

My brows are quite narrow and thin so adding more color makes them appear thicker.

title: Probably performs as advertised
text:
I tried it out on my legs as shown in the marketing image and video. The surface of the product is like a fine silicone sandpaper, and it creates some not-uncomfortable friction against the skin as you vigorously rub in the area you want to eliminate hair from. I saw only minimal results with light rubbing so I rubbed up and down as shown in the video with more pressure until it became uncomfortable. I don't have a high pain tolerance, so it is entirely possible someone else with a higher one would be able to rub harder. My skin turned red temporarily, and I did end up having to shave per usual to achieve total hair removal. I spoke with my pharmacist and she checked and confirmed again that my insurance would not cover but she checked several discount cards they used and I was able to find them for about $30 less than here. PROS to buying here: No RX required, Convenience. CONS to buying here: Price, Not always in stock. text:

When it worked, I was not thrilled with it. It has three buttons in a row at the top, the top one being the one to release the little nozzle wand for want of a better term, the second one the on/off button and the third being the mode button. When you go to use it, and you decide to stop while it still has water in it, you need to turn it off while keeping the nozzle wand in your mouth so you don't shoot water everywhere but you cannot see the buttons so you just start pushing and maybe you will get lucky and hit the power button, but just as often, you will hit the mode button and it just starts working at a different pressure as you grope around. My solution was to not stop when I wanted to but keep going until it ran out, then pull it away from my face far enough to find the buttons and turn it off.

It is not practical to try to rotate the nozzle wand so is easier to use by just rotating the whole unit which means you lose track of where the buttons even are.

title: Not quite there yet
text: I initially ordered this razor just for the handle. When I got it I was surprised in some ways, and not so much in others. First, the handle was balanced, looked well-made, and attractive. However, it came unscrewed almost immediately as it was not tightened well at the factory. Easy fix with some thread locking compound. I was very surprised by the apparent quality of the materials. Fit and finish was very good and the chrome looked extremely nice. The head looked nice although the top cap showed flaws in the final polish by way of minor machining marked still visible in the reflection of the chrome. Really, that is the ONLY visible defect. However, upon using it to shave things became less surprising. The blade noise and feel is extreme. I could not get a close shave no matter how hard I tried, despite this being a fairly aggressive shaver. Upon closer inspection I notice the top cap is quite narrow and a very large portion of the cutting edge of the blade protrudes and is unsupported. This leads to blade deflection and as some refer to it- blade chatter. This is an issue really only if you have stiff beard growth as I do. Basically, when the blade is not well supported it can flex slightly changing blade Geometry as you shave. Not sure if that was happening here but even with fresh blades I got an uncomfortable amount of tugging using this razor. The blade felt dull even when new. As for the handle, it’s nice but huge! I have big hands and it was too big for me. This razor might be better suited for leg/body shaving given its characteristics, although it’s quite aggressive for such a purpose. For $10 it’s amazing. But for $25 you can get something far better. Your choice.

title: Fantastic out of the box

The only curious and apparent defect has to do with the foam padding on the base. The base is actually hollow and they filled in the cavity with thick closed cell foam which is typical of padding for whatever surface you place it on. However, the foam is about 1/8" too thin so it actually is not what touches the your counter, the metal edges are. This is an easy fix but it's just odd that this is so well executed and the only apparent defect is something so easily avoided by the manufacturer. Assuming it holds up, it's still well worth the price however.

Update: after comparing the finishing of this stand to a Muhle razor I received, the quality difference is slightly apparent in the chrome. The Muhle has a mirror finish. The reflections in it are crisp. This stand does show some surface imperfections in the reflections revealing that the original metal surface was not perfectly polished prior to the addition of the chrome finish. However, we are talking a very slight difference. I really didn’t notice it until I had the Muhle razor to compare. I don’t think this is as much a knock on the stand as it is a testament to the insane quality of the Muhle. As such, I’m maintaining my original rating. For a stand, this is more than good enough.

title: Also great for dry, brittle, baby-fine, slippery hair!!!
text:
While most of the reviews for these clips are to promote them for thicker hair, I am here to tell all of you who have hair like mine - dry, brittle, slightly kinky, fly-away, baby-fine, slippery - that these work great for our hair, too.

You know what kind of problems we have with clips and bands and what-not either falling out of our hair while trying to use them, or worse, pulling our hair out when we remove them. I think this happens for two reasons:

One, our hairs are so fine that they actually get caught in the small tiny working parts of these kinds of clips - cracks that a thicker hair shaft is simply too large to get caught in. My sister's hair is the opposite of mine - dense, poker straight, and an extremely thick shaft - and she was surprised when I told her about this happening to me. It's hard to believe, but it happens to us all the time!! In fact, I have to wind electrical tape onto new brushes where the handle meets the head because individual hairs get caught in the crack there all the time if I don't seal it up. Let me tell you, OUCH. It took me years to figure that one out.

The other problem is that once treated with product and dried, and especially flat-ironed, baby-fine hair feels wonderful to the touch but it is very *slippery*. If you use a roller or a clip that does not hold well or is too heavy, it simply falls out. Useless!

So... these are stronger & lighter, and the moving parts are better made, than any other ones I have tried of their kind. And they work really well for my fickle, difficult hair.

I am not saying that these won't ever pull your hair out if you are careless and move too fast. I am also not saying that they won't fall out if you don't secure them properly. They will. But if you have baby-fine hair then you have already learned to slow down and concentrate to avoid those problems anyway. :)
